One tap starts a voice turn by the same path as the chat panel's Talk. The Assistant row stays for typing; it had fallen below the fold once WhatsApp was added.

adr.title: Dumb phone mode is a manual switch that shrinks HOME, holds notifications and silences strangers

chunks.heading: 62. Dumb phone mode is a manual switch that shrinks HOME, holds notifications and silences strangers > Amendment, 2026-10-24: Matrix mode blocks feeds, not everything
chunks.text:
Kevin: *"i just need to stop the social media apps... everything thats not a distraction or causes me
to doomscroll should stay."* This replaces the Standing section's **"Allowlist, not blocklist"**
paragraph, including "the browser" being hidden.

- **Blocked:** an app Android tags Social, Video or News, or one on a seed list of known feed apps
  (Instagram, TikTok, Reddit, X, Facebook, Threads, Snapchat, YouTube, Pinterest, LinkedIn). Whatever
  answers a web link, `mailto:` or SMS is never blocked by category (on the A25, Play tags Chrome,
  Firefox, Samsung Internet and Gmail Social). Games are allowed. Any app can be
  flipped either way on the Matrix settings screen; a new install is judged by the same rule. Everything
  else stays open, the browser included. YouTube is blocked.
- **Matrix HOME keeps its short list** and adds "All apps", the drawer minus blocked apps.
- **Notifications, the chosen people, the leave friction and the digest are unchanged.**
- **LEGION's own screens get sparse Matrix versions**, text-only like Matrix HOME: lists and to-dos,
  calendar and brief, notes and voice notes, ledger, pantry and fleet. The Soft screens are not
  recoloured. Map: `.scratch/matrix-open/`.

adr.title: Dumb phone mode is a manual switch that shrinks HOME, holds notifications and silences strangers

chunks.heading: 62. Dumb phone mode is a manual switch that shrinks HOME, holds notifications and silences strangers > Amendment, 2026-11-02: LEGION never leaves a Do Not Disturb of its own on
chunks.text:
Kevin: *"when i take it off quiet mode, its still in do not disturb and i dont get calls or message
notifications"*. On the A25 (Android 15, One UI) Quiet's rule was off, but the system's MANUAL DND rule
had been on for six days with `enabler=com.kevin.legion`.

- **Cause (traced, from the A25's `dumpsys audio`):** Quiet "off" restores the saved ringer. When that
  is SILENT, `setRingerMode` makes Android's ringer delegate turn on manual DND, owned by the caller,
  LEGION. The rule then outlives Quiet's own. It feeds itself: with DND on the ringer reads SILENT, so
  the next Quiet "on" saves SILENT again. The log shows `setRingerMode external to 0,
  caller=com.kevin.legion` at the 11-02 Quiet off. The 10-27 event that started it is older than the
  phone's logs; that it began the same way is reasoned, not seen.
- **Second path (code, not seen on the phone):** Matrix saved `currentInterruptionFilter`, which counts
  Quiet's rule. Entering Matrix with Quiet on saved PRIORITY, and leaving wrote it back as a manual DND.
- **Rule: the filter restored is the one the user had before LEGION touched DND.** Quiet records it on
  its first "on"; Matrix saves that record, not the live filter, when Quiet is on. When either mode
  already holds a save, the other uses it.
- **Quiet off, with Matrix holding no save:** if the user had no DND before Quiet and DND is on anyway,
  set the filter back to ALL. A DND the user had is left exactly as it was. A Quiet turned on by an
  older build that recorded nothing counts as "the user had none".
- **Matrix off while Quiet is still on:** the policy is restored, the filter is left alone. Writing
  ALL then would snooze Quiet's rule. Quiet's own "off" ends the manual DND.
- **Known edge:** Android does not tell an app who enabled the manual rule. If a schedule (such as
  Sleeping) starts while Quiet is on, Quiet "off" ends it too.

adr.title: The phone has one persona, Alfred

chunks.heading: 63. The phone has one persona, Alfred > Standing
chunks.text:
**The phone app has exactly one assistant persona, `ALFRED` in `ai/Personas.kt`.** There is no
roster, no picker and no `switch_companion` voice tool. Alfred's name and voice stay editable on the
Companion screen (`settings/companions`).

adr.title: The phone has one persona, Alfred

chunks.heading: 63. The phone has one persona, Alfred > Context
chunks.text:
The phone carried four built-in registers (Alfred, Dorothy, Kratos, Marcus), a roster screen to pick
between them, a voice tool to hand the conversation from one to another, and a Marcus-only
Meditations reader and tool. Kevin ruled that the phone has one assistant.

adr.title: The phone has one persona, Alfred

chunks.heading: 63. The phone has one persona, Alfred > Decision
chunks.text:
- `personaFor(key)` returns `ALFRED` for every key, so a stored `dorothy`, `kratos` or `marcus` key
  answers in Alfred's register. Nothing is migrated in Room: `companion_profiles` and its sync
  contract are unchanged, and no row is deleted (CLAUDE.md §5, additive-only).
- When this device's active profile is not an Alfred row and the synced roster holds one, the active
  selection moves to that Alfred row the next time the active profile is materialised
  (`CompanionProfileStore.materializeActive`, at app start and after every sync). With no Alfred row,
  the active profile stays and still answers as Alfred.
- The Companion screen edits the active profile's name and voice and writes `persona = "alfred"` on
  save. On an install with no profile it creates one from Alfred's defaults.
- Meditations is deleted: the reader, the `consult_meditations` tool and the bundled text.

adr.title: The phone has one persona, Alfred

chunks.heading: 63. The phone has one persona, Alfred > Consequences
chunks.text:
- **ADR 0047 is superseded.** With one persona there is nothing to hand over to, so the socket
  rebuild and spoken handover it describes are gone with the voice tool and the tap-to-switch.
- **Editing Alfred's voice does not rebuild a warm socket**, the same as editing a profile did
  before; the next socket picks it up.
- **The name is still not hardcoded** (CLAUDE.md §1). A profile can be Alfred's register under any
  name the household gives it.

adr.title: The phone ends turns locally, and you can talk over Alfred

chunks.heading: 64. The phone ends turns locally, and you can talk over Alfred > Standing
chunks.text:
**A phone conversation's turn ends on the phone, not on Gemini's server VAD**, and **on the phone
speaker or a wired headset the user can interrupt Alfred by talking**. Both are settings, both
default on (Settings > Assistant). Server VAD (900 ms, `START_SENSITIVITY_LOW`) is still what runs on
car Bluetooth, when Silero cannot load, or with the switch off.

- **End of turn:** Silero VAD v6.2 decides speech and silence. The turn ends after **700 ms** of
  silence. A Pipecat Smart Turn v3.2 check starts at 192 ms of silence. If it says "not done" before
  700 ms, the turn is held: checks run back to back until one says done, up to a 2.5 s cap. **Smart
  Turn can only extend a turn, never end one early.** No Smart Turn means silence only.
- **Barge-in:** call-style audio (MODE_IN_COMMUNICATION, voice-communication playback and capture
  with AEC), only during a conversation. The mic stays open while Alfred speaks. Speech
  interrupts only when Silero is confident and above the reply's own echo for 256 ms of any
  512 ms (amended 2026-10-28, below). After two
  self-interrupts it turns off for that conversation, and the user is told so.
- **Off on car Bluetooth in v1.** Those sessions keep half-duplex and server VAD.
- **A write tool cancelled by an interruption is reported, never undone.**

adr.title: The phone ends turns locally, and you can talk over Alfred

chunks.heading: 64. The phone ends turns locally, and you can talk over Alfred > Context
chunks.text:
Server VAD has one silence number for every pause. At 900 ms it cut Kevin off mid-thought and was
slow on short questions. Half-duplex meant Alfred could not be stopped by voice. The Live API accepts
`activityStart`/`activityEnd` only with server VAD disabled, so a content-aware end of turn has to
own both. On the A25, Smart Turn took p50 ~165 ms (4 threads) to 280-530 ms (2 threads), with a long
tail. That is too slow to end a turn faster than 700 ms of silence.

adr.title: The phone ends turns locally, and you can talk over Alfred

chunks.heading: 64. The phone ends turns locally, and you can talk over Alfred > Decision
chunks.text:
Local end of turn with a 700 ms silence base, which Smart Turn may only extend. Call-style barge-in
on Silero plus a learned echo floor. Both on by default, off on Bluetooth. Code in
`app/src/main/java/com/kevin/legion/service/turn/`.

adr.title: The phone ends turns locally, and you can talk over Alfred

chunks.heading: 64. The phone ends turns locally, and you can talk over Alfred > Consequences
chunks.text:
- The APK carries a second ONNX Runtime (about 34 MB of arm64 native code) and 11 MB of models,
  because sherpa-onnx's runtime is linked statically and exposes no general session API.
- While a conversation with barge-in runs, the phone is in call audio. The volume keys drive call
  volume, music may pause rather than duck, and dumb mode ignores this mode (`CallAudioMode.ownCommActive`).
- A barge-in starts an activity at once, with its pre-roll. If the trigger was Alfred's own echo,
  that echo is what the model hears. The self-interrupt cut-off limits how often this can happen;
  it does not prevent it.

adr.title: The phone ends turns locally, and you can talk over Alfred

chunks.heading: 64. The phone ends turns locally, and you can talk over Alfred > Amendment, 2026-10-28: the trigger is 256 ms of qualifying windows within 512 ms
chunks.text:
The barge-in trigger was 256 ms of consecutive qualifying windows (Silero >= 0.8 and above the echo
threshold), one stray window tolerated. On the A25 in call mode (run 5, build `191266c2`) Kevin said
"stop" into the mic over a 12.6 s reply: Silero peaked at 1.00, the level at 30,560 against a
threshold of 3,000, and 27 windows qualified, but Silero's probability jitters across a short plosive
word, so the longest run was 224 ms, one window short, and the reply never stopped. **The gate now
fires when 8 of the last 16 windows (256 ms within 512 ms) qualify, in any order.** A backchannel of
under 256 ms still never fires, and two short ones more than a span apart never add up. A barge-in
now seeds Smart Turn's turn audio and the wire pre-roll with the whole span plus one window
(544 ms), so a word whose onset is up to 512 ms before the fire is not clipped. The self-interrupt
verdict is unchanged.

adr.title: The phone ends turns locally, and you can talk over Alfred

chunks.heading: 64. The phone ends turns locally, and you can talk over Alfred > Amendment, 2026-10-29: the echo floor learns the echo, not the user
chunks.text:
On the A25 in call mode (run 6), the reply after a barge-in began while Kevin was still talking and
learned his voice as its echo (`echo_floor=9785 threshold=14677`); his next words reached 7 of the 8
windows a fire needs, at five times the threshold that had just fired. Every other run 5 and 6 reply
learned 400 to 550, yet each began at the 12,000 default (threshold 18,000). **Two rules now hold.**
For 1 s after the user was last known to be talking (a fire, speech during the verdict watch, or the
phone's `activityEnd`), a window Silero calls speech (>= 0.5) is not learned. And a reply starts from
the floor the previous reply learned in the same session; 12,000 applies only before any reply has
learned one. The trigger and the self-interrupt verdict are unchanged.

**Same day: a normal turn start sends 544 ms of pre-roll, not 400.** In run 5, "stop" said as a
reply ended reached the model as "top". By reading: a start confirms 224 ms after Silero's first
speech window, the ring also holds up to 100 ms of mic buffer after that window, and right after a
drain the policy does not listen for up to ~180 ms, so 400 ms reached only 76 to 176 ms before the
first counted window. 544 ms (the barge-in figure) reaches 220 to 320 ms. Every start now logs a
`pre_roll_ms=` line so the phone can confirm it. Silero's start threshold is unchanged.

adr.title: Read-only lookups may run non-blocking; writes stay blocking

chunks.heading: 65. Read-only lookups may run non-blocking; writes stay blocking > Standing
chunks.text:
**AMENDED 2026-11-03 by 0070-procedures-run-by-the-engine (procedures ticket 04): the set
grows from a fixed name list to "these four plus any procedure whose computed `writes` is
false"**, run through `run_procedure` with `WHEN_IDLE`; a procedure with a write step blocks, and
the disjointness test grows to cover it. Takes effect when procedures ticket 16 builds the phone
side. The text below is the original decision, kept as written.

**On the phone's Live socket, a write tool always blocks, and a named read-only lookup may run
`NON_BLOCKING`**: the model says one short holding line, keeps the floor while the lookup runs, and
answers when the result arrives. The set is `LiveToolbox.NON_BLOCKING_READ_TOOLS`, today `ask_fleet`,
`ask_body`, `ask_goals` and `ask_pantry`. **A write is a user-visible record change the assistant
could claim as an outcome** (Kevin, 2026-10-28); internal bookkeeping is not one. Its result goes back with `scheduling: WHEN_IDLE`. A setting, "Answer lookups
while talking" (Settings > Assistant, default on), empties the set; off means every declaration
blocks, as before. Typed chat and the head unit are untouched.

adr.title: Read-only lookups may run non-blocking; writes stay blocking

chunks.heading: 65. Read-only lookups may run non-blocking; writes stay blocking > Context
chunks.text:
`gemini-3.8-live` made non-blocking function calls the default, and on 2026-09-27 every declaration
was stamped `BLOCKING` because the model could say "done" before a result existed, which makes
[ADR 0031](0031-speech-honesty-clause.md)'s outcome rule unobeyable. That reasoning is about
outcomes. A read has none to misreport; its risk is a fact spoken before the data exists. Slow
lookups (a sub-agent POST plus tools) left dead air that blocking could not fill.

adr.title: Read-only lookups may run non-blocking; writes stay blocking

chunks.heading: 65. Read-only lookups may run non-blocking; writes stay blocking > Decision
chunks.text:
`GeminiLiveSession.withToolBehavior` stamps `NON_BLOCKING` on a name in the set and `BLOCKING` on
everything else, at the one choke point, so a new tool blocks unless someone opts it in. Only a
read may be in the set: a test proves it, and every tool behind it, is disjoint from
`isMutatingTool`, from the read-through tools, and from `ask_engine`, `aspect_clerk` and `ask_mail`.
Kevin ruled on 2026-10-28 what "write" means here: a user-visible record change the assistant could
claim as an outcome. `lookup_vin`'s spec-cache refresh (behind `ask_fleet`) and `ask_advisor`'s
advice-log row (behind `ask_goals`) are bookkeeping, so both dispatchers are reads. The result goes back `WHEN_IDLE`, never `INTERRUPT` (it would cut the holding line) and
never `SILENT` (a lookup the user asked for must be spoken). The prompt's `LOOKUP_HOLD_CLAUSE`, at
file scope beside `CANNOT_CLAUSE`, allows one holding line with no figure, date, name, fact or
outcome, then nothing until the result. Source: `.scratch/async-lookups/issues/01-*.md`.

adr.title: Read-only lookups may run non-blocking; writes stay blocking

chunks.heading: 65. Read-only lookups may run non-blocking; writes stay blocking > Consequences
chunks.text:
- **Bookkeeping may run under a holding line.** A spec-cache refresh or an advice-log row can land
  while the model is still talking; neither is something the user asked to have recorded, so
  neither is an outcome to claim. An advisor proposal is still applied only by `accept_proposal`,
  which blocks.
- **`lookup_vin` is not in `MUTATING_TOOLS`.** If it ever joins that set, the dispatcher test fails
  and points here: decide which ruling changed rather than silently dropping `ask_fleet`.
- **Unverified on the model.** Google's Live tools page does not list 3.8 as supporting
  asynchronous calls. If a `WHEN_IDLE` result is not spoken unprompted, the default flips to off
  (one line, `VoiceTurnSettings.ASYNC_LOOKUPS_DEFAULT`). Ticket 04 is that test.
- **The follow-up window waits for the lookup.** A lookup still running when the 8 s window
  ([ADR 0064](0064-phone-turn-taking-local-end-of-turn-and-barge-in.md)) expires holds the
  conversation open, and its result re-arms the window, so an answer never spoken still ends it. Since ticket 07 the window holds while an answer is owed (a sent result or a bare holding line), at most 20 s, so a holding line spoken after the result cannot end the conversation before the answer.
- **A cancelled lookup is dropped.** Barge-in cancels it like any call; nothing was written, so
  there is nothing to report.
- **The prompt rule is the only lever.** As with ADR 0031, a test guards the clause's presence,
  never its obedience.

adr.title: Feed apps can be blocked outside Matrix mode, with a 15 minute pass

chunks.heading: 66. Feed apps can be blocked outside Matrix mode, with a 15 minute pass > Standing
chunks.text:
**One switch, "Block feed apps always", blocks feed apps in normal mode too.** It lives on the Matrix
mode settings screen (Settings > Matrix mode, reachable without turning Matrix mode on), is stored under
its own key in the Matrix mode preferences file, not in the mode's own state, and is **off by default**
(clone-and-run: a stranger's build blocks nothing until they choose it). Kevin turns it on once.

**The same ladder decides.** What is blocked is ADR 0062's 2026-10-24 rule, unchanged: the seed list of
known feed apps, Android's Social, Video and News tags, and his manual flips. The bounce, the settings
list and the All apps drawer all read `BlockModel`; nothing keeps a second list.

**The bounce runs when Matrix mode is on OR the switch is.** Matrix behaviour is unchanged. Outside
Matrix mode the bounce screen says "<App> is blocked", with "Go back" as the primary button and "Ask for a
15 min pass" below it.

**The way in is a 15 minute pass, and it is friction, not a lock.** The same 60 second wait as leaving
Matrix mode, on the wall clock from the tap and persisted, then the typed sentence "I am choosing to open
<app> for 15 minutes" (case-insensitive, trimmed). It opens that ONE app for 15 minutes; then the app is
blocked again. Both instants, requested and granted-until, are wall-clock and persisted per package, so a
process kill or a screen lock cannot reset or extend them. The wait is clamped like the Matrix leave's,
and a clock set backwards cannot stretch a pass past 15 minutes. One pass at a time per app; asking again
while waiting keeps the original instant.

**No pass in Matrix mode.** While Matrix mode is on, a pass is refused and a running one does not count.
Matrix leave stays the only way out of Matrix mode.

**A pass ending with the app still open sends it home.** The bounce service sees only window-state
changes and may not read window content (ADR 0062). It remembers the last foreground app from the
events it already gets and checks when the pass ends; it bounces only if that app is still the one in
front. The next window change catches anything the timed check misses.

**Only the block comes out of Matrix mode.** The streak, the held notifications, the digest, chosen
people, call screening and code rain stay Matrix-only.

adr.title: Feed apps can be blocked outside Matrix mode, with a 15 minute pass

chunks.heading: 66. Feed apps can be blocked outside Matrix mode, with a 15 minute pass > Standing
chunks.text:
**The browser stays open, and no URL is blocked in LEGION.** Chrome and anything that answers a web link
are exempt in `BlockModel` (ADR 0062, 2026-10-24), so a feed's website is one tap away. Kevin closes that
hole himself with phone-wide Private DNS (NextDNS); LEGION does no in-app URL blocking.

adr.title: Feed apps can be blocked outside Matrix mode, with a 15 minute pass

chunks.heading: 66. Feed apps can be blocked outside Matrix mode, with a 15 minute pass > Context
chunks.text:
Kevin, 2026-10-30: Matrix mode stops the feeds only while it is on, and the feeds are the point. He wants
them blocked all the time, with a way in that costs a minute and a sentence rather than a trip into
Settings to unblock the app (which then stays unblocked).

adr.title: Feed apps can be blocked outside Matrix mode, with a 15 minute pass

chunks.heading: 66. Feed apps can be blocked outside Matrix mode, with a 15 minute pass > Consequences
chunks.text:
- `BlockModel.decide` gains a worded rung, `PASS` ("15 min pass, N min left"), after SYSTEM and before
  a manual block, applied only outside Matrix mode. A settings tap on a passed app changes what the app
  is after the pass, not the pass.
- An unfinished request lapses 10 minutes after the tap, and "Go back" drops it, so a pass is never one
  sentence away hours later.
- The accessibility service's description now names both switches.
- **2026-10-30, Kevin could not find the switch:** it also has its own "Feed blocker" row at the top
  level of Settings (same preference as the Matrix mode screen's), and the accessibility service is
  labelled "LEGION blocker" rather than "Matrix mode". The service class and component name are
  unchanged, so an install over the top keeps it enabled.
- **2026-11-02, Kevin: turning it down costs the same as a pass.** The switch was one tap off, a
  settings tap unblocked an app for good, and turning the accessibility service off killed the block
  silently, so the 15 minute pass was never the cheapest way in. Now:
  - Switch ON to OFF, and a settings tap that would make a blocked app open, both take the pass's 60
    second wall-clock wait (persisted, clamped, clock-backwards safe, lapsing 10 minutes after the
    tap), then a typed sentence: "I am choosing to turn off the feed blocker" or "I am choosing to
    unblock <app>" (case-insensitive, trimmed). The change applies the moment the sentence lands; the
    switch reads on until then. `dumb/FeedOffGate.kt`, own prefs prefix `feed_off.requested.`, timing
    rules from `FeedPassRule`.
  - Turning it ON and blocking an app stay instant. The unblock direction is read without the pass,
    so an app on a pass is still gated.
  - The gate applies in Matrix mode too; Matrix's own rules (no pass, leave as the only exit) are
    unchanged.
  - Switch on with the LEGION blocker service off posts an ongoing "Feed blocker is off" notice that
    taps through to Accessibility settings (`dumb/FeedBlockWatch.kt`). Checked when the service
    unbinds (the moment it is turned off) and connects, on every app foreground
    (`ProcessLifecycleOwner`), and when a screen with the switch resumes; no polling, no WorkManager.
    Cleared when the service is back or the switch is off. It needs the notification permission; with
    it refused nothing shows.

adr.title: Feed apps can be blocked outside Matrix mode, with a 15 minute pass

chunks.heading: 66. Feed apps can be blocked outside Matrix mode, with a 15 minute pass > Consequences
chunks.text:
- Still friction, not a lock: no device admin, nothing stops an uninstall.
- The pass's expiry check runs on a `Handler`, which runs on uptime: in deep sleep it fires late, and the
  next window change is the backstop.
- Compulsion test (CLAUDE.md section 7): nothing here is an unsolicited raise; the bounce answers an app
  Kevin opened, and the switch silences all of it (since 2026-11-02, behind the same minute and sentence
  as a pass). The "Feed blocker is off" notice is anchored to a setting he can check, actionable now,
  and goes away when the switch is off.

adr.title: Claude session: Alfred hands tasks to Claude Code on Kevin's laptops

chunks.heading: 67. Claude session: Alfred hands tasks to Claude Code on Kevin's laptops > Standing
chunks.text:
**Alfred may send a task to Claude Code on Kevin's laptops only when Kevin named it, or said yes to
a one-line offer as the very next thing he said.** The task runs headless on whichever claude.ai
subscription the laptop's CLI is logged into (on the Alienware, Kevin's personal Max plan, limits
shared with his own sessions), never the API. The engine (ADR 0044) holds the task, its summary, any file
Kevin asked for and each machine's status, 30 days, tenanted by household (ADR 0045). The
laptop's transcript never leaves the laptop. It is called "Claude session" in speech, on screen
and in code.

adr.title: Claude session: Alfred hands tasks to Claude Code on Kevin's laptops

chunks.heading: 67. Claude session: Alfred hands tasks to Claude Code on Kevin's laptops > Context
chunks.text:
Kevin wanted the assistant to do what Claude Code does: find a file, write a small script, parse a
PDF, book something. Alfred's own tools cannot. Kevin pays for a Claude subscription and does not
want API spend (*"i was hoping more of using my monthly sub and not the api"*). Ticket 02's spike
(2026-11-01, Claude Code 2.1.316) showed one long-lived headless `claude -p` stream-json session
can take several messages, start a background helper per task, stay free, and resume by id.

adr.title: Claude session: Alfred hands tasks to Claude Code on Kevin's laptops

chunks.heading: 67. Claude session: Alfred hands tasks to Claude Code on Kevin's laptops > Decision
chunks.text:
- **Named or asked.** Named ("use Claude on my Alienware to...") is sent. Not named: Alfred offers
  only after his own tools cannot do it, in one line, and only the next thing Kevin says counts as
  the yes. A yes covers that one task. ADR 0031's outcome verbs apply: Alfred says "sent" only
  after `POST /api/claude/tasks/` succeeded, and "done" only for a task the engine says is done.
- **Machines by spoken name.** "Alienware" and "work laptop". A named machine wins. Unnamed goes to
  the only machine online; with more than one online the task comes back `needs_machine`, Alfred
  asks which, and the answer assigns it (`POST tasks/{id}/assign/`).
- **Scope per machine.** The Alienware is `full`: every fixed drive, read and write, as Kevin's
  Windows user, not elevated. The work laptop is `listed`: its repos folder only, summaries only.
  The engine enforces the second half: for a `listed` machine it keeps no found-file rows,
  refuses send-file and upload, and drops `last_prompt_summary` from its interactive session rows.
  **The work laptop may email Kevin a summary, never a file** (ruling 18, Kevin 2026-11-01): it
  takes `deliver: "email_self"`, and the mail carries summary text only.
- **The ask list.** Deleting or overwriting Kevin's files, sending, booking or paying, installing
  software and changing system settings stop and come back as one question
  (`needs_confirmation`). Everything else runs. On the Alienware (Kevin, 2026-11-01) this is
  permission mode `dontAsk`, a broad explicit allowlist, and a `PreToolUse` hook that denies the
  ask-list operations with a reason; the hook is the enforcement, the allowlist a second guard.
  That is worker configuration (ticket 04), not engine code. Kevin's yes is a follow-up task with
  `confirms: true`, accepted only when its parent is `needs_confirmation`; the worker unlocks the
  asked step for that task alone.
- **Delivery by mail (amended 2026-11-01).** Alfred has his own Gmail; every send is on the ask
  list, except that **naming his own email in the request is the yes for that one task** ("...and
  email it to me"): the phone sets `deliver: "email_self"` on the task, and the worker's
  `send_mail.py` mails the file to Kevin from Alfred's account on the laptop. The engine carries
  the flag and never sends mail. Mail to anyone else still asks. WhatsApp delivery was chosen and
  dropped the same day.

adr.title: Claude session: Alfred hands tasks to Claude Code on Kevin's laptops

chunks.heading: 67. Claude session: Alfred hands tasks to Claude Code on Kevin's laptops > Decision
chunks.text:
- **Gmail and Amazon orders (amended 2026-11-04, Kevin).** On the Alienware a helper may read
  Kevin's Gmail, read only (search and read thread; `session.py` `GMAIL_READ`). For Amazon orders,
  mail first, then the carrier's public tracking page (UPS, USPS, FedEx) when the mail names one;
  never Amazon's own site. A headless read of his Amazon orders page was built and dropped the same
  day: Amazon sent the unattended browser to a fresh sign-in (`max_auth_age=0`) hours after Kevin
  signed in, and getting past that would be getting past a bot check (Kevin chose option A). The
  summary keeps only the answer (CLAUDE.md section 7, carve-out 2026-11-04). The work laptop has
  no Gmail.
- **Availability.** A locked laptop is on; powered off is off. A machine with no heartbeat for
  90 s is offline. A running task is failed after 30 minutes, or after its machine is silent for
  10. All three are computed when read, never written by a job.
- **Files.** A helper lists what it found; nothing uploads until Kevin says yes to "want it on your
  phone?". Files up to 25 MB, stored in Postgres beside the task because Cloud Run's filesystem
  does not persist. Results and files are deleted after 30 days (`manage.py
  claude_session_prune`, daily, from `deploy/crontab`). **On deploy,
  `deploy/cloudrun/install_schedule.py` must be run** or Cloud Scheduler never runs the prune.
- **Interactive sessions are readable** (machine, project, state, a one-line summary of the last
  prompt, except from a `listed` machine). A session waiting on Kevin is listed first, and a
  running task shows its helper's current step (120 characters, cleared when it finishes).
- **A hands path exists** (ADR 0035): the Claude session screen on the phone, first.
- **Nothing logs a request, a summary or a file name**, on the engine or in admin.

adr.title: Claude session: Alfred hands tasks to Claude Code on Kevin's laptops

chunks.heading: 67. Claude session: Alfred hands tasks to Claude Code on Kevin's laptops > Decision
chunks.text:
- **A researched page reaches the phone** (amended 2026-11-03, Kevin, ticket 09). `deliver:
  phone` asks for the result as one HTML page. The worker uploads it at finish (asking for it was
  the yes); the engine keeps it 5 MB at most, `text/html` only, and serves it only through a signed
  link that names one household and one file and lives 10 minutes, with `Content-Security-Policy:
  sandbox allow-scripts`, so its scripts run in an opaque origin. Alfred asks before opening it;
  a yes, a notification tap or the screen's button opens it in LEGION's browser. The web desk lists
  it under its task. The work laptop never takes one. Retention is the task's 30 days.

adr.title: Claude session: Alfred hands tasks to Claude Code on Kevin's laptops

chunks.heading: 67. Claude session: Alfred hands tasks to Claude Code on Kevin's laptops > Consequences
chunks.text:
- Every laptop worker and hook holds an ordinary household device token. The engine cannot tell a
  worker from the phone; the API's "who" is convention, and a household member's token could
  finish a task. Accepted for v1 (Kevin 2026-11-01; ADR 0045: membership is the only
  authorization). **Later: worker endpoints restricted to machine tokens.**
- 25 MB rows in Postgres cost database storage for 30 days; a storage backend would replace them
  when the engine gets one.
- Subscription use is not metered or warned about (*"just run it"*).
- Recurring tasks are not in this decision; they come later, set by voice.
- Source: `.scratch/claude-session/map.md` rulings 1 to 17, tickets 01 to 03.

adr.title: Recruiter is a third household role, and it only narrows

chunks.heading: 68. Recruiter is a third household role, and it only narrows > Standing
chunks.text:
**AMENDED 2026-11-02 by 0069-each-recruiter-visit-gets-its-own-household (ticket 13):
recruiters write inside their own visit household.** Each visit gets its own throwaway copy of the
demo household, and the visitor is its only member. The role still only narrows: routes and tools
are named lists (default deny), outside accounts, devices, body and settings stay closed, and a
recruiter's writes land only in its own copy. The "default deny on routes" and "no writes by any
credential" bullets below are the original decision, kept as written; 0069 says what replaced them.

**A `HouseholdMember` may have the role `recruiter`.** It is set only on throwaway visitor users in
the demo household, made by `POST /api/demo/enter`. It is the first role that governs data, and it
only ever takes access away. This amends 0045-households-are-tenants's "no roles inside a
household except `owner`". `owner` and `member` are unchanged.

adr.title: Recruiter is a third household role, and it only narrows

chunks.heading: 68. Recruiter is a third household role, and it only narrows > Context
chunks.text:
Kevin gives recruiters a link and one shared invite code so they can try LEGION on the live engine.
They must read a fake household and never reach Kevin's data, his accounts or his machines. Tenancy
already keeps them in the demo household. Inside it, the web assistant and the REST API hand every
member everything, which is too much for a stranger.

adr.title: Recruiter is a third household role, and it only narrows

chunks.heading: 68. Recruiter is a third household role, and it only narrows > Decision
chunks.text:
- **Role follows the user.** A session and a token for the same visitor are both recruiter. The
  browser cannot say what it is.
- **Default deny on routes.** `IsHouseholdMember` refuses a recruiter on every route unless the view
  sets `allows_recruiter = True`. Today only the two assistant doors do (`/api/assistant/session`,
  `/api/assistant/tool`). `/mcp` refuses.
- **Default deny on tools.** A recruiter's assistant may call `assistant.surface.RECRUITER_TOOLS`
  only, read tools over ledger, fleet, pantry, notes, dates and places. The same list builds the
  locked Live token's declarations and gates the tool door. A tool added to the registry does not
  reach a recruiter until someone lists it.
- **No writes by any credential.** `household.permissions.write_refusal` refuses a recruiter before
  the token scope is even read. The visitor token is also `read` scope. Either fence alone holds.
- **Visits end.** The visitor token expires in two hours (`DeviceToken.expires_at`). The browser
  session dies with it. `manage.py prune_demo_visitors` deletes expired visitors and keeps the visit
  row with its `ref`.

adr.title: Recruiter is a third household role, and it only narrows

chunks.heading: 68. Recruiter is a third household role, and it only narrows > Consequences
chunks.text:
- The shared code is stored hashed, unlike `household.Invite`. It is shown once by
  `manage.py demo_code rotate`. `demo_code off` closes the door.
- The assistant stays session-only (ADR 0056). The visitor token does not open it; the session
  `/api/demo/enter` sets beside the token does.
- A role that WIDENS access is still a new ruling, not a refactor.

adr.title: Each recruiter visit gets its own household, and only there may a gated row be deleted

chunks.heading: 69. Each recruiter visit gets its own household, and only there may a gated row be deleted > Standing
chunks.text:
**Every recruiter visit has its own throwaway copy of the demo household**, flagged
`Household.is_demo_visit`, and the visitor is its only member. The recruiter uses the normal web
app and assistant on that copy, writes included. **The database lets a gated money row be deleted
only when its household carries that flag**, so a visit can be deleted whole when it ends. This
amends 0068-recruiter-role-narrows-only ("no writes by any credential") and narrows the scope of
the gated-row immutability 0042-business-rules-live-in-postgres keeps in SQL; it does not change
what a gated row means anywhere else.

adr.title: Each recruiter visit gets its own household, and only there may a gated row be deleted

chunks.heading: 69. Each recruiter visit gets its own household, and only there may a gated row be deleted > Context
chunks.text:
Kevin, 2026-11-02: *"everything i can do on the phone save the phone only functions i should be able
to do on the web legion page and by extension the recruiter on the demo mode"*, then option C: each
visitor gets a private copy. A shared read-only demo household cannot show writes, and writes in a
shared household would leak between visitors. A per-visit copy has to be cleaned up, and the
`forbid_mutation` triggers refuse to delete a verified statement, transaction, receipt or line item
anywhere (post a reversal instead), so without an exemption no visit could ever be removed. Kevin
approved the exemption the same day: *"ok"*.

adr.title: Each recruiter visit gets its own household, and only there may a gated row be deleted

chunks.heading: 69. Each recruiter visit gets its own household, and only there may a gated row be deleted > Decision
chunks.text:
- **One household per visit.** `POST /api/demo/enter` creates `Demo visit <id>`, sets
  `is_demo_visit = true`, seeds it through the same gate and serializers as the shared demo household
  (`household.demo_seed.seed_household`), and makes the visitor its only member, role `recruiter`,
  all in one transaction. The shared "Demo" household is no longer joined by anyone.
- **The flag is set by that door and nothing else.** `editable=False`, named by no serializer, no
  admin form, no view. Kevin's household can never carry it.
- **The exemption is by household, checked last, DELETE only.** `public.gated_row_guard()`
  (statements, receipts, receipt line items) and `public.ledger_transactions_guard()` keep every
  existing rule (UPDATE refused everywhere; DELETE only for `UNRECONCILED`, and for the ledger
  ADR 0057's `BANK_API` and supersede cases) and add one last case: DELETE is allowed when the row's
  household has `is_demo_visit`. Shipped by `household/migrations/0008`, SQL in
  `household/demo_visit_sql.py`, nothing in `private`.
- **Prune deletes the visit whole, and nothing else.** `manage.py prune_demo_visitors` deletes every
  tenant-table row of an expired visit's household in foreign-key order, then the visitor, then the
  household, and refuses any household without the flag.
- **The recruiter fence moves, and still only narrows.** Routes: `household/recruiter_routes.py`
  names every guarded view as allowed, read-only or denied with a reason (outside accounts, devices,
  body, memory, settings, `/mcp` denied); a view in none of them is refused. Tools: the member web
  surface less `list_tables`, record tools narrowed to ledger, fleet, pantry, places and voice notes
  (body out, Kevin's ruling 3; voice notes in, ruling 4). A recruiter writes only inside a
  demo-visit household (`write_refusal`), and only through its browser session: the visitor token
  stays `read`.

adr.title: Each recruiter visit gets its own household, and only there may a gated row be deleted

chunks.heading: 69. Each recruiter visit gets its own household, and only there may a gated row be deleted > Consequences
chunks.text:
- A bug that set the flag on a real household would make its gated rows deletable. The flag has one
  writer, the trigger reads it live, and `delete_visit_household` refuses an unflagged household, so
  that bug needs two independent mistakes. `tests/test_demo_visit.py` pins each fence.
- Seeding a visit runs the whole demo seed inside the request (measured about 0.2 s on a local
  Postgres with fsync off; Cloud Run will be slower).
- A recruiter made before this (a member of the shared household) is treated as an ended visit
  everywhere.

adr.title: Procedures: compiled multi-step answers, run by the engine

chunks.heading: 70. Procedures: compiled multi-step answers, run by the engine > Standing
chunks.text:
**A recurring multi-step answer ("how's the car", "money", the morning briefing) is a procedure:
a versioned DAG of steps stored in Postgres and run by the Django engine, reached by every client
through ONE engine tool, `run_procedure`.** No graph database, no new service. This amends
0065-read-only-lookups-may-be-non-blocking: on the phone, a procedure whose computed `writes`
is false joins the non-blocking set.

adr.title: Procedures: compiled multi-step answers, run by the engine

chunks.heading: 70. Procedures: compiled multi-step answers, run by the engine > Context
chunks.text:
Kevin, 2026-11-03, adapting a talk on "graph engineering" to every LEGION client. Traced on dev the
same day: a car or money ask costs 2-5 model round trips (a Live turn per tool, plus a sub-agent
router or `ask_engine`'s up to four POSTs), and the phone computes car and money figures locally
while the engine computes them again in Django. `brief/compose.py` and the phone's `get_sitrep`
already showed the alternative: a fixed sequence composed by code, one call. Kevin ruled all nine
decisions as recommended (*"approve all 9 as recommended"*).

adr.title: Procedures: compiled multi-step answers, run by the engine

chunks.heading: 70. Procedures: compiled multi-step answers, run by the engine > Decision
chunks.text:
- **Storage.** App `server/procedures/`. Tables `procedures` and `procedure_versions` in `public`,
  carrying `household_id` (NULL for a built-in), listed in `household.tenancy.TENANT_TABLES`. A
  version is immutable; a change is a new version. Built-ins are YAML in
  `server/procedures/builtin/`, loaded after every schema migration, a new version only when the
  file's hash changed, so a stranger's clone has them with no manual step.
- **Six step kinds, a closed set:** `tool` (one registry tool through `run_engine_tool`), `compute`
  (a named pure function), `decide`, `ask`, `check`, `say`. A seventh is a ruling, not a refactor.
  **DAG only**: no loops, no recursion, no procedure calling a procedure.
- **`writes` is computed**, true when any reachable `tool` step's tool writes. Clients stamp
  BLOCKING from it.
- **`decide`**: a small model on the household's own key picks one of the branch names the
  definition lists, nothing else; any other output fails the step and the run takes `on_fail`.
  Labelled in the trace (`chosen_by = model`) and in the result ("a model chose"). **Not allowed in
  a procedure that writes.**
- **`ask`**: the run returns `needs_answer` with a resume token and never holds the call open; only
  the very next utterance answers; **2 minutes** and it is cancelled, said in words. **Every write
  step is preceded by an `ask`** unless marked `named_by_request`. Both refused at load.
- **Clients.** Phone and head unit declare `run_procedure` directly, not behind `ask_engine`. On the
  phone a read-only procedure runs NON_BLOCKING `WHEN_IDLE`; a writing one is BLOCKING; the head
  unit stays all-BLOCKING. Web gets it from the registry. Recruiters get only procedures built
  entirely from `RECRUITER_TOOLS`, and the runner applies `surface.refusal_for` per step, because
  that fence is not in `run_tool`.
- **Engine down**: when the engine is reachable, voice speaks the engine's figures; when it is not,
  the phone answers from its own copy and says so, with the sync time.
- **Traces** keep step args and trimmed results like the conversation record, not `McpCall`'s
  no-arguments posture: members 60 days, recruiter visit runs deleted with the visit household
  (30-day cap). A step that would read third-party content is refused, so it is never stored.
- **Distillation** only proposes; Kevin approves every new procedure. Never auto-activated.

adr.title: Procedures: compiled multi-step answers, run by the engine

chunks.heading: 70. Procedures: compiled multi-step answers, run by the engine > Consequences
chunks.text:
- Car and money answers move onto the Django copy of each figure (CLAUDE.md §7: a business rule
  lives in Django once). The phone's local copies stay as the engine-down fallback until an
  evaluation shows where the two disagree.
- `run_procedure` is `writes=False` on the registry so a read-scoped token can run read-only
  procedures; the runner checks the write fence itself before any writing step. A future change
  that let the static flag decide would refuse every procedure to a recruiter.
- The branch report can list "never ran" branches only because the graph is finite. Loops would
  end that, which is why they are out of v1.

adr.title: LEGION has its own browser, and Alfred drives it by voice

chunks.heading: 71. LEGION has its own browser, and Alfred drives it by voice > Standing
chunks.text:
**LEGION's browser is its own Android WebView, not Chrome.** A full-screen screen in the phone app
with an address/search bar, back, forward, reload and close. Kevin chose it (option B) over Chrome
Custom Tabs, which LEGION cannot read or drive, and over driving Chrome through an accessibility
service, which is brittle and far too powerful. Kevin's words and the comparison are on
`.scratch/voice-browser/map.md`.

**The profile persists.** Cookies and site storage live in WebView's own store and survive closing
the browser and restarting the app. They are not Chrome's cookies: he signs in to each site once.
JavaScript is on; file and content access are off; downloads are refused in words; pop-up windows are
off, so a link that would open a new tab opens in place. **Third-party cookies are on** (Chrome's own
default), because single sign-on redirects need them.

**Passwords are Android's Autofill framework's**, the same Google Password Manager store Chrome uses.
The WebView is marked important for autofill and the framework reads its fields. **The model never
sees or types a password:** the page reader reports a password field as a password field with no
value, and the `type` action refuses one.

**Search is Google.** Words that are not a web address become a Google search; `kind: images` is
Google Images.

**One voice tool, `browser`**, to keep the Live setup payload small: `open`, `read`, `click`,
`scroll`, `type`, `back`, `close`. CLAUDE.md section 7 binds every result: "opened" only after the
page finished loading in that call, "clicked" only when an element was found and clicked. A question
to be answered in words goes to `ask_engine` (the engine's `web_search`); `browser` is for seeing a
page.

**Ask first, and the ask is enforced in code.** Submitting a form, anything labelled pay, buy,
purchase, order, checkout, send, post, publish, delete, remove, book, reserve, confirm, subscribe or
transfer, and typing into any field on a checkout or payment page, returns a question and a one-use
token instead of acting. Only a second call with that token and `confirmed: true`, on the same page
and element, within 90 seconds, acts. The `type` action never presses Enter.

adr.title: LEGION has its own browser, and Alfred drives it by voice

chunks.heading: 71. LEGION has its own browser, and Alfred drives it by voice > Standing
chunks.text:
**Page text is read-through** (CLAUDE.md section 7): `browser` is in
`LiveToolbox.EPISODIC_EXCLUDED_TOOLS` and the engine's `READ_THROUGH_TOOLS` mirror. Nothing a page says
is stored, synced or remembered; `remember` is refused in a turn that read a page.

**The feed blocker reaches the browser.** Each seed feed app (`BlockSeed.PACKAGES`) names its web
domains in one map, `dumb/FeedDomains.kt`. A main-frame navigation to one of them is blocked when the
bounce is active (Matrix mode, or "Block feed apps always") and `BlockPolicy` says that app is
blocked, so ADR 0066's 15 minute pass, Matrix mode's no-pass rule and a manual allow or block all
apply unchanged. The browser shows the same bounce words and pass the app bounce shows.

**Hands path (ADR 0035):** "Browser" on Matrix home's kept list, and a launcher entry named "Browser",
which every app drawer lists.

adr.title: LEGION has its own browser, and Alfred drives it by voice

chunks.heading: 71. LEGION has its own browser, and Alfred drives it by voice > Consequences
chunks.text:
- **Category intent does not reach websites.** Android's Social/Video/News tag belongs to an
  installed package, not a host, so only the seed list's sites block in the browser. A new feed site
  is a line in `FeedDomains`, not a category rule.
- **Embedded frames are not blocked**: a YouTube video embedded in a recipe page plays. Blocking
  sub-frames would break ordinary pages.
- **Google's own sign-in refuses WebView** (`disallowed_useragent`). Sites that sign in with Google
  may not work; sites with their own passwords do. LEGION does not disguise its user agent.
- Pages that need pop-up windows (some payment and OAuth flows) do not work in place.
- Adding "Browser" to Matrix home's kept list changes a ruled list (ADR 0062); it sits after Brief,
  before Books, so All apps still follows Books.

adr.title: Alfred's wording comes from the engine; the phone updates itself, and asks first

chunks.heading: 72. Alfred's wording comes from the engine; the phone updates itself, and asks first > Standing
chunks.text:
**Two halves, both binding** (map `.scratch/alfred-ota/`, Kevin ruled all five decisions as
recommended on 2026-11-05).

**A. The Alfred pack.** Alfred's wording (prompt clauses, tool wording, flags, extra rules) is a
versioned pack in the repo, `server/assistant/packs/alfred.yaml`, generated from
`shared_clauses.txt` plus `alfred.source.yaml` and changed only by an engine deploy (decision 1).
The engine serves it at `GET /api/assistant/pack` with an ETag. The phone (`ai/AlfredPack.kt`)
fetches it at app start and whenever the cached prompt is dropped, with a 2 s timeout, keeps the
last good pack on disk, and otherwise runs the pack its APK was built with. Engine down or any
error is silent: only LIVE_AUDIT's `session_start ... pack=<version>/<remote|cache|bundled>` says
which wording a conversation ran. A remote pack with a lower version than the APK's is ignored.

**The locked set is compiled into the app** (decision 2): `CRISIS`, `SAFETY_INSTRUCTIONS`,
`CANNOT_CLAUSE`, `ASK_BEFORE` and `NO_PASSWORDS`. The engine refuses to load a pack that names
one; the phone drops them anyway, as a clause, a tool override or a flag, in any letter case. A
compromised engine cannot talk Alfred out of these. The layer order of the prompt stays in code;
only slot text comes from the pack.

**B. Self-update.** A release is an APK in a private bucket, recorded on the engine
(`server/releases/`) by `tools/release_apk.py`, which Kevin runs, or the worker after his yes
(decision 4: a publish counts as a send). The `fast` build stays signed with this laptop's debug
key (decision 5); `deploy/release/signer.sha256` pins it. The phone (`update/`) checks
`/api/releases/latest`, downloads on Wi-Fi only unless Kevin allows mobile data, and refuses in
words a file whose sha256 differs from the release's or whose signer is not the installed app's.

adr.title: Alfred's wording comes from the engine; the phone updates itself, and asks first

chunks.heading: 72. Alfred's wording comes from the engine; the phone updates itself, and asks first > Standing
chunks.text:
**Always ask** (decision 3). A notification with Install and Later, and Alfred says it once at a
natural pause. Kevin's yes, by voice or tap, is required every time. **Never installed
mid-conversation, in Matrix mode, or with the car connected:** a yes given in a conversation
installs when the conversation ends; Matrix or the car refuses in words. `PackageInstaller`
commits with `USER_ACTION_NOT_REQUIRED` on Android 12+, so after the first update Kevin's yes is
the only prompt. `MY_PACKAGE_REPLACED` restarts the assistant service. The voice tool `app_update`
and Settings, Updates call the same `UpdateController` (ADR 0035).

**versionCode is `yyDDDHHmm` UTC** for `fast` and `release` (year, day of year, hour, minute;
monotonic, under Android's 2,100,000,000 cap until 2099), `debug` stays 1 and never self-updates.
The map first said `yyMMddHHmm`, which is already past both the Int and Android caps.
versionName is `<yyyy-MM-dd>-<short sha>`, or `-dev` with no git.

adr.title: Alfred's wording comes from the engine; the phone updates itself, and asks first

chunks.heading: 72. Alfred's wording comes from the engine; the phone updates itself, and asks first > Context
chunks.text:
The only way to change Alfred on the phone was a laptop, wireless adb and an install, and most
Alfred fixes are wording. An APK is 180-220 MB, and Android only accepts an update signed by the
installed app's key.

adr.title: Alfred's wording comes from the engine; the phone updates itself, and asks first

chunks.heading: 72. Alfred's wording comes from the engine; the phone updates itself, and asks first > Consequences
chunks.text:
- A wording fix is an engine deploy; the next conversation runs it. A code fix is a published
  release and Kevin's yes.
- Losing `~/.android/debug.keystore` means no more updates without an uninstall. Back it up.
- The first update after an adb install still shows Android's own confirm (adb is the installer
  of record); after it LEGION is.
- Rollback is a new build of the old code with a higher versionCode. Nothing downgrades.
- Every word the pack adds to the prompt is billed on every Live reconnect, like any clause
  (`LiveSetupPayloadSizeTest` measures the bundled pack, not what the engine later sends).

adr.title: Household finance: layers, internal transfers, floors and estimates

chunks.heading: 73. Household finance: layers, internal transfers, floors and estimates > Standing
chunks.text:
**The engine holds the whole household's money across two countries, and Alfred tracks, projects
and warns; he never moves money.** Accounts, dated balances, the day's USD/SGD rate, the income
plan and the limits Kevin set live in `server/finance/`. The real figures never enter the public
repo: they are loaded from a private file outside it (`manage.py load_household_finance`).

adr.title: Household finance: layers, internal transfers, floors and estimates

chunks.heading: 73. Household finance: layers, internal transfers, floors and estimates > Standing
chunks.text:
- **Layers** (map ruling 2): liquid (bank accounts less cards), investments, CPF (locked),
  property (flat less loan, locked), other. Runway counts liquid and investments only.
- **Money is int cents; a rate is int `rate_micros`**, rounded half to even. **Debt is negative.**
  The headline is USD; the SGD view, and the USD view of SGD accounts, use today's stored rate (the
  nearest earlier day's when today has none, never a later day's). A figure that needs a rate when
  none is stored is refused in words, never converted at a guess. Read-only surfaces never fetch a
  rate; `manage.py fx_rates` does, daily.
- **Household-internal money is not spend** (map ruling 10). It is a layer ABOVE the ported spend
  rules (`api/spend.py`, the phone's Kotlin, kept cent for cent by `tests/test_spend_parity.py`),
  never inside them. A row is internal when it is shaped like a transfer AND names a member's
  configured payer name (both: a bank prints the holder's name on payroll too), or when a USD and
  an SGD transfer leg of opposite sign, within 10 days, agree within 3% at the earlier day's stored
  rate. A fee or charge line never is. Every internal row says why.
- **Floors** (map ruling 4): test A, no burn, is planned income covering spend plus the mortgage;
  test C is a household liquid floor, and a US top-up trigger: checking less what is owed on the
  card covers the next 30 days of US bills, warned before the card's due day.
- **Safe to spend** (Kevin, 2026-11-05), the main daily money figure: checking, less everything
  owed on the card (current balance plus pending charges), less the US fixed bills due before the
  next expected pay date or 30 days out, whichever is sooner (the top-up rule's own window, so a
  months-long gap in pay does not hold back months of bills). A top-up is needed when it is below
  zero or the top-up trigger is short, by that day less the warning days.
- **Anything worked out is an estimate, and says so** (CLAUDE.md section 4 rule 5): a computed
  balance, every projection, the plan's pay dates, a detected bill or subscription. A balance from
  the bank feed or a gated statement is fact.

adr.title: Household finance: layers, internal transfers, floors and estimates

chunks.heading: 73. Household finance: layers, internal transfers, floors and estimates > Context
chunks.text:
Kevin is a student until full-time work starts, his household's money sits in two countries, and
a transfer from Singapore takes days. Plaid covers only his two US accounts; everything else
arrives monthly. The repo and its wiki are public, so the mechanism is public and the figures
cannot be.

adr.title: Household finance: layers, internal transfers, floors and estimates

chunks.heading: 73. Household finance: layers, internal transfers, floors and estimates > Decision
chunks.text:
One engine app, read-only surfaces and pull-based tools (`net_worth`, `cash_flow`, `runway`,
`safe_to_spend`, `budgets`), every figure computed once in Django and shared by the routes and the
tools. Definitions this ADR fixes that Kevin did not rule on, so a future change is a change here:

- **Runway** projects each side month by month for two years from the income plan and the average
  netted spend of the last 3 FULL months, plus the mortgage while it is not in the ledger. It names
  the month household liquid falls below the floor, on the expected plan and on the fallback plan
  (as if every expected income never came), and the cross-border transfer the US side needs to stay
  above its own floor (the next 30 days of US bills) through every gap month: the largest
  shortfall, by the first day of the first short month less `transfer_lead_days`.
- **Wave 1's spend is the ledger's**: only accounts with ledger rows. Every body names the liquid
  accounts it cannot see.
- **The card's statement balance is not on the bank feed**, so its current balance (never smaller
  once a statement has closed) stands in for it, labelled an estimate.
- **A recurring merchant** is the first three words of the description, seen in 3 or more months,
  amounts within 15% of the median, charges 25 to 35 days apart. A subscription is new when its
  merchant first appears this month in the Subscriptions category.
- **Budget pace**: the marker is cap x days elapsed / days in the month; a projection is given only
  from day 10.

adr.title: Household finance: layers, internal transfers, floors and estimates

chunks.heading: 73. Household finance: layers, internal transfers, floors and estimates > Consequences
chunks.text:
- The privacy guard has two layers: `tests/test_finance_privacy.py` holds every finance file to
  the synthetic household's figures, and `tools/finance_privacy_check.py <private file>` searches a
  branch's added lines and commit messages for the real file's figures, names and account numbers.
  The first can be fooled by adding a real figure to the synthetic list; the second catches that.
- `GET /api/ledger/spend` now differs from the phone's Money screen by exactly
  `excluded.household_internal_cents` until the phone reads the engine's figure.
- The alerts (wave 3) are bound by CLAUDE.md section 7's compulsion test and by map ruling 6: at
  most one spoken money alert a day.

adr.title: Alfred builds Alfred: one yes ships a change

chunks.heading: 74. Alfred builds Alfred: one yes ships a change > Standing
chunks.text:
**The Claude worker on the Alienware may fix, build and ship LEGION itself, and ships nothing
without Kevin's one yes to "Ready: <one line>. Ship it?"** A fix, a feature and a book take the
same path: Claude works on a branch in its own work folder, tests, asks; on the yes the worker
merges to dev and main, pushes, deploys the engine and/or publishes the phone update, or adds
the book to the household library. Red tests never reach the question. Pushing, deploying and
publishing happen only inside `tools/claude_session/ship.py` and `undo.py`, which check the yes
token; the ask-list hook denies them everywhere else, token or not. This amends ADR 0067 (which
left deploys to Kevin) for this path only; Kevin can still deploy by hand.

adr.title: Alfred builds Alfred: one yes ships a change

chunks.heading: 74. Alfred builds Alfred: one yes ships a change > Context
chunks.text:
Kevin wanted "build me Snake", "that was wrong, fix it" and "find me a horror book" to work from
the phone, away from the laptop (map `.scratch/alfred-builds/`, 2026-11-05). ADR 0067 already
gives Alfred a Claude session on the Alienware with an ask list and confirmation tokens; what was
missing was a way to read the conversation that went wrong, one controlled door out of the
laptop, a way back, and a guard against the laptop overheating under two builds.

adr.title: Alfred builds Alfred: one yes ships a change

chunks.heading: 74. Alfred builds Alfred: one yes ships a change > Decision
chunks.text:
- **The ship step** (ticket 03). `ship.py ask` rebases on origin/dev (a conflict stops it), runs
  the targeted tests (red stops it), and prints the question, adding "This also changes <X>"
  when the diff touches a locked safety clause, a CLAUDE.md ruling or ADR, auth or household
  isolation, the section 4 money gate, the recruiter demo or the worker's ask list (ruling 4).
  `ship.py run --token` ships exactly the branch head Kevin was asked about, in order: rebase,
  targeted tests plus the suites for what changed, merge and push dev then main, the engine
  deploy with the new revision's `/health` checked, `assembleFast` then release_apk.py
  (alfred-ota, ADR 0072's publisher; called, never reimplemented). One token, one ship, recorded
  in `work/ships.jsonl`.
- **Undo** (ticket 05). "Undo the last update" is the same question-and-yes: traffic back to the
  revision before the ship, a revert commit on dev and main, the previous phone ship rebuilt with
  a new versionCode (Android never downgrades), or the book removed.
- **The hook** (`asklist_hook.py`). `git push`, the deploy scripts, `release_apk.py` and `gcloud`
  are denied to every helper; only this folder's own `ship.py` / `undo.py`, run alone, pass.
  Kevin's private skills (`work/.claude`) are his files: a helper writing one asks. The worker's
  own files (tokens, config, ship history) are never a helper's to write.
- **Records** (ticket 02). `GET /api/device-logs/` and `/api/device-logs/<id>/render` give a
  household member (the worker's token) the same rendered conversation `manage.py device_logs
  --render` prints; mail stays redacted as stored; a recruiter visit's record has no household
  and is never readable.
- **One build at a time** (ticket 08). `build_lock.py`: an OS file lock, and a pause before each
  build step while laptopctl reports over 92 C, until under 80 C. No CPU cap (Kevin).
- **Books** (tickets 06, 07). A household library on the engine (`book_library`), EPUB only, with
  a required licence note and source. The book-finder skill adds only legal free copies
  (Standard Ebooks, Project Gutenberg, Wikisource, public-domain Internet Archive items, the
  author's own), never a pirate site; with none, it says where to borrow or buy.

adr.title: Alfred builds Alfred: one yes ships a change

chunks.heading: 74. Alfred builds Alfred: one yes ships a change > Consequences
chunks.text:
- The worker can now change production after one spoken yes. The guard is the question's
  content (the one line, the guarded-area line) and the tests; a wrong yes is undone by "undo".
- The hook matches commands by pattern. A helper that writes a script doing a push itself is not
  seen by it; the prompt rule ("never work around it") holds that, as ADR 0067 already accepts.
- Phone shipping needs alfred-ota merged (release_apk.py, versionCode from build time)
  and `ship.apk_bucket` in the worker config; until then `ship.py` refuses a phone ship in words.
- Book files live in Postgres like Claude task files; a bucket (the alfred-ota pattern) can
  replace that without changing any client, because downloads already go through signed links.
- Source: `.scratch/alfred-builds/map.md`, tickets 02 to 08.

adr.title: Memory lives on the engine, private to the member it is about

chunks.heading: 75. Memory lives on the engine, private to the member it is about > Standing
chunks.text:
ACCEPTED 2026-11-05. Engine half built on `feat/memory-vault-engine` (`.scratch/memory-and-vault/`
tickets 01-04, not deployed); the phone half is tickets 09-11. Amends 0052-a-row-may-be-private-to-one-member
(a new privacy-bearing table whose default is private) and **reverses the engine-mcp ruling of
2026-10-02** that no engine tool reads or writes memory (`server/engine_mcp/tools.py` module doc,
engine-mcp ticket 06 sub-question 2), for memory v2 only.

adr.title: Memory lives on the engine, private to the member it is about

chunks.heading: 75. Memory lives on the engine, private to the member it is about > Context
chunks.text:
Alfred's memory lived on the phone (`ai/AriaBrain.kt`, `ai/MemoryConsolidator.kt`). The engine held
a replica (`companion_memories`, `memories`) with no member column, and the engine's tools were
barred from it, so the web assistant said it had no memory and the Claude worker could not see
any. Kevin, 2026-11-05: *"alfred's memory should stay on a centralized place, like the engine no?
i thought we did memories that way"*, then *"yeah lets do it. centralized memory. and the id
vault"*.

adr.title: Memory lives on the engine, private to the member it is about

chunks.heading: 75. Memory lives on the engine, private to the member it is about > Decision
chunks.text:
- **One store on the engine**, `public.member_memories` (`server/member_memory/`). The phone, the
  web assistant and the Claude worker read and write it; the phone keeps a cache.
- **A memory is private to the member it is about.** A shared household fact (an address, a car)
  may be marked shared. ADR 0052's `owner_user` column and `household.tenancy.visible()` enforce
  it, with a check constraint that a memory is only ever private to the member it is about.
  Sharing is an explicit act; the consolidation job never shares.
- **Saving is automatic, visible and forgettable.** `manage.py consolidate_memories` distils
  finished conversation records. A Memory screen lists them (phone ticket 11). **"Forget that" or a
  swipe is a hard delete**, of the memory and every older version it superseded.
- **Consolidation reads only the person's own words**, plus the assistant's words from turns that
  called no tool. A turn that called a read-through tool is dropped whole. CLAUDE.md section 7
  holds by the shape of the extraction: mail never reaches the prompt.
- **A newer contradicting fact supersedes** the old one, which leaves recall but stays until the
  newer one is forgotten.
- **Recall is the phone's score on the engine** (recency + importance/10 + relevance, top 6,
  rehearsal), lexical, with two decay classes: `durable` 0.999/hour, `episodic` 0.99/hour (the
  first is an estimate). Embeddings are the next ticket; the test cluster has no pgvector.
- **Tools:** `recall_memory`, `list_memories`, `remember`, `forget_memory`, on `/mcp` and the web
  assistant. The three legacy tables stay out of the generic record tools.
- **Who:** members, and the Claude worker on the Alienware, which may read AND write (*"claude
  can write too."*). **Never a recruiter** (ADR 0068). **Never the work laptop:** each worker
  heartbeat binds its token to its machine, and memory refuses a token bound to a `listed`
  machine or a `claude-session-*` token bound to none.
- **Vault identifiers never become memories.** A deterministic filter refuses passport, NRIC,
  SSN, A-number and account-number shapes at every door (0076-the-id-vault).

adr.title: Memory lives on the engine, private to the member it is about

chunks.heading: 75. Memory lives on the engine, private to the member it is about > Consequences
chunks.text:
- **The work-laptop fence is convention, not proof.** The scope is what the worker reports and the
  token name is the installer's. A member's token copied to another machine is a member's token.
  ADR 0067's follow-up, worker endpoints on machine tokens, closes it.
- **The engine cannot tell where a `/mcp` write's words came from.** The phone refuses `remember`
  after a mail tool; the Alienware worker reads Kevin's Gmail (ADR 0067, 2026-11-04) and may now
  write memories. The only lever there is the worker's prompt (ticket 08 adds the rule).
- A hard delete leaves no tombstone, so a cache refreshes from the whole list.
- The filter refuses any nine-digit run, so a nine-digit insurance policy number is refused too.
- Head-unit conversation records are consolidated like the phone's; they are the same member.

adr.title: The ID vault: phone only, behind the fingerprint

chunks.heading: 76. The ID vault: phone only, behind the fingerprint > Standing
chunks.text:
ACCEPTED 2026-11-05. Engine half built on `feat/memory-vault-engine` (`.scratch/memory-and-vault/`
ticket 05, not deployed); the phone screen is ticket 12; web entry is ticket 15 (KIV).

adr.title: The ID vault: phone only, behind the fingerprint

chunks.heading: 76. The ID vault: phone only, behind the fingerprint > Context
chunks.text:
Some identifiers must be at hand and must never reach a model: a passport number at a counter, a
bank account number on a form. Memory (0075-memory-lives-on-the-engine) is read back to a
model on every recall, so they cannot live there. Kevin, 2026-11-05: *"centralized memory. and
the id vault"*; later the same day, *"can i enter it on the pc man, but later. not important
now"*.

adr.title: The ID vault: phone only, behind the fingerprint

chunks.heading: 76. The ID vault: phone only, behind the fingerprint > Decision
chunks.text:
- **What goes in:** passport, NRIC, SSN, A-number and bank account numbers. Plates, VINs and
  insurance policy numbers are ordinary data and stay out (the plate is a vehicle field).
- **Phone only, behind fingerprint. Never on the web, never readable by Claude, never spoken
  aloud, never sent to the AI model, never logged.**
- **Stored sealed** in `public.vault_items` with Fernet under `LEGION_VAULT_KEY`, the helper that
  seals Plaid tokens (`server/ingest/vault.py`). Each item is one member's; another member gets a
  404.
- **Write-only everywhere but the reveal.** List, create and update never answer with a value. A
  browser may list labels, create and update (ticket 15); it may never reveal or delete.
- **Reveal** (`POST /api/vault/items/<id>/reveal`) needs the member's device token and the header
  `X-Legion-Unlocked: biometric`, which the phone sets only after `BiometricPrompt` succeeds. Rate
  limited (10 an hour per member), audited in `public.vault_reveals` (label, time, device name,
  never the value), `Cache-Control: no-store`.
- **Refused on every route:** any token the engine ties to a Claude worker (a `claude-session-*`
  name or a machine binding), and recruiters.
- **No engine tool, no admin entry.** The phone's voice tool `show_vault_item(label)` opens the
  screen and returns only "opened on the phone".

adr.title: The ID vault: phone only, behind the fingerprint

chunks.heading: 76. The ID vault: phone only, behind the fingerprint > Consequences
chunks.text:
- **The server cannot verify a fingerprint.** The header is the phone's word. A member's device
  token that sends it gets the value, so the guarantee rests on the phone and on the token never
  leaving it. This is stated rather than implied.
- "Never readable by Claude" holds for the worker's tokens as installed. A member token copied by
  hand to a laptop is not recognised (same limit as ADR 0075's work-laptop fence).
- A value the person speaks aloud lands in the conversation record like any speech; the phone
  screen takes values typed, never dictated.
- The nightly backup holds ciphertext; losing `LEGION_VAULT_KEY` loses the vault.

chunks.heading: C1: System context
chunks.text:
**LEGION is one Django server over one Postgres, and everything else is a limb that talks to it over HTTPS JSON.** The server owns the schema, runs the CLAUDE.md §4 gate, holds auth and scopes every row to a household. The Android app is a device limb; a React web app served from the same server is the second limb. 0044-django-is-the-engine is the binding ruling and 0045-households-are-tenants is what "whose row is this" means. > **This page said the opposite until 2026-09-16.** It claimed "there is no LEGION server, no proxy, > no broker, no hosted key" and listed "no backend of any kind" as a deliberate absence. Two ADRs had > already killed that topology. The part that survived the rewrite is the *reason* the old sentence > existed: **nothing Kevin-hosted for strangers.** The household hosts its own engine. That is a > different claim from "there is no server", and conflating the two is what let this page rot. ```mermaid graph TB Kevin(["Household members
invite-only"]) subgraph Engine["The engine - the household hosts it"] Django["Django + DRF
schema, gate, auth, tenancy"] PG[("Postgres

subgraph Local["On the device, no network"] OBD["ELM327 dongle
