chunks.heading: C1: System context > The engine
chunks.text:
| Piece | Where | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| Project config | `server/legion/settings.py`, `server/legion/urls.py` | The Django project. Everything else is an app under it |
| Sync API | `server/api/synced.py`, `server/api/registry.py` | `SyncedModelViewSet`, the generic per-table read/write surface the phone syncs against |
| Events | `server/api/events.py` | Hand-written ahead of the generic viewset, and still its own code path |
| Checklists | `server/checklists/models.py` | The first tables Django owns end to end, with no legacy shape to honour |
| Identity and tenancy | `server/household/models.py`, `server/household/authentication.py`, `server/household/tenancy.py` | `Household`, `User`, `DeviceToken`, `Invite`; the token auth class; `TENANT_TABLES` |
| The §4 gate | `server/ingest/gate.py`, `server/ingest/views.py` | The reconciliation arithmetic in pure Python, behind `POST /api/ingest/statement` and `/api/ingest/receipt` |
| Scheduled jobs | `deploy/crontab`, `server/ingest/management/commands/` | The one schedule. Canvas polling, the Drive statements watcher, the Plaid sync, the nightly backup to Drive and Web Push dispatch, each a `manage.py` command. Compose's `worker` runs it under supercronic; `deploy/cloudrun/install_schedule.py` turns each line into a Cloud Scheduler entry |
| Bank feed | `server/ingest/plaid_client.py`, `server/ingest/plaid_sync.py`, `server/ingest/plaid_views.py` | Plaid link and sync. Rows land as `BANK_API`, ungated by ruling (0057-the-bank-feed-is-the-ledgers-truth) |
| Bought log | `server/purchases/` | The household's purchases, and the Groceries tick hook (0055-a-groceries-tick-is-a-purchase) |
| Web assistant | `server/assistant/` | The Gemini Live token mint, the session-authenticated tool door, each member's companion (0056-the-household-key-serves-the-web-assistant) |
| MCP server | `server/engine_mcp/` | The engine's tools at `/mcp`, with an audit table. Answers 404 in words until `LEGION_MCP` is on |
| Web Push | `server/push/` | Subscriptions, preferences and the dedupe ledger behind `manage.py push_dispatch` |
| Legacy mirrors | `server/legacy/models/` | `managed = False` models over the pre-existing `public` schema. Django does not migrate these |

chunks.heading: C1: System context > The engine
chunks.text:
| Web client | `server/frontend/`, `server/web/views.py` | React 19, Vite, TanStack Router and Query, built into the image and served at the site root by a catch-all view |

**Authentication is a device token per limb**, `Authorization: Token <key>`, hashed at rest and
revocable alone, so a lost phone is revoked without touching anyone else. Browser sessions are the
second accepted scheme, for the web client which has no such header.

**Tenancy is by household and nothing finer.** Every scoped read and write narrows on the request's
household in `SyncedModelViewSet`. Note what that is and is not: it is **one Python code path**, not
a database guarantee. 0045-households-are-tenants describes Postgres row-level security keyed on
a per-request session variable as the backstop under it; **that is not in the code**. A grep of
`server/` for `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`, `CREATE POLICY` or `set_config` returns nothing outside
Django's own vendored library. Treat the filter as the only thing standing between two households,
and the ADR's second layer as designed rather than built.

**It runs from one image.** `server/Dockerfile` builds the Vite bundle in a Node stage and the Django
app in a Python stage; `server/entrypoint.sh` migrates and then execs gunicorn on `${PORT:-8000}`.
The same image serves the household's own `deploy/docker-compose.yml` stack and a managed deployment.
Both an arm64 VM target and a Cloud Run target are wired, with Cloud Run named in the build comments
as the rollback of the two.

chunks.heading: C1: System context > What each boundary costs
chunks.text:
| System | How it authenticates | Offline behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| **The engine** (`backend/engine/EngineConfig.kt`) | Device token minted at `POST /api/auth/login`, stored encrypted | **Reads keep working** from the Room replica. Writes queue in the outbox and the app says so in words |
| **Gemini Live** (`service/GeminiLiveSession.kt`) | BYO key only. `service/LiveConnection.kt` resolves direct-or-nothing; no broker path exists | Hard fail, pre-flight checked. Says "NO SIGNAL OUT HERE" rather than hanging |
| **Gemini REST** (`ai/SubAgent.kt`) | Same key, `?key=` | Returns a typed result so callers distinguish offline from rate-limit from bad-key |
| **Drive appDataFolder** (`sync/DriveClient.kt`) | `drive.appdata` scope via `sync/DriveAuth.kt` | Opportunistic. A failed pass is just a failed pass |
| **Gmail** (`gmail/GmailClient.kt`) | `gmail.readonly` via `gmail/GmailAuth.kt` | Degrades with distinct spoken causes per failure kind |
| **Spotify** (`media/SpotifyController.kt`) | User's own client ID, redirect `com.kevin.legion://spotify-callback` | Needs the Spotify app installed and logged in with Premium. App Remote creates the active device, so playback works with Spotify closed - see c3-music |
| **Shelly Cloud** (`vehicle/ShellyCloudOpener.kt`) | `auth_key` query parameter | **No offline path.** See the caveat below |
| **Open-Meteo** (`weather/WeatherController.kt`) | None | Serves the last cached reading rather than failing |
| **NHTSA** (`vehicle/VinDecoder.kt`) | None | Feature simply unavailable |
| **OBD dongle** (`vehicle/ObdTransport.kt`, `vehicle/BleTransport.kt`) | Bluetooth pairing | Local radio. No dongle means the telemetry tools refuse rather than guess |

chunks.heading: C1: System context > Three things that are easy to get wrong
chunks.text:
**The phone has two backends, not one, and the switch is per aspect.**
`backend/engine/EngineTransport.kt` answers `SUPABASE` or `DJANGO` for each aspect name, and
`backend/engine/EngineBackends.kt` turns that answer into an object. All nine aspects now default to
Django **when the device has an engine address and a token**; with neither, every aspect falls back
to Supabase exactly as before. So "which server does this write go to" has no single answer at rest
- read the transport. c2-containers carries the detail.

**Calendar is not a REST integration, and is no longer a ContentProvider read either.** One-today
ticket 01 cut the live `CalendarContract` read and write entirely. Events are rows
(`data/local/Event.kt`, `engine/dates/DatesAgenda.kt`) that sync through the engine like any other
aspect. There is no Google Calendar scope and no network call to Google for it.

**The garage opener depends on a third-party cloud.** `vehicle/ShellyCloudOpener.kt` posts to Shelly's
servers. That does not violate the hosting rule (nobody here runs it) but it *is* the one feature with
a hard cloud dependency and no local fallback. A local BLE implementation exists at
`vehicle/ShellyBleOpener.kt`, fully written, and **is never instantiated** - it sits behind a seam
waiting for someone to wire it up.

chunks.heading: C1: System context > What deliberately does not exist
chunks.text:
Absences worth knowing, because each was a choice and each gets proposed again otherwise:

- **Nothing Kevin-hosted for strangers.** No Firestore, no broker, no proxy, no hosted key. A
  stranger clones, brings up their own stack and points their own build at it. That is
  0003-clone-and-run, and the engine did not weaken it: the engine is a thing the household runs,
  not a thing Kevin runs for them. One engine holding Kevin's parents is the household widened, not a
  customer (0045-households-are-tenants).
- **No Postgres row-level security**, despite 0045-households-are-tenants describing it. Said
  again here because an absence that an ADR implies is present is the dangerous kind.
- **One schedule, not a job framework.** `deploy/crontab` is a plain list of `manage.py` commands;
  there is no Celery or other task queue in `server/requirements.txt`. (This
  bullet said "no scheduled job, the crontab is empty" until 2026-10-14; the backend-etl map filled
  it.)
- **No object storage.** `MEDIA_ROOT` is a filesystem path with the default Django storage backend.
  `server/legion/settings.py` names this as an open gap, not a design.
- **No WorkManager, JobScheduler, or CoroutineWorker.** `androidx.work` is not a dependency.
  `AlarmManager` via `notes/AlarmScheduler.kt` is the only OS scheduler on the phone.
- **No embedding API call.** `data/local/CompanionMemory.kt` has `embeddingVector` and
  `embeddingModel` columns and nothing populates them. Memory recall in `ai/AriaBrain.kt` is lexical,
  written so one term can be swapped for cosine similarity later.
- **No FusedLocationProvider.** `location/LocationController.kt` uses raw `LocationManager` GPS and
  NETWORK providers. `play-services-location` is in the build only for geofencing
  (`location/GeofenceManager.kt`).
- **No comparative or anonymised fleet data**, ever.

chunks.heading: C1: System context > Related
chunks.text:
c2-containers for what runs inside the phone process and how a write reaches the engine.
adr-index for why the boundaries are where they are.

chunks.heading: C2: Containers
chunks.text:
A container here is a separately deployable or separately lifecycled runtime. Since 0044-django-is-the-engine there are containers on **both sides** of the HTTPS boundary, and this page used to describe only the phone's. ```mermaid graph TB subgraph Host["The household's own host"] Web["web
gunicorn + Django
serves API and the SPA"] Worker["worker
supercronic
runs deploy/crontab"] PG[("postgres
system of record")] Caddy["caddy
TLS front"] Caddy --> Web Web --> PG Worker --> PG end subgraph Browser["Browser"] SPA["React SPA / PWA
TanStack Router + Query"] end subgraph Phone["Android phone - ONE OS process"] MA["MainActivity
the NavHost, and HOME"] AFS["AriaForegroundService
the voice loop"] Svc["LegionMediaLibraryService
LegionConnectionService
MediaNotificationListener"] RX["Broadcast receivers"] Ctl["Controllers
object singletons"] Room[("Room replica
legion_database")] OB["Outboxes

com.kevin.midnightai

Its inside is not documented here.

chunks.heading: C2: Containers > Server-side containers
chunks.text:
From `deploy/docker-compose.yml`, all built from the one `server/Dockerfile`:

| Container | What it runs | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `web` | `server/entrypoint.sh` migrates, then gunicorn on `${PORT:-8000}` | Serves the JSON API **and** the built SPA at the site root |
| `worker` | supercronic over `deploy/crontab` | The one schedule: Canvas poll, Drive statements, Plaid sync, nightly backup, Web Push. On Cloud Run the same lines become Cloud Scheduler entries (`deploy/cloudrun/install_schedule.py`) |
| `postgres` | The system of record | Only Django writes it |
| `caddy` | TLS termination, per `deploy/Caddyfile` | |

The SPA is not a separate deployment. It is built into the image in a Node stage and served by a
catch-all Django view (`server/web/views.py`), which is why the browser limb has no container of its
own here.

chunks.heading: C2: Containers > The phone: still exactly one OS process
chunks.text:
**No component declares `android:process`**, so there is no IPC inside the app and no cross-process
state to reconcile. "Container" on this side means a long-lived Android component with its own
lifecycle.

| Container | Entry point | Why it exists separately |
|---|---|---|
| `MidnightApplication` | `MidnightApplication.kt` | Process entry. Owns `appScope`, a `SupervisorJob` on IO that lives as long as the process. Runs the one-time `data/MidnightImport.kt` |
| `MainActivity` | `ui/MainActivity.kt` | The app's one `NavHost`, routes as string constants in `ui/LegionRoute.kt`. Declares `CATEGORY_HOME`, so it is selectable as the phone's home app (0050-legion-may-be-the-home-app). Also hosts the Spotify OAuth token exchange, deliberately above the NavHost so a recomposition cannot lose it |
| `AssistActivity` | `ui/AssistActivity.kt` | A translucent Activity for `ASSIST` and `VOICE_COMMAND`, so the phone's assistant gesture starts a conversation. Shows over the lock screen and finishes itself |
| `MirrorSyncActivity` | `ui/mirror/MirrorSyncActivity.kt` | Not exported; reached only by `adb shell am start` until it folds into the NavHost |
| `AriaForegroundService` | `service/AriaForegroundService.kt` | The voice loop. Owns `LiveSessionController`, starts Vosk, runs the health, arrival, drive and recap monitors. Also holds the Spotify App Remote connection for its whole life, deliberately - see 0032-spotify-app-remote-spine |
| `LegionMediaLibraryService` | `car/LegionMediaLibraryService.kt` | Exported media3 stub. Android Auto binds it cross-process. Probe stage |
| `LegionConnectionService` | `car/LegionConnectionService.kt` | Exported Telecom self-managed ConnectionService. Probe stage |
| `MediaNotificationListener` | `service/MediaNotificationListener.kt` | Exists purely so the OS will hand over `MediaSessionManager`. Parses no notifications |
| `QuietTileService` | `quiet/QuietTileService.kt` | The Quick Settings tile for Quiet mode |

chunks.heading: C2: Containers > How a write reaches the engine
chunks.text:
This is the part 0044-django-is-the-engine rule 4 turns into a hard requirement, and it is built:
**the phone depends on the server to write, and never to read.**

1. A controller writes the local Room row first, so the UI updates at local-write speed.
2. The same call enqueues the server write. Per-aspect queues live in `backend/` (`EventsOutbox.kt`,
   `ChecklistsOutbox.kt`, `BodyOutbox.kt`, `MemoryOutbox.kt`, `LedgerConfigOutbox.kt`,
   `LastAspectsOutbox.kt`); the generic durable table behind that shape is
   `data/local/SyncOutbox.kt`, whose `sync_outbox` rows carry the target table, the operation, the
   local id and an opaque JSON payload.
3. A drain sends them. It is **at-least-once and bounded**: `attempts` and `lastError` are columns, a
   row that hits the cap is left in the table and excluded from the next drain rather than deleted or
   retried forever. There is no other durable record of a write that never landed, which is why it is
   never deleted.
4. Reads come from Room. With the engine unreachable the app still reads everything and says in words
   that it is behind.

**Realtime is a poll, not a socket** on the Django path: foreground, after every write, and on an
interval (`backend/engine/EnginePoll.kt`).

chunks.heading: C2: Containers > Two backends at once, per aspect
chunks.text:
`backend/engine/EngineTransport.kt` stores one transport per aspect name and answers `SUPABASE` or
`DJANGO`; `backend/engine/EngineBackends.kt` is the single place that answer becomes an object. All
nine aspects sit in `DJANGO_BY_DEFAULT`, but the default is **conditional on the device having an
engine address and a token** - without both, every aspect resolves to Supabase.

So the Supabase implementations are still compiled in and still reachable, and `supabase-kt` is still
declared in `app/build.gradle.kts`. 0044-django-is-the-engine says Supabase retires and it has
not finished retiring. Do not write "Supabase is gone" into a doc or a comment while
`SupabaseEventsBackend` and its siblings still exist
(`ls app/src/main/java/com/kevin/legion/backend/Supabase*Backend.kt`).

chunks.heading: C2: Containers > Coroutine scopes, and which ones never die
chunks.text:
This matters more than usual here, because there is still no DI container, and only a handful of
screens have a ViewModel to bound anything.

**Process-lifetime, never cancelled:**

- `MidnightApplication.kt` `appScope` - deliberately has no `CoroutineExceptionHandler`
- `sync/SyncEngine.kt` `engineScope` - its own doc says nothing cancels it
- `media/NowPlayingController.kt` `ioScope`
- `service/WakeWordEngine.kt` - on `Dispatchers.Default`, cancelled on `stop()`

**Session-scoped:** `service/GeminiLiveSession.kt` holds an IO scope and a `Main.immediate` scope.
`service/LiveSessionController.kt` runs on `Main.immediate`, which is why its `activeToolCalls`
counter can be a plain `Int` without a race.

**Real threads:** the mic loop (`AudioRecord`) and the playback path (`AudioTrack`) in
`service/GeminiLiveSession.kt`. The playback path carries an explicit lock added after a crash in
August 2026.

Each broadcast receiver spins its own IO scope inside `onReceive`. `ReminderAlarmReceiver` runs
whether or not the foreground service is alive, which is the point of it being a receiver.

chunks.heading: C2: Containers > The controller layer
chunks.text:
**Almost every controller is a Kotlin `object` singleton** - process-global, no DI, no ViewModel
between it and Compose. `LiveSessionController` is the long-standing exception, a `class`
instantiated exactly once by `AriaForegroundService`.

Counts belong where they are computed, not in this sentence:

```
grep -rc "^object [A-Za-z]*Controller" app/src/main/java/
```

That is unusual enough to state plainly: **state lives in top-level singletons and Room, and the UI
reads them directly.** If you are looking for the layer that mediates, there isn't one.

**CLAUDE.md §8 rules that this changes** - Hilt on KSP, constructor injection, a ViewModel per
screen. Step 1 of its migration order is done: Room's annotation processor is KSP and the kapt plugin
is gone from `app/build.gradle.kts`. Hilt is not: there is no `@HiltAndroidApp` and no `@Inject`.
A few screens (HOME, its calendar and Games, Lists, Money, Bought, navigation, the assistant chat)
have plain `ViewModel` or `AndroidViewModel` subclasses built by hand, without Hilt. Read the rule as the direction, and
this page as the state. To list them:

```
grep -rlE ": (Android)?ViewModel\(" app/src/main/java/
```

c3-ingestion for what is left of on-phone ingestion.

chunks.heading: C3: Data layer and controllers > Where the data actually lives
chunks.text:
**Postgres, behind Django, is the system of record** (0044-django-is-the-engine). Room is a
replica the phone reads from and a staging area it writes through. Every row belongs to exactly one
household (0045-households-are-tenants).

That inverts what this page used to say. The old text described Room plus `engine/RecordStore.kt` as
the storage endpoint, with no server anywhere in it.

chunks.heading: C3: Data layer and controllers > Room
chunks.text:
Declared in `data/local/CarDatabase.kt`. `exportSchema = true`, schema JSON committed under
`app/schemas/`, migration chain in `data/local/Migrations.kt`. No destructive fallback: the downgrade
path was removed 2026-08-12.

> **The version number is deliberately not written on this page.** CLAUDE.md §5: never quote a schema
> version from a document, including that one. This page said v25 at v34, v37 at v41, and v37 again
> while the code was far past it. The code is the only truth:
>
> ```
> sed -n '/version = /p' app/src/main/java/com/kevin/legion/data/local/CarDatabase.kt
> ```
>
> `CarDatabase.SCHEMA_VERSION` is a second hand-maintained copy that `DriveSyncScreen` reads to
> decide whether a backup may be restored. `CarDatabaseSchemaVersionTest` fails the build on drift
> between the two.

```

chunks.heading: C3: Data layer and controllers > Two storage shapes, both live
chunks.text:
This is the single most confusing thing about the data layer and it is a migration in progress, not
a muddle.

**Shape one, the generic aspect engine.** `aspects`/`record_types`/`field_defs` define what a record
TYPE looks like and `records` holds every record of every type as a JSON payload plus a typed
identity. `engine/RecordStore.kt` is the only writer of **that table**: reference integrity,
per-field delete policy, a 30-day trash and computed-field materialization live there and nowhere
else.

**Shape two, per-aspect typed tables.** `Checklist`/`ChecklistItem`/`ChecklistTick`, `Event`, and the
fleet replicas are ordinary typed Room tables with their own DAOs, written by their own controllers.
`checklists/ChecklistController.kt` writes `ChecklistDao` and never touches `RecordStore`.

0039-per-aspect-typed-tables supersedes 0037-the-aspect-engine-is-the-spine and makes shape
two the direction: once several clients write one Postgres, enforcement has to live where the
database can see it, and a jsonb payload caps foreign keys and CHECK constraints at whatever the
calling code remembers to do.

**So the old sentence "`RecordStore` is the only writer of records" is wrong twice over.** It is the
only writer of the engine's `records` table, which is now one shape of two; and the phone is not the
authority for any of it, because the server is. Say which table you mean.

Both shapes still have code and rows. Do not delete either on the strength of this page.

chunks.heading: C3: Data layer and controllers > Controllers
chunks.text:
Almost all are Kotlin `object` singletons. No DI container; most screens read them directly, and the
few with a hand-built ViewModel read them through it (c2-containers). Three are classes:
`LiveSessionController`, instantiated once by `AriaForegroundService`; `MapboxNavController`, the live
navigation trip; and `PurchasesController`, the bought log over the engine.
`engine/RecordStore.kt` is a second `class`, instantiated and threaded with a `CarDatabase` rather
than reaching for one, which is why it is not in this roster: it is storage, not a domain controller.

**Fleet** - `VehicleController` (the roster, labels, identity and VIN writes; the largest),
`VehicleSpecController`, `BuildSheetController`, `DailyDriveLogController`, `MonthlyRecapController`,
`YearlyWrappedController`, `FleetSpendController` (the fleet-to-ledger seam), `DtcClearController`,
`GarageController`, `WeatherController`, `LocationController`, `PlaceController`,
`ArrivalController`, `ReminderController`.

**Ledger** - `LedgerController`.

**Pantry and food** - `PantryController`, `GroceryController`, `MealController`,
`PurchasesController`.

**Body and goals** - `WorkoutController`, `SleepController`, `GoalController`.

**Checklists and notes** - `ChecklistController`, `TickHistoryController`, `NotesController`,
`OutstandingController`, `VoiceNoteController`.

**Media** - `MusicController`, `SpotifyController`, `NowPlayingController`, `VolumeController`.

**Navigation** - `MapboxNavController`.

**News** - `FeedSubscriptionController`.

**Books** - `BooksController` (the Books sheet and the `books` voice tool both call it; ADR 0061).

**Platform** - `LiveSessionController`, `TelephonyController`, `GlanceCardController`,
`VoiceModalController`, `GeneratedViewController`.

To recount rather than trust the roster above:

```
grep -rnE "^(internal )?(object|class) [A-Za-z]*Controller " app/src/main/java/
```

chunks.heading: C3: Data layer and controllers > Sync
chunks.text:
**The live path is the engine.** `backend/engine/` holds the per-aspect Django backends and
`backend/engine/EnginePoll.kt` the poll that stands in for a realtime socket. Writes go through the
per-aspect outboxes in `backend/` and the durable `sync_outbox` table
(`data/local/SyncOutbox.kt`); reads come from Room. c2-containers has the write path step by
step.

**`sync/` is a different, older thing and it is not that path.** `sync/SyncEngine.kt` is the
Drive-`appDataFolder` cross-device engine written for the head-unit era; its own KDoc still talks
about "the head unit and phone" converging. `sync/DatabaseSnapshot.kt` is whole-database backup and
restore into the same folder. Two merge modes are documented in it, `Mode.UNION` on `syncId` and
`Mode.LWW` on a natural key, and 0011-ledger-sync-union-and-lww records why the old
"sync must become append-only" blocker turned out to be false.

**Standing caveat, unchanged: `sync/` has never executed in LEGION.** Every claim about its behaviour
is traced from source; none is tested. It is not the sync path, and `appDataFolder` is not the store
- see the glossary entry, which used to say it was.

chunks.heading: C3: Ingestion and the gate
chunks.text:
**AMENDED 2026-08-29, backend-erp ticket 25 ("statement ingestion leaves the phone entirely").**
This doc used to cover two aspects ingesting documents on the phone - ledger (bank statements) and
pantry (photographed grocery receipts). Kevin ruled the phone never ingests a bank statement any
more: *"kill ledger ingestion from phone. just keep pantry."* A statement PDF is already on the
laptop; a receipt needs a camera the laptop does not have. Only **pantry** ingests on the phone now.

The rule is still 0006-reconciliation-gate. Everything below is that rule made concrete for the
one aspect left that runs it on-device.

chunks.heading: C3: Ingestion and the gate > What used to be here, and where it went
chunks.text:
the old folder scanner, the five statement parsers plus `StatementDispatcher`,
the LLM statement fallback, `LedgerFolderPreferences`, `LedgerIngestService`, and
`ledger/IngestPipeline.kt`'s `stage`/`commit` machinery are all deleted. Bank statements are
ingested off the phone now. CLAUDE.md §4's amendments are the source of truth for that side; this
doc no longer diagrams it because there is nothing left on the phone to draw. In one paragraph, as
of 2026-10-14:

- **Statements** are dropped in the household's Drive statements folder and read on a schedule by
  `manage.py drive_statements` (`server/ingest/statements.py`). A Python parser runs first where one
  exists (`server/ingest/parsers/`); otherwise Gemini on the household's own key emits LEGION's
  statement CSV, which must meet three anchors. Bank of America files are now skipped as retired.
  (This paragraph used to say the user's own LLM masked a CSV before upload. That ruling was
  replaced on 2026-09-27; raw documents reach the server.)
- **A linked bank's own feed** (Plaid, `server/ingest/plaid_sync.py`) is the ledger's truth for the
  accounts it covers, stored as `BANK_API` with no gate, by ruling
  (0057-the-bank-feed-is-the-ledgers-truth). It is the one exception to everything below.

**The gate now runs in Python, not in plpgsql.** This paragraph used to say statements were committed
against `public.commit_statement`, a Postgres RPC implementing the same rules in SQL. Since
0044-django-is-the-engine rule 2 ("the gate moves language, not posture") the arithmetic lives in
`server/ingest/gate.py` - deliberately pure functions with no ORM and no Django imports - behind
`POST /api/ingest/statement` and `POST /api/ingest/receipt` in `server/ingest/views.py`. The rules
below are unchanged; only the language they are written in moved. The RPC name still appears in
Kotlin KDoc as history, so finding it in a comment is not evidence it is still the path.

`ledger/IngestPipeline.kt` still exists as a single shared utility (`sha256`), because pantry's own
receipt hashing happens to want the exact same primitive - see that file's own doc comment.

chunks.heading: C3: Ingestion and the gate > The gate, stated exactly (still binding, pantry included)
chunks.text:
1. **Deterministic first** where a deterministic path exists. Pantry has none - a receipt is
   photographed, not born-digital - so LLM vision is primary there by necessity.
2. **Rows must reconcile against the document's own stated total, exactly.** Not within a tolerance.
   Sum equals printed total, or the whole document quarantines. Nothing partial is ever written.
3. **Money is `Long` cents.** 0007-money-as-long-cents. The equality in rule 2 is why.
4. **Every row is tagged** `DETERMINISTIC` or `LLM_RECONCILED` (or `UNRECONCILED` under rule 7;
   `BANK_API` is the ruled exception above, not a gate outcome).
5. **Anything the document does not state is an estimate**, excluded from the check and labelled.
   0008-estimates-are-not-facts.
6. **A check that passes when nothing parsed is not a gate.** Inside a recognised section, every
   line that is not the section's own total must parse, or the document quarantines.
7. **A source with no anchor may be stored provisionally, never as fact.**
   0009-provisional-unreconciled-tier. (Pantry has never needed this rule - a receipt not
   printing a subtotal still prints a total; ledger's mid-cycle card CSV was the only source that
   needed it, and it left with the rest of ledger ingestion.)
8. **Persist the anchors, not just the verdict.** A gate that discards its own inputs leaves rows
   nobody can ever re-verify. The numbers the gate checked against are stored in their own columns
   beside the rows they gated; an anchor the source never stated is stored NULL and recorded as
   absent, never synthesised from `sum(lines)` - which would make the check an identity, rule 6's
   shape again. CLAUDE.md §4 rule 8. **This rule was missing from this page** while the two cases
   that produced it were already on record: three pantry receipts whose legacy table kept only
   `totalCents`, and the ledger's entire verified history, whose stated total and balances were read
   inside a parser and never written down.

chunks.heading: C3: Ingestion and the gate > The gate, stated exactly (still binding, pantry included)
chunks.text:
Rule 6 was learned the hard way, on the ledger side that is now gone: BofA's card statement printed
interest rows in a different shape, all four silently failed to match, and the section check
reconciled zero parsed rows against a printed $0.00 and passed. It held only because interest
happened to be zero that month. The rule survives here because pantry's own line-item sum is
exactly the same shape of check, and the same blind spot is possible in principle.

chunks.heading: C3: Ingestion and the gate > Pantry
chunks.text:
Pantry has **no deterministic path at all**. Receipts are photographed, not born-digital, so there
is no layout to recognise. `pantry/PantryReceiptAgent.kt` runs LLM vision as the primary and only
extractor, via `ai/SubAgent.kt`'s inline image part.

That is a necessity, not a preference, and the gate still applies unchanged: line items must sum to
the receipt's printed total or the receipt quarantines.

The macros are the interesting part. Calories, protein, carbs and fat are model guesses from a
product name. **A receipt has never printed any of them**, so they cannot be gated even in
principle. They are excluded from the check, labelled estimates in the tool description and in every
string, and since 2026-08-02 they are physically segregated into a block headed `ESTIMATED, NOT ON
THE RECEIPT`.

chunks.heading: C3: Ingestion and the gate > Adding a new ingestion path
chunks.text:
The feature checklist in CLAUDE.md §7 is binding. In short: wire the gate, quarantine on mismatch,
tag provenance, use `Long` cents, label anything the source did not state, and make sure your check
cannot pass on an empty extraction.

If your source states no anchor at all, you are in 0009-provisional-unreconciled-tier territory
and all four of its conditions apply together.

**Remember the phone-only scope, though:** if the new source is a document rather than a photo -
anything that could equally well sit on a laptop - the phone is very likely the wrong place for it
per Kevin's ruling above. Ask before building a second phone-side document importer.

chunks.heading: C3: Ingestion and the gate > Related
chunks.text:
c2-containers for the container map (`LedgerIngestService` is gone from it). adr-index for
the full decision set.

chunks.heading: C3: The music path
chunks.text:
How a spoken music request becomes sound. Built across `.scratch/spotify-voice/` (ten tickets, 2026-08-19). **On-device since 2026-08-22**: that map's ship-pass ticket 12 closed with Kevin's "verified on a real drive - all Spotify functions work". (This page said "nothing is on-device yet" until 2026-10-14.) Since then `play_music` refuses a search hit that does not match the request and names the closest hits instead of falling back to popularity (`media/SpotifyMatch.kt`). ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant T as LiveToolbox participant W as SpotifyWebApi participant S as SpotifyController
(App Remote) participant M as MusicController
(MediaSession) participant N as NowPlayingController T->>W: play_music("name") Note over W: own library first:
his playlists, saved albums,
THEN the catalogue W-->>T: URI + what was actually picked T->>S: play(uri) Note over S: App Remote CREATES the
active device - works with
Spotify closed S-->>N: pushed PlayerState N->>N: history row WITH uri
(replayable) Note over T,M: no Spotify set up?
control_music transport falls
back to plain MediaSession ```

chunks.heading: C3: The music path > Division of labour
chunks.text:
| Piece | Role |
|---|---|
| `media/SpotifyWebApi.kt` | Resolves names into URIs. Search order is the driver's OWN library (playlists, saved albums) before the public catalogue - "play my gym mix" must never land on a stranger's playlist. Also the library writes: like, follow, add-to-playlist |
| `media/SpotifyController.kt` | App Remote. The only thing that makes sound come out, and the only route that creates an active device. Connection held in `AriaForegroundService`, see 0032-spotify-app-remote-spine |
| `media/MusicController.kt` | Generic MediaSession transport. The zero-setup fallback: pause/skip works on whatever is playing, Spotify or not, once notification access is granted |
| `media/NowPlayingController.kt` | Observes playback, writes `MusicPlayHistoryEntry`. Since ticket 09 the row carries the Spotify URI when App Remote agrees, so `legion_history` can replay what it saw, not just name it |
| `media/VolumeController.kt` | Stream volume, no Spotify involvement |

chunks.heading: C3: The music path > The tool surface
chunks.text:
Five voice tools: `play_music` (by name, says what it actually picked), `control_music` (20
actions: transport, queue, like/unlike, follow/unfollow artist, shuffle/repeat, seek/restart,
add-to-playlist, more-from-this-artist), `get_music_queue`, `browse_my_music`, `control_volume`.
None sit behind a dispatcher - a driver mid-song does not want a sub-agent round-trip.

Every tool obeys the outcome-verb rule (0031-speech-honesty-clause): a play that did not
happen is reported as not having happened.

chunks.heading: C3: The music path > The structural fact that shapes everything
chunks.text:
**LEGION holds no Spotify playback scopes.** The Web API cannot start, stop, or transfer playback
anywhere. Everything audible goes through App Remote's app-to-app binding on THIS phone: no seeing
what plays on another device, no transferring playback to the car. That is a designed boundary,
not a gap - see the spotify-voice map's traced table.

chunks.heading: C3: The music path > What is deliberately absent
chunks.text:
- **Podcasts and audiobooks.** Out by decision, which also avoids the unverified question of
  whether App Remote plays episode URIs at all.
- **Creating playlists by voice.** Adding to one is in; creating one at speed is a thing done twice.
- **Spotify's discovery endpoints.** Dead for post-2024 client IDs; see
  0034-own-recommendation-engine.
- **MusicRouter / MusicSource / mixtapes.** Retired in the 2026-07-31 pivot; callers check
  `SpotifyController.isConnected` directly.

chunks.heading: C3: The music path > Two numbers nobody has measured
chunks.text:
The playlist fuzzy-match threshold (0.6) and its cache TTL (15 min) were tuned against unit tests,
never against a spoken transcript. Treat both as provisional.

chunks.heading: C3: The music path > Related
chunks.text:
c2-containers for the service that holds the App Remote connection. c3-voice-loop for how
the tool call arrives. 0033-byo-spotify-client-id for why setup requires the driver's own
Spotify dev app.

chunks.heading: C3: The voice loop
chunks.text:
One utterance, end to end. This is the most tangled path in the app and the one most worth having a picture of. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant U as User participant W as WakeWordEngine participant C as LiveSessionController participant G as GeminiLiveSession participant T as LiveToolbox participant S as SubAgent U->>W: "hey " Note over W: Vosk, on-device,
grammar built from the profile name W->>C: ACTION_TALK via startForegroundService Note over C: gates: in a call?
has a key? online? C->>G: newSession() Note over C,G: systemInstruction from AriaBrain
tools from LiveToolbox.declarations()
voice from CompanionProfile G->>G: open WSS, stream mic PCM Note over G: turn ends on the phone (Silero + Smart Turn,
extend-only, ADR 0064) or server VAD G-->>C: LiveEvent.ToolCall C->>T: dispatch(name, args) alt direct tool T-->>C: result else dispatcher tool T->>S: investigate(), bounded loop Note over S: max 4 model calls,
30s budget, REST S->>T: agent tool calls replay through
the same dispatch() S-->>T: text T-->>C: text end C->>G: sendToolResponse() Note over C,G: writes BLOCK; a named read-only lookup is
NON_BLOCKING, result sent WHEN_IDLE (ADR 0065) G-->>U: speech via AudioTrack ```

chunks.heading: C3: The voice loop > Where each named piece actually sits
chunks.text:
The names are not self-explanatory and several are not where you would guess.

| Piece | Role | Not in the turn loop? |
|---|---|---|
| `service/WakeWordEngine.kt` | Vosk, on-device, opt-in. Grammar is `"hey <name>"` built from the active companion profile | Entry only |
| `service/LiveSessionController.kt` | **The conversation state machine and sole socket owner.** Three doors in: prewarm, start conversation, start proactive, all funnelled through one `newSession()` | Core |
| `service/GeminiLiveSession.kt` | The WebSocket, the mic loop, the playback path. Emits `LiveEvent`s | Core |
| `service/turn/TurnTaker.kt` | Local end of turn and barge-in (ADR 0064): Silero over each mic buffer, `EndOfTurnPolicy` for activityStart/activityEnd, `BargeInGate` while Alfred speaks, Smart Turn checks on one shared thread | Core, inside the session's mic loop |
| `service/LiveToolbox.kt` | Every tool declaration and the single `dispatch()` entry | Core |
| `service/EngineToolbox.kt` | The nine aspect-engine meta-tools (generic record CRUD over `RecordStore`) plus the Flash clerk and the Pro schema generator. Declarations folded into `LiveToolbox.declarations()`, dispatch tried first in `LiveToolbox.dispatch()` before the per-domain tools | Core, but merged in rather than standalone |
| `ai/SubAgent.kt` | Bounded investigate loop over Gemini REST. Its tool calls replay through the *same* `dispatch()` | Core |
| `ai/AriaBrain.kt` | **A context supplier, not a turn participant.** Called once per socket for the system instruction and the greeting context. Also backs the `remember` tool and memory recall | Yes, outside |
| `service/Phase.kt` | `IDLE / CONNECTING / LISTENING / THINKING / SPEAKING`. Set through one method that writes status *before* phase, deliberately, then mirrors to `service/CompanionPhase.kt` so the Activity draws what the service drew | Cross-cutting |
| `service/ProactiveBus.kt` | The unsolicited-speech ingress. Collected in exactly one place, `AriaForegroundService` | Separate ingress |

chunks.heading: C3: The voice loop > Two constraints that bite
chunks.text:
**The mic is exclusive.** `WakeWordEngine` is now the only background listener - `AmbientListener`
was retired 2026-08-21 (`.scratch/proactive-mode/issues/12-retire-ambient-listening.md`), taking the
mutual guard with it. The constraint has not gone away: if you add a second listener, this is where
it breaks, and the retired pair is the worked example of what guarding it looks like.

**Sub-agent tools recurse through the same dispatcher.** `LiveToolbox.dispatch()` is called by the
live session *and* by every sub-agent tool call. It has to be safe to re-enter. Five dispatcher
tools exist: fleet, body, goals, pantry, mail. Each hands a domain-specific grounding prompt and a
filtered tool set to `SubAgent`. Not every `ask_*` tool is one of these five: `ask_engine` sends the
question to the engine's `/mcp` endpoint instead (`backend/engine/EngineMcpClient.kt`), and
`ask_maintenance` and `ask_advisor` have their own handlers.

chunks.heading: C3: The voice loop > Where a spoken write lands
chunks.text:
The loop above ends at speech, which makes it easy to miss that a tool call is often a **write**, and
that the phone is not the authority for it. A tool calls the same controller the hands path calls
(ADR 0035), the controller writes Room so the UI moves at local-write speed, and the server write
goes on an outbox to be drained. c2-containers has the steps and the retry cap.

Two consequences for anything added to `service/LiveToolbox.kt`:

- **A tool that reports success must have a result to stand on.** CLAUDE.md §7's outcome-verb rule is
  conditioned on the tool RESULT, and "queued to the outbox" is not "sent". A tool whose write is
  still in the queue says so.
- **Every voice tool needs a hands path to the same capability**, calling the same controller, not a
  second implementation (0035-every-voice-capability-has-a-hands-path).

chunks.heading: C3: The voice loop > Known stale comment
chunks.text:
`service/AriaForegroundService.kt` carries a KDoc saying *"There's no wake word (the old offline
'Hey Moose' engine shipped arm64-only native libs...)"*. That comment is wrong. `WakeWordEngine` is
wired and started by that same class, and Vosk is a live dependency. The comment is stale by at
least one feature generation. Left in place rather than fixed here, because this document is not
allowed to silently edit code it is describing. Worth a cleanup commit.

chunks.heading: C3: The voice loop > Related
chunks.text:
c2-containers for the service that hosts this. 0018-pull-based-tools for why the model gets
tools rather than pre-injected context.

chunks.heading: Cutover 1: Notes and Places become engine-native
chunks.text:
Owed by `.scratch/aspect-engine/issues/22-cutover-per-aspect.md` ("Cutover per aspect: the engine
becomes the read and write path"). This is the checklist a reviewer verifies branch
`feat/cutover1-notes-places` against - written before this doc's own author claims the branch is
done, per CLAUDE.md §8's L11 ("a ticket's own verification steps are gates, not notes").

**The reconciliation-gate/money rules (CLAUDE.md §4) do not apply to this wave** - every row here
is `RecordProvenance.USER` (hand/voice-entered), never document-extracted, same reasoning
`docs/architecture/wave1-carve-2026-08-23.md` already gives for the copier itself.

chunks.heading: Cutover 1: Notes and Places become engine-native > What "cutover" means here, precisely
chunks.text:
Before this branch: the engine held a COPY of every `ListItem`/`TaggedPlace` (wave 1), but nothing
read or wrote it - `NotesController`/`PlaceController` were still 100% legacy-table-backed, and the
engine copy was write-once, dead weight.

After this branch: `NotesController`/`PlaceController` are internally engine-backed (every read and
write goes through `RecordStore` against the Notes/Places aspects), and every caller - screens,
voice tools, digests, the recurrence engine, the goal-checklist sweep - keeps calling the SAME
public functions on those two objects, unchanged (ADR 0035: "the controller keeps its seam"). The
legacy `list_items`/`item_lists`/`places` tables are **frozen for new content** - every value a user
sees or acts on from this branch forward was written through the engine, never the legacy DAO.

chunks.heading: Cutover 1: Notes and Places become engine-native > Senior review, 2026-08-24: one blocking finding, three should-fixes (all taken)
chunks.text:
**BLOCKING - `sync/SyncEngine.kt`'s raw-SQL `places` registration.** The original reader/writer
sweep below grepped only DAO-shaped calls (`listItemDao()\.`/`itemListDao()\.`/`placeDao()\.`/
`listItemSkipDao()\.`) and missed `SyncEngine.REGISTRY`'s `Spec("places", ...)` entirely - it merges
Drive snapshots into the legacy `places` table via raw `execSQL`, not through `PlaceDao` at all, so
it was invisible to that grep by construction. **Methodology fix, applied and re-swept**: added a
raw-table-name grep (`"list_items"|"item_lists"|"list_item_skips"|"places"` as bare string literals,
not just DAO method calls) across `app/src/main/java/com/kevin/legion` - result: `list_items`/
`item_lists`/`list_item_skips` are registered nowhere outside their own entity/DAO files (confirmed
clean); `places` had exactly the one real hit, `SyncEngine.REGISTRY` (plus an inert, asset-less
historical importer, `data/MidnightImport.kt`'s own `TableSpec("places", ...)` - see its own note
below). **Fix, per ticket 13's already-decided answer** ("the appDataFolder SyncEngine retires for
record data"): the `places` `Spec` is removed from `REGISTRY` entirely - not narrowed, not
re-filtered, gone - and `SyncEngine.kt`'s own class doc now states in words that cross-device place
sync rides the engine mirror channel (`engine/mirror/MirrorSync.kt`) exactly like every other engine
record, plus the transition consequence: **a peer phone still on a pre-cutover build keeps syncing
`places` through the OLD registry entry to itself only** - a real, known dead window (not a data-loss
risk; nothing here deletes what a peer already has) that closes the moment both of Kevin's phones run
a cutover-or-later build. Full reasoning lives in `SyncEngine.kt`'s own class doc comment now,
not duplicated here.

chunks.heading: Cutover 1: Notes and Places become engine-native > Senior review, 2026-08-24: one blocking finding, three should-fixes (all taken)
chunks.text:
**A second raw-SQL hit, noted rather than fixed - out of this blocking finding's scope.**
`data/MidnightImport.kt`'s `SPECS` list also names `TableSpec("places", listOf("label"), naturalPk =
true)` - a one-time, guarded-to-run-at-most-once historical importer of Kevin's actual Midnight AI
fleet history, reading from `assets/midnight_import/` (a directory that does not exist in this repo
- the import is presently inert on every real build, nothing to decode). It writes raw
`INSERT OR IGNORE` SQL straight into the legacy `places` table, bypassing `RecordStore`/
`PlaceController` entirely, and would resurrect a dead-table writer if that asset bundle were ever
added back. Left alone here because (a) it is unreachable today (no asset), (b) it is explicitly a
one-shot PRE-LEGION migration path, not an ongoing sync/record-write surface, and (c) the reviewer's
blocking finding named `SyncEngine` specifically. Stated in words rather than silently left for a
future sweep to rediscover.

**SHOULD-FIX 1 - skip-rekey misdirection, fixed.** `EngineDataMigrationWave1.rekeySkipsToEngineIds`
now checks whether `skip.itemId` already resolves to a LIVE Notes-aspect `EngineRecord` FIRST,
unconditionally, before ever touching the legacy `list_items` table - closing the real
misdirection risk where an already-correct, post-cutover, engine-keyed skip could numerically
collide with an UNRELATED legacy `list_items` id (two independent `AUTOINCREMENT` sequences have no
reason to disagree) and get silently rekeyed onto the wrong item. New test:
`EngineDataMigrationWave1CutoverTest`'s `an already-correct engine-keyed skip is never misdirected by
an id-space collision with an unrelated legacy row` forces the exact collision (a real Notes engine
record at id 1, an unrelated legacy `list_items` row whose own independent AUTOINCREMENT sequence
also starts at 1) and asserts the skip is left completely untouched.

chunks.heading: Cutover 1: Notes and Places become engine-native > Senior review, 2026-08-24: one blocking finding, three should-fixes (all taken)
chunks.text:
**SHOULD-FIX 2 - orphaned skips, logged.** `MidnightEvents.skipRekeyOrphaned(skipId, legacyItemId,
reason)` (new) fires whenever the rekey pass cannot find a live target for a skip row (no legacy
item, or no matching engine record) - the row is still left un-rekeyed exactly as before (the same
accepted cost `EngineDataMigrationWave1`'s own doc comment already named), but now it is
`Log.w`-visible so the owed on-device run can actually observe whether this fires for real data
rather than only in a unit-test fixture.

**SHOULD-FIX 3 - outcome-verb honesty across the bridge, fixed.** `NotesController.tick`/`untick`/
`removeItem`/`renameItem`/`moveItem`/`clearTime`/`setExactDowngraded`/`markMissed`/`markLogged` now
return a real `Boolean` (`true` only on a genuine `RecordStore.WriteResult.Success`/
`DeleteResult.Trashed` - never unconditionally `true` the way most of them did before this fix);
`setTime`/`setPlaceTrigger`/`setRepeat`/`setExact` now return `ListItem?`, null on a failed write
rather than silently handing back a stale item that looks unchanged-but-successful.
`PlaceController.tagPlace`/`forgetPlace` now check the real `WriteResult`/`DeleteResult` before ever
speaking an ack, and `forget` returns `Boolean`. Every call site that chains these return values
(`LiveToolbox.dispatchItemAction`/`scheduleItem`, `ui/notes/ListDetailScreen.kt`'s save handler) was
updated to bail out with a worded failure rather than silently continuing on a stale/null item - see
those files' own `should-fix 3` comments. New/updated tests: `NotesControllerTest`'s `setTime returns
null rather than a stale item when the record does not exist`, `removeItem returns false for an
already-removed item, never a false success`, `tick returns false for an already-removed item, never
a false success`; `PlaceControllerTest`'s `forget returns true on a real delete and false for an
unknown label, never a false success`.

chunks.heading: Cutover 1: Notes and Places become engine-native > The reader/writer ruling table
chunks.text:
Grep-proven (`listItemDao()\.|itemListDao()\.|placeDao()\.|listItemSkipDao()\.` PLUS a raw-table-name
sweep - `"list_items"|"item_lists"|"list_item_skips"|"places"` as bare string literals, added
2026-08-24 after the SyncEngine finding above - across `app/src/main/java/com/kevin/legion`) at the
end of this branch. Every match, ruled:

chunks.heading: Cutover 1: Notes and Places become engine-native > The reader/writer ruling table > `list_items`
chunks.text:
| File | Call | Ruling | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `notes/NotesController.kt` | (removed - was ~20 calls) | **rewired-to-engine** | Every read/write now goes through `RecordStore` against the Notes `Item` record type. See "The bridge" below. |
| `engine/migration/EngineDataMigrationWave1.kt` `copyNotesIfNeeded` | `db.listItemDao().allActive()` | **stays** (read-only, one-time copier) | This IS the migration - it must read the legacy table to copy from it. Not a live path; runs once per row (guid-guarded), and again once at cutover catch-up (see below). |
| `engine/migration/EngineDataMigrationWave1.kt` `rekeySkipsToEngineIds` | `db.listItemDao().getById(skip.itemId)` | **stays** (read-only, one-time rekey) | Reads a legacy item's `syncId` to find its matching engine record - the rekey pass, not a live path. |
| `notes/AlarmScheduler.kt`, `service/ReminderAlarmReceiver.kt`, `service/ReminderActionReceiver.kt`, advisor/GoalChecklistSync.kt (deleted 2026-09-10, one-home ticket 05 - the advisor writes a recurring `checklists` row through `advisor/AdvisorChecklistMigration.kt` now), `advisor/digest/*.kt`, ui/TodayScreen.kt (deleted 2026-09-01, one-today ticket 07), `location/ReminderController.kt` | (all previously present) | **rewired-to-engine** | Every one of these now calls `NotesController`'s engine-backed functions instead - see the per-file list below. |

**Result: `list_items` has ZERO writers after this branch.** `NotesController.addItem`/`tick`/
`untick`/`setTime`/`setPlaceTrigger`/`setRepeat`/`setExact`/`setExactDowngraded`/`markMissed`/
`markLogged`/`removeItem`/`renameItem`/`moveItem`/`dismissMissed` all write through `RecordStore`
now, never `ListItemDao`. Its only remaining callers are the migration/rekey code, which reads it
(never writes it) for the sole purpose of copying rows OUT of it.

chunks.heading: Cutover 1: Notes and Places become engine-native > The reader/writer ruling table > `item_lists`
chunks.text:
| File | Call | Ruling | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `notes/NotesController.kt` `theList` | `db.itemListDao().getAll(includeArchived = true)` | **stays, read-only** | `ItemList` was never migrated onto the engine (wave 1 carve: "dies... every list VERB is already dead code"). `theList()` still reads the legacy row once, so an existing install's list NAME is unchanged, but it no longer inserts a fallback row or calls `touch()` on every mutation - both writes are gone. A fresh install with no legacy row gets an in-memory placeholder (`ItemList(id = 1L, ...)`) instead. |

**Result: `item_lists` has ZERO writers after this branch**, one read-only caller.

chunks.heading: Cutover 1: Notes and Places become engine-native > The reader/writer ruling table > `list_item_skips`
chunks.text:
**Deliberately NOT frozen.** Per `wave1-carve-2026-08-23.md`, `ListItemSkip` "stays plugin-internal
- not migrated" - it is recurrence-engine implementation state, the same category as OBD session
config, never a user-facing record type. It keeps being the live store for per-occurrence skips;
what changed is which id space `ListItemSkip.itemId` points into.

| File | Call | Ruling | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `notes/NotesController.kt` `skipOccurrence`/`skippedDates`/`scheduleAlarmFor` | insert/read | **stays, now keyed by engine record id** | `itemId` now stores the item's `EngineRecord.id`, not a legacy `list_items.id` - `ListItemSkip` itself needed no schema change (it was always "whatever id the active item store assigns"; cutover just changes which store that is). |
| `notes/AlarmScheduler.kt` `rescheduleAll`, `service/ReminderAlarmReceiver.kt` `rearmNextOccurrence` | `skippedDatesForItem(item.id)` | **stays, same table** | `item.id` here is now an engine record id (the `ListItem` value object `NotesController` hands back carries the engine id in its own `.id` field), so these reads automatically follow the rekey. |
| `engine/migration/EngineDataMigrationWave1.kt` `rekeySkipsToEngineIds` | read every row, `rekeyItemId` | **new, one-time** | Walks every pre-cutover skip row and re-points `itemId` at the matching engine record's id - see "Catch-up design" below. |

chunks.text:
| File | Call | Ruling | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `location/PlaceController.kt` | (removed - was 4 calls) | **rewired-to-engine** | `tagPlace`/`forgetPlace`/`forget`/`all`/`currentLabel` all go through `RecordStore` against the Places `Place` record type now. Also **closes a known v1 gap** wave 1 flagged but did not fix: `tagPlace` now looks up any existing record with the same label and updates it in place, reproducing `TaggedPlace.label`'s old `@PrimaryKey`/`REPLACE` upsert behaviour by hand (`RecordStore` has no column-level uniqueness). |

| `data/MidnightImport.kt` `SPECS` | `TableSpec("places", listOf("label"), naturalPk = true)` | **noted, not fixed - out of this branch's scope** | Raw-SQL, one-time, guarded-to-run-once historical importer; presently inert (no `assets/midnight_import/` bundle ships). See "Senior review, 2026-08-24" above. |

**Result: `places` has ZERO writers after this branch** - `PlaceController` internally, and (as of the
senior review fix) `SyncEngine.REGISTRY` too.

chunks.heading: Cutover 1: Notes and Places become engine-native > What died
chunks.text:
Nothing was deleted in this pass. See "A genuine fork, surfaced rather than built" below for why
`tag_place`/`forget_place`/`read_list`/`manage_item` - the four LiveToolbox tools the tool-inventory
marks "dies into meta-tools (eventually)" - were deliberately NOT deleted here, contrary to a literal
reading of the dispatching brief's point 5.

chunks.heading: Cutover 1: Notes and Places become engine-native > The bridge: how the controller keeps its seam
chunks.text:
Every public `NotesController`/`PlaceController` function keeps its exact pre-cutover signature and
return type (`ListItem`/`TaggedPlace`), so every caller flips with zero changes of its own. What
changed is entirely internal:

- `NotesController` resolves the Notes aspect schema (`NotesAspectSeeder.ensureSeeded`), converts
  every `EngineRecord` it reads into an in-memory `ListItem` (`toListItem`, reusing
  `wave1-carve-2026-08-23.md`'s exact field mapping - not a second mapping), and writes through
  `RecordStore.create`/`update`/`delete`.
- `PlaceController` does the same against the Places aspect (`PlacesAspectSeeder`), converting to
  `TaggedPlace`.
- **`loggedAt` needed a new home.** Wave 1 deliberately did not carry `ListItem.loggedAt` onto the
  engine (it was GoalChecklistSync's own sweep bookkeeping, not user content; that class was deleted 2026-09-10) - true only as long
  as the legacy table stayed live. This branch adds `FIELD_LOGGED_AT` to the SAME Notes `Item`
  record type (`NotesAspectSeeder`) - a new `FieldDef` row, not a Room migration, exactly the
  benefit the engine is designed to provide. `NotesAspectSeederTest` updated from 20 to 21 fields.
- **`ListItem.listId` is now cosmetic.** `ItemList` was never migrated (see above); every converted
  `ListItem` carries `listId = theList(context).id`, so every caller that ever compared
  `item.listId == list.id` (GoalChecklistSync, since deleted, and the `advisor/digest` builders) keeps working
  unchanged - there is still exactly one list, exactly as the live app already behaved before this
  wave.

chunks.heading: Cutover 1: Notes and Places become engine-native > Catch-up design (point 3)
chunks.text:
`EngineDataMigrationWave1.catchUpOnce(context)`:

1. Guarded by its own SharedPreferences marker (`cutover1_catchup_v1_completed`) - runs at most once
   ever, called from `MidnightApplication.onCreate` in the SAME coroutine as, and immediately after,
   the ordinary wave-1 `copyNotesIfNeeded`/`copyPlacesIfNeeded` calls (not a second, racing
   `appScope.launch` - see that file's own comment for why the ordering is deliberate).
2. Clears BOTH `KEY_NOTES_COMPLETED`/`KEY_PLACES_COMPLETED` flags (the ordinary fast-path skip those
   two functions would otherwise take), then re-runs `copyNotesIfNeeded`/`copyPlacesIfNeeded`. Their
   own per-row `guid` check (unchanged) makes this an actual rescan: any row already copied is
   recognized and skipped, any row written to `list_items`/`places` between wave 1 landing and this
   cutover install is picked up for the first time.
3. Runs `rekeySkipsToEngineIds` - walks every `ListItemSkip` row, looks up its legacy item's
   `syncId`, finds the matching `EngineRecord` by `getByGuid`, and re-points `itemId` at that
   record's id. A skip whose legacy item or matching engine record cannot be found is left alone
   (same accepted cost as wave 1's own "does not copy tombstoned rows" scope cut).
4. Only then sets the completion marker - a crash between the rescan and the rekey leaves the marker
   unset and the WHOLE catch-up (rescan included) retries next app start.

Verified: `EngineDataMigrationWave1CutoverTest` - a legacy row written after the first wave-1 pass
is picked up by `catchUpOnce`; a second `catchUpOnce` call is a no-op; a skip row keyed to a legacy
id is rekeyed onto its item's new, DIFFERENT engine id, and is no longer findable under the stale
one.

chunks.heading: Cutover 1: Notes and Places become engine-native > Recurrence/skips (point 4)
chunks.text:
`ListItemSkip.itemId` needed no schema change - see the `list_item_skips` row in the reader/writer
table above. Verified end to end: `NotesControllerTest`'s
`skipOccurrence keys ListItemSkip by the engine record id` writes a skip through the now-engine-backed
`NotesController.skipOccurrence` and reads it back by the engine id; `EngineDataMigrationWave1CutoverTest`
covers the historical rekey of a skip written before cutover.

chunks.heading: Cutover 1: Notes and Places become engine-native > Reminders (point 6)
chunks.text:
**Notes/place reminders were already NOT on `DatesAgenda`/`dueAt` before this branch, and still are
not after it - this is stated plainly rather than silently assumed.** `NotesAspectSeeder` wires
`startsAt` as the Notes `Item` record type's `primaryDueDateFieldId` (unchanged since wave 1), which
means a Notes item with a time trigger DOES populate `EngineRecord.dueAt` and DOES appear in
`DatesAgenda.windowed`'s cross-aspect query - that part was already true the moment wave 1 landed,
before any cutover. What this branch changes is narrower and different: the actual FIRING mechanism
(`AlarmManager`, via `notes/AlarmScheduler.kt`) now reads its candidate items from
`NotesController.allWithTimeTrigger`/`markMissed`/`setExactDowngraded` - engine-backed - instead of
`ListItemDao` directly, so a reminder set today keeps firing on schedule using the SAME OS-level
`AlarmManager` plumbing as before cutover. **No product behaviour changed here**: reminders fired
off `AlarmManager` before this branch and still do; what changed is which table the trigger data
underneath that alarm now lives in. `NotesControllerTest`/`EngineDataMigrationWave1CutoverTest`
exercise the read side; the actual `AlarmManager` schedule/fire cycle is unchanged code
(`AlarmScheduler.schedule`) and is not itself under test in this branch (it wasn't before, either -
it needs a real device clock/AlarmManager, out of Robolectric's reach) - **owed on-device**.

chunks.heading: Cutover 1: Notes and Places become engine-native > A genuine fork, surfaced rather than built
chunks.text:
The dispatching brief's point 5 said: "delete the dies-into-meta-tools notes/lists/places tools from
LiveToolbox per the inventory." Read literally, that means deleting `tag_place`, `forget_place`,
`read_list`, `manage_item` (the tool-inventory's own bucket) and letting the model fall through to
`EngineToolbox`'s nine generic meta-tools (`create_record`/`update_record`/`query_records`/etc.)
for Notes and Places.

**Traced end to end and stopped rather than built**, per CLAUDE.md's standing instruction to STOP
and surface a genuine product/architecture fork rather than improvise past it: `EngineToolbox` is
PURE generic `RecordStore` CRUD with no domain hooks at all. Deleting the four tools above and
routing solely through the meta-tools would silently drop, with no replacement:

- **Alarm scheduling.** `RecordStore.create`/`update` never call `AlarmScheduler` - a reminder
  created through `create_record` would never actually fire.
- **The recurring-item tick refusal** (`NotesController.tick`'s `repeatKind != null` guard, ticket
  04) - `update_record` would happily flip `done` on a recurring item.
- **At-most-one-trigger enforcement** (charting decision 4) - `update_record` writes a partial field
  set with no cross-field invariant at all.
- **Place-label normalization** ("home"/"work" synonyms, `PlaceController.normalizeLabel`) and the
  re-tag-upsert-by-label semantics this branch just added.
- **Missed-item bookkeeping** (`markMissed`/`dismissMissed`, ticket 12).

chunks.heading: Cutover 1: Notes and Places become engine-native > A genuine fork, surfaced rather than built
chunks.text:
The wave 1 carve doc's own tool table already names the shape of this problem for one row -
"`AlarmScheduler`-driven notification/missed-item surfaces: No - alarm scheduling is native OS
integration... only the record STORAGE moves to the engine, the scheduling mechanism does not
become a meta-tool" - but does not extend that reasoning to the other three tools, which carry the
SAME kind of non-CRUD domain logic. **Ruling for this branch**: `tag_place`/`forget_place`/
`read_list`/`manage_item`/`set_reminder` all stay as LiveToolbox tools, rewired to call the (now
engine-backed) `NotesController`/`PlaceController`/`ReminderController` - satisfying "rewire the
surviving verbs to the controller" - but NOT deleted, since deleting them today would ship a real
regression the generic meta-tools cannot cover without a capability-plugin hook the engine does not
have yet (ticket 11's own "unbuilt API", named in CLAUDE.md §10). This is a decision for whoever

chunks.heading: Cutover 2: Pantry becomes engine-native
chunks.text:
Owed by `.scratch/aspect-engine/issues/22-cutover-per-aspect.md` ("Cutover per aspect: the engine
becomes the read and write path"), open question 2 ("Pantry: persist subtotal/tax/other so the
gate invariant is re-checkable post-hoc"). Written before this doc's own author claims the branch
is done, per CLAUDE.md §8's L11 ("a ticket's own verification steps are gates, not notes") - same
discipline `cutover1-2026-08-24.md` set, and the worked example this doc follows rather than
re-deriving its own shape from scratch.

**The reconciliation gate (CLAUDE.md §4) is UNCHANGED and applies harder here than it did to
cutover 1.** Every `PantryReceipt`/`PantryLineItem` row is `RecordProvenance.LLM_RECONCILED`,
never `USER` - this is document-extracted data, gated before it ever reaches Room
(`docs/architecture/wave2-carve-2026-08-23.md`'s own finding: "the gate is enforced upstream of
Room, not inside it"). Cutover does not touch `PantryReceiptAgent.parseAndReconcile` at all - the
gate's arithmetic, its quarantine messages, and its "nothing partial is ever written" posture are
byte-for-byte identical to the pre-cutover code. What cutover changes is only WHERE a gate-passed
`Success` result lands.

chunks.heading: Cutover 2: Pantry becomes engine-native > What "cutover" means here, precisely
chunks.text:
Before this branch: the engine held a COPY of every `PantryReceipt`/`PantryLineItem` (wave 2), but
nothing read or wrote it - `PantryController` was still 100% legacy-table-backed, and the engine
copy was write-once, dead weight, exactly like wave 1's notes/places before cutover 1.

After this branch: `PantryController` is internally engine-backed (every read and write goes
through `RecordStore` against the Pantry aspect's `Receipt`/`LineItem` record types), and every
caller - `ui/PantryScreen.kt`, `service/LiveToolbox.kt`'s `list_recent_groceries`/
`get_grocery_spend` - keeps calling the SAME public functions on `PantryController`, unchanged
(ADR 0035: "the controller keeps its seam"). The legacy `pantry_receipts`/`pantry_line_items`
tables are **frozen for new content** - every receipt imported from this branch forward is written
through the engine, never the legacy DAO.

chunks.heading: Cutover 2: Pantry becomes engine-native > The reader/writer ruling table

2. **Raw-table-name grep** (the methodology fix cutover 1's senior review forced, applied from the

chunks.heading: Cutover 2: Pantry becomes engine-native > What died
chunks.text:
Nothing was deleted. `PantryReceipt`/`PantryLineItem` entities, their DAOs, and every existing
column stay exactly as they are - this cutover adds new engine SCHEMA (three `FieldDef` rows on
the `Receipt` record type) and rewires one controller's internals, nothing more. Matches wave 2's
own closing note and cutover 1's "nothing was deleted in this pass."

chunks.heading: Cutover 2: Pantry becomes engine-native > The bridge: how the controller keeps its seam
chunks.text:
Every public `PantryController` function keeps its exact pre-cutover signature and return type
(`PantryReceipt`/`PantryLineItem`/`PantryCurrencyTotal`/`PantryReceiptSummary` - the legacy Room
row shapes), so every caller flips with zero changes of its own. What changed is entirely internal:

chunks.heading: Cutover 2: Pantry becomes engine-native > The bridge: how the controller keeps its seam
chunks.text:
- `PantryController` resolves the Pantry aspect schema (`PantryAspectSeeder.ensureSeeded`),
  converts every `EngineRecord` it reads into an in-memory `PantryReceipt`/`PantryLineItem`
  (`toReceipt`/`toLineItem`, reusing `wave2-carve-2026-08-23.md`'s exact field mapping - not a
  second mapping), and writes through `RecordStore.create`.
- **`importReceipt`'s gate boundary is exactly where it always was.** `PantryReceiptAgent.extract`/
  `parseAndReconcile` are untouched. A `PantryIngestResult.Quarantined` returns straight back with
  no engine call at all - the gate still writes NOTHING on a quarantine, same as before cutover.
- **`importReceipt` delegates a `Success` result to `writeReceipt`, its own network-free half**
  (mirrors `PantryReceiptAgent.parseAndReconcile`'s "network-free... unit-tested directly" split -
  `PantryControllerTest` calls `writeReceipt` directly with a hand-built `Success`, no Gemini key or
  network needed). `writeReceipt` writes receipt-then-items inside one `androidx.room.withTransaction` block,
  same primitive `ledger/IngestPipeline.kt`/`ledger/LedgerController.kt` already use elsewhere in
  this codebase. The receipt is created first (its engine id is required by every line item's
  `REFERENCE` field - `RecordStore.create`'s reference-validation step rejects a reference to an
  id that doesn't exist yet, same ordering constraint the wave-2 copier itself already documented).
  Any `RecordStore.WriteResult.Failure` - on the receipt OR any line item - throws a private
  `EngineWriteFailedException` that `withTransaction` catches to roll back the WHOLE write, so a
  receipt can never be left with some but not all of its line items. `writeReceipt` then reports a
  worded failure ("checked out, but I couldn't save it") rather than a false success - CLAUDE.md
  §7's outcome-verb rule, applied from the first line of this rewrite rather than retrofitted after
  a senior review found it missing (cutover 1's should-fix 3).
- **`recentLineItems`/`recentLineItemsWithCurrency`/`recentReceiptsWithItems` re-derive the old SQL
  `JOIN ... ORDER BY purchaseDate DESC LIMIT` in memory** - reading every active engine record for
  the aspect and sorting/capping in Kotlin, same "personal household app's data volume, not an
  enterprise table scan" tradeoff `RecordStore`'s own class doc already accepts for its aggregate

chunks.heading: Cutover 2: Pantry becomes engine-native > The bridge: how the controller keeps its seam
chunks.text:
scans, and the same one CLAUDE.md §10 already accepted for the untested pre-cutover DB-write
  paths this replaces.

chunks.heading: Cutover 2: Pantry becomes engine-native > Anchor persistence (the owed wave-2 follow-up, ticket 22 open question 2)
chunks.text:
`PantryReceiptAgent.parseAndReconcile` already reads `subtotal`/`tax`/`otherCharges` off the
receipt's own print and reconciles against them - before this branch, that arithmetic's INPUTS were
thrown away the instant a receipt was written, so nothing later could re-derive "did this actually
tie out" without re-running the whole extraction.

1. **`PantryIngestResult.Success`** gained three new nullable fields - `subtotalCents`, `taxCents`,
   `otherChargesCents` - populated directly from the same local `val`s
   `PantryReceiptAgent.parseAndReconcile` already computed for its own gate check. Not re-derived,
   not re-verified - carried straight through.
2. **`PantryAspectSeeder`** gained three new optional `MONEY_CENTS` fields on the `Receipt` record
   type (`FIELD_SUBTOTAL`/`FIELD_TAX`/`FIELD_OTHER_CHARGES`), added via the SAME idempotent
   `ensureField` path every other field in that seeder uses - additive schema DATA (new
   `field_defs` rows), not a Room migration, no `app/schemas/` diff, reaching Kevin's
   already-seeded phone the next time `ensureSeeded` runs (exactly the benefit the engine is
   designed to provide - see `NotesController`'s own `loggedAt` precedent from cutover 1).
   `PantryAspectSeederTest`'s field-count assertion updated 5 -> 8.
3. **`PantryController.importReceipt`** writes all three into the receipt's `fieldValues` map
   alongside the five wave-2 fields.
4. **Not required, not locked.** A receipt legitimately prints no subtotal/tax line (the
   tax-free-basket branch `PantryReceiptAgent`'s own doc comment names - Singapore GST-inclusive
   receipts) - null there means "not printed," never "not checked," since the gate already ran
   either way before the row could exist at all.
5. **Historical rows stay anchor-less - not backfilled.** Neither `PantryReceipt` nor
   `PantryLineItem` (the legacy Room entities) ever carried these three columns, so
   `EngineDataMigrationWave2`'s copier has nothing to read them FROM - a migrated row's three
   anchor fields are explicit JSON `null` (the field exists in schema, the value was never known).
   This is honest, not a gap: fabricating a subtotal for a receipt imported before this branch
   existed would assert a fact nobody verified. Stated here per instruction 3's own requirement,
   not silently left implicit.

chunks.heading: Cutover 2: Pantry becomes engine-native > Catch-up (point 4)
chunks.text:
`EngineDataMigrationWave2.catchUpOnce(context)`, same shape as
`EngineDataMigrationWave1.catchUpOnce`:

1. Guarded by its own SharedPreferences marker (`cutover2_pantry_catchup_v1_completed`) - runs at
   most once ever, called from `MidnightApplication.onCreate` in the SAME coroutine as, and
   immediately after, the ordinary wave-2 `copyPantryIfNeeded` call.
2. Clears `KEY_PANTRY_COMPLETED` (the ordinary fast-path skip `copyPantryIfNeeded` would otherwise
   take), then re-runs it. Its own per-row `guid` check (unchanged, and unaffected by the three new
   anchor fields - `RecordStore.create`'s reference/idempotency logic doesn't care how many
   optional fields a record type has) makes this an actual rescan: any row already copied is
   recognized and skipped, any row written to `pantry_receipts`/`pantry_line_items` between wave 2
   landing and this cutover install is picked up for the first time.
3. **No rekey pass needed - checked, not assumed.** Cutover 1 needed to rekey `ListItemSkip.itemId`
   because that column stored a legacy `list_items.id` directly. Grepped this codebase for anything
   analogous keying off a legacy `PantryReceipt.id`/`PantryLineItem.id`: nothing found.
   `data/PantryPhotoStore.kt` - the only other pantry-adjacent piece of state - is keyed by a
   save-time millisecond filename (`"${System.currentTimeMillis()}.jpg"`), never by a receipt row
   id, confirmed by reading the whole 39-line file. Stated as a finding, not silently assumed.

- **Macros stay estimate-labelled everywhere.** `PantryAspectSeeder`'s `estimated`-prefixed field
  names are untouched by this branch, and `ui/pantry/PantryReceiptSection`'s `ON THE RECEIPT` /
  `ESTIMATED, NOT ON THE RECEIPT` segregation (ticket 09) reads the SAME `PantryLineItem` value

chunks.heading: Cutover 3: Ledger becomes engine-native
chunks.text:
Owed by `.scratch/aspect-engine/issues/22-cutover-per-aspect.md` ("Cutover per aspect: the engine
becomes the read and write path"). Written before this doc's own author claims the branch is done,
per CLAUDE.md §8's L11 ("a ticket's own verification steps are gates, not notes") - the same
discipline `cutover1-2026-08-24.md`/`cutover2-2026-08-24.md` set, and the worked example this doc
follows rather than re-deriving its own shape from scratch.

**This is the highest-stakes of the three cutovers so far** - ledger is the one aspect whose data
carries CLAUDE.md §4's reconciliation provenance for real, including rule 7's provisional-row
supersession. The reconciliation gate itself (`ledger/LedgerStatementAgent`, the deterministic
parsers, `resolveDedup`, `buildBudgetVsActual`) is **byte-for-byte untouched** by this branch - see

write, exactly as cutover 2 found for pantry. What cutover 3 changes is only WHERE a gate-passed
result lands, and where rule 7's transience guarantee is enforced.

chunks.heading: Cutover 3: Ledger becomes engine-native > What "cutover" means here, precisely
chunks.text:
Before this branch: the engine held a COPY of every `LedgerTransaction` (wave 3), but nothing read
or wrote it - `LedgerController`/`IngestPipeline` were still 100% legacy-table-backed, and the engine
copy was reconciled by `EngineDataMigrationWave3`'s own per-call pass, dead weight otherwise, exactly
like wave 1/2's notes/places/pantry before their own cutovers.

After this branch: `LedgerController`/`IngestPipeline` are internally engine-backed (every read and
write goes through `RecordStore`/`EngineRecordDao` against the Ledger aspect's `Transaction` record
type), and every caller - `ui/LedgerImportActivity`, the Money tab screens, `service/LiveToolbox.kt`'s
ledger tools, `advisor/digest/CredDigestBuilder`/`HomeDigestBuilder`, `goals/GoalProgress` - keeps
calling the SAME public functions, unchanged (ADR 0035: "the controller keeps its seam"). The legacy
`ledger_transactions` table is **frozen for new content** - every value a user sees or acts on from
this branch forward was written through the engine, never the legacy DAO. `ingested_files`
(per-file ingestion ledger), `categories`/`category_rules` (classification vocabulary), and
`budget_targets` stay plugin-internal and legacy-backed, unchanged - `wave3-carve-2026-08-23.md`'s
carve table already ruled all three off the engine, and nothing here re-opens that ruling.

chunks.heading: Cutover 3: Ledger becomes engine-native > The reader/writer ruling table
chunks.text:
Grep-proven, both methods, across `app/src/main/java/com/kevin/legion` at the end of this branch -
cutover 1's senior-review-forced methodology (a DAO-shaped grep AND a raw-table-name grep, applied
from the start here rather than discovered the hard way):

1. **DAO-shaped grep**: `ledgerTransactionDao()\.`
2. **Raw-table-name grep**: `"ledger_transactions"` as a bare string literal.
3. **A third grep this cutover adds, because it caught a real bypass the first two structurally
   cannot**: `ledgerTransactionDao()` (no trailing dot) - an assign-then-use pattern
   (`val txnDao = db.ledgerTransactionDao(); txnDao.foo()`) that grep #1 cannot see because the
   method call and the field access never appear on the same line. This is exactly the same class of
   miss cutover 1's senior review found for `SyncEngine.REGISTRY`'s raw-SQL `Spec` - a different
   syntactic shape defeating a pattern-shaped grep, not a raw-SQL bypass this time, but the same
   underlying lesson. **This grep is what found `goals/GoalProgress.kt`'s `savingsBalanceCents`** -
   see "A genuine bypass this cutover's own methodology caught" below.
