chunks.heading: Cutover 3: Ledger becomes engine-native > The commit-transaction design
chunks.text:
`IngestPipeline.commit`'s `Success` branch, in order, all inside ONE `db.withTransaction` block:

1. **Replace-flow deletion** (`staged.isReplace`): every ACTIVE engine `Transaction` record whose
   `sourceFileId` field equals the incoming `driveFileId` is trashed via `RecordStore.delete` - the
   engine-side equivalent of the retired `LedgerTransactionDao.deleteBySourceFileId`. Any
   non-`Trashed`/non-`AlreadyTrashed` result throws `EngineWriteFailedException`.
2. **Rule 7 supersession, engine-side, in the same transaction as the insert that follows.** When
   `stamped.first().ingestMethod != UNRECONCILED` (a reconciled file), every ACTIVE engine
   `Transaction` record tagged `RecordProvenance.UNRECONCILED` for the SAME physical card (`sameCard`,
   suffix-matched exactly as the retired legacy query `deleteSupersededProvisional` was) whose
   `txnDate` falls inside the incoming statement's own `[minDate, maxDate]` range is trashed. The
   three load-bearing properties the legacy version's own doc comment named are preserved exactly:
   **the guard** (an `UNRECONCILED` file can never supersede anything, including its own prior
   import), **before the dedup read** (a stale provisional row must not survive to be matched as a
   duplicate and drop the verified row that was meant to replace it), **inside the transaction** (a
   crash between the delete and the insert can never leave the account with neither).
3. **Dedup read**, now against the ENGINE mirror (`activeByRecordType`, converted via
   `LedgerRecordBridge.toTransaction`) instead of `getForAccountInRange`, read AFTER steps 1-2 so it
   never sees a row that was just trashed. `resolveDedup` itself - the pure per-tuple counting
   function - is REUSED VERBATIM, untouched by this cutover; only its data source changed.
4. **Insert**, one `RecordStore.create` per `resolveDedup`'s `toInsert` row, provenance mapped via
   `LedgerRecordBridge.provenanceFor(txn.ingestMethod)`, `guid = txn.syncId`. Any
   `WriteResult.Failure` throws.
5. `ingested_files` bookkeeping (`ingestedDao.upsert`) - unchanged, still legacy, still inside the
   same transaction.

chunks.heading: Cutover 3: Ledger becomes engine-native > The commit-transaction design
chunks.text:
**Any exception anywhere in steps 1-5 rolls the WHOLE transaction back** (Room's `withTransaction`
rolls back on a thrown exception, never a plain early return - the same primitive
`pantry/PantryController.writeReceipt` already established for a receipt-plus-items write). The
`try`/`catch` sits OUTSIDE `db.withTransaction`, catching `EngineWriteFailedException` after Room has
already rolled back, then writes the file's `IngestedFile` record back to `IngestState.NEW` (OUTSIDE
the rolled-back transaction, as its own write) so the file is re-offered on the next scan rather than
vanishing, and returns `CommitOutcome.EngineWriteFailed(reason)` - a worded failure (CLAUDE.md §7),
never a false success. `LedgerController.commitResult` and the folder-scan service that sat beside
it both handled this new sealed-class case exhaustively at the time (Kotlin's `when` forced both
call sites to be updated at compile time). **Both are gone now** - backend-erp ticket 25
(2026-08-29) deleted phone-side statement ingestion entirely, `commitResult` and the scan service
included; this paragraph is historical record of the cutover, not a live code path.

chunks.heading: Cutover 3: Ledger becomes engine-native > Rule-7 semantics: what changed and what did not (a fork, resolved rather than surfaced blind)
chunks.text:
**Not a semantic change** - the supersession RULE itself (which rows get trashed, on what
guard, in what order, relative to what read) is preserved exactly; only its storage layer moved.
This was checked, not assumed: every one of the three load-bearing properties the legacy
`deleteSupersededProvisional` caller comment named is still true of the engine-side version, and the
new `IngestPipelineEngineCommitTest`'s supersession test pins the exact in-window/out-of-window/
non-`UNRECONCILED` boundary the legacy SQL query enforced (`substr(accountId, -4) = substr(:accountId,
-4) AND txnDate BETWEEN :fromMs AND :toMs AND ingestMethod = 'UNRECONCILED'`), now expressed as a
Kotlin filter over `sameCard`/date-range/provenance instead of SQL.

**What DID change, stated rather than left implicit**: before this branch, `RecordStore.delete`
trashes (30-day restorable) rather than hard-deleting the way the legacy `DELETE FROM
ledger_transactions WHERE ...` did. This is a strictly SAFER guarantee, not a weaker one - a
superseded provisional row is now recoverable for 30 days instead of gone the instant it is
superseded - and it costs nothing: no surface reads trashed rows (`activeByRecordType` excludes
them everywhere), so a driver-visible balance/total is identical either way. Same reasoning
`LedgerController.purgeAll`'s own doc comment now states for its own move onto `RecordStore.delete`.

chunks.heading: Cutover 3: Ledger becomes engine-native > What retired
chunks.text:
**`EngineDataMigrationWave3.reconcileSupersededProvisional`'s automatic per-call invocation is
retired.** Wave 3 originally ran this pass on EVERY call to `copyLedgerIfNeeded`, including the fast
path, because the ONLY place rule-7 supersession happened was the legacy table, and a purely additive
copier could not mirror a deletion any other way. Cutover 3 moves supersession itself into
`IngestPipeline.commit`'s own engine-side transaction (see above) - a newly superseded provisional row
is trashed at write time now, in the exact same transaction as the write that supersedes it, so the
reconciliation pass is no longer needed on every call.

**The function itself is KEPT, not deleted** - its doc comment's own reasoning ("an additive-only
copier cannot mirror a deletion") still holds for exactly one remaining case: legacy-table
supersession that happened BEFORE this cutover branch's `IngestPipeline` took over (the historical
window between wave 3's original landing and this build). `EngineDataMigrationWave3.catchUpOnce` -
new this branch, same shape as `EngineDataMigrationWave1.catchUpOnce`/`EngineDataMigrationWave2.catchUpOnce`
- calls it exactly once, guarded by its own SharedPreferences marker
(`cutover3_catchup_v1_completed`), after re-running the ordinary additive copy. `EngineDataMigrationWave3.Result`
lost its `supersededTrashed` field (no longer meaningful for `copyLedgerIfNeeded`'s own per-call
return value, since that pass no longer runs the reconciliation step) - `EngineDataMigrationWave3Test`
was updated to assert `catchUpOnce`'s effects directly instead (four tests, listed below), not deleted.

**Neither `LedgerTransaction` nor `IngestedFile` is dropped.** Both stay exactly as they are today -
this branch rewires WRITE and READ paths, not schema; no `app/schemas/` diff, no migration, no
version bump.

chunks.heading: Cutover 3: Ledger becomes engine-native > The bridge: how the controller keeps its seam
chunks.text:

- **`LedgerController.allTransactions(context)`** is the one read every other function funnels

  DAO-query-shaped read (`getForAccountInRange`, `getForCurrencyInRange`, `allAccountIds`,
  `accountIdsForCurrency`, `currencyForAccount`, `earliestTxnDate`/`latestTxnDate`,
  `uncategorizedTransactions`, `categoryPendingRows`, etc.) is now a Kotlin filter/aggregate over this
  one in-memory list, same "personal household app's data volume, not an enterprise table scan"
  tradeoff `RecordStore`'s own class doc already accepts, and the same one
  `pantry/PantryController.allReceipts`/`allLineItems` already applies.
- **Every PURE business-logic function this codebase already had - `resolveDedup` (`LedgerDedup.kt`),

- **Category application** (`applyCategoryRules`/`applyCategoryGuesses`/`confirmCategoryGuess`/

  queries - now read the matching rows out of `allTransactions`, then write each one through

chunks.heading: Cutover 3: Ledger becomes engine-native > Dedup discipline (point 5)
chunks.text:
`LedgerController`'s pre-cutover cross-file dedup was two-layered: `resolveDedup` (pure, per-tuple
counting, `LedgerDedup.kt` - REUSED VERBATIM) plus a DAO-backed candidate-set fetch

description, different `lineRef`) is skipped, and a genuinely new row from the same statement still

chunks.heading: Cutover 3: Ledger becomes engine-native > Senior review, 2026-08-24: one blocking finding, one should-fix (both taken)
chunks.text:
**BLOCKING - `catchUpOnce` first-launch race.** `reconcileSupersededProvisional`'s original logic
trashed any active engine `UNRECONCILED` `Transaction` record whose `guid` was missing from legacy
`allSyncIds()`. Post-cutover, `IngestPipeline.commit`/`LedgerController.logPendingTransaction`
create BRAND-NEW engine `UNRECONCILED` rows whose `guid` was NEVER written to the legacy table
(`ledger_transactions` has zero writers, per this doc's own ruling table) - such a `guid` is, by
construction, always "missing" from legacy. A driver importing a card CSV or voice-logging a pending
transaction on first launch, before the fire-and-forget `catchUpOnce` coroutine finishes, would have
that legitimate row silently trashed with nothing superseding it - rule 7 inverted.

chunks.heading: Cutover 3: Ledger becomes engine-native > Senior review, 2026-08-24: one blocking finding, one should-fix (both taken)
chunks.text:
**Fix chosen: a persisted, positively-tracked migrated-guid set**, not a `createdAt`-cutoff (the
review's other offered shape). `createdAt` was checked, not assumed, and ruled out: both the copier
and `IngestPipeline.commit`'s own create call pass `now = txn.txnDate` to `RecordStore.create` (the
field-mapping doc comment's own "closest available anchor" reasoning), so `EngineRecord.createdAt`
reflects the TRANSACTION'S OWN DATE for both a migrated row and a live-imported one, never wall-clock
insert time - a timestamp cutoff would have been silently wrong on real data (a transaction dated
yesterday, imported ten seconds ago, reads as "older" than any reasonable catch-up cutoff).
`EngineDataMigrationWave3.copyLedgerIfNeeded` now records every `guid` it confirms as legacy-derived
(newly created OR found already-copied on a rescan) into a SharedPreferences string set
(`migrated_guids_v1`); `reconcileSupersededProvisional` gates on membership in that set BEFORE ever
asking whether a guid is missing from legacy. A live-imported row's `guid` (a fresh UUID, never
touching the frozen legacy table) can never be a member, so it is structurally exempt regardless of
timing - no race window exists to lose. Full reasoning is in `EngineDataMigrationWave3.kt`'s own
class doc and `reconcileSupersededProvisional`'s doc comment. New tests: `EngineDataMigrationWave3Test`'s
`catchUpOnce never trashes an engine-native row whose guid was never in the legacy table, even if
created before reconcile runs` (the exact race) and `catchUpOnce still trashes a genuinely migrated
row once its legacy backing disappears, proving the new gate isn't overbroad` (the positive control -
proves the fix didn't just make reconciliation trash nothing at all).

chunks.heading: Cutover 3: Ledger becomes engine-native > Senior review, 2026-08-24: one blocking finding, one should-fix (both taken)
chunks.text:
**SHOULD-FIX (pre-existing, taken now because ledger's multi-row commits make it hot) - `RecordStore`'s
`_afterWrite.tryEmit` fires INSIDE the caller's `withTransaction`.** Traced end to end rather than
changed: the only production subscriber (`MirrorLifecycleBinder`) always routes through
`MirrorSync.scheduleExport()`, which unconditionally delays 5 seconds before touching Room and then
reads fresh via DAO calls at read time - several orders of magnitude past how long a ledger/pantry
multi-row `db.withTransaction` block takes to settle, and independent of that margin, Room's own
transactional isolation means a reader outside a transaction cannot observe its uncommitted writes at
all. No code change; `RecordStore.kt`'s `afterWrite` doc comment now carries the full traced
justification. Deliberately NOT covered by an automated test - a genuine cross-connection commit/
rollback race is not something Robolectric's single-process SQLite harness can be trusted to
reproduce meaningfully, so this is stated as `traced`, not `tested`.

  card-CSV provisional-then-superseded flows on real Drive files.
- Voice tools (`import_statement`/`get_balance`/`list_recent_transactions`/`categorize_transactions`/

chunks.heading: Cutover 4: Fleet becomes engine-native > Senior review, 2026-08-24: one blocking finding, one should-fix (both taken)
chunks.text:
**BLOCKING - `FleetRecordBridge.projectAnchor` fabricated joint facts.** The first version of this
function took the highest mileage across every `ServiceHistory` row for a service and the latest
date across every row INDEPENDENTLY, so a mileage from one row could pair with a date from a
completely different row - a joint (mileage, date) fact no single write ever actually stated
together. `VehicleController.mergeBackfillAnchors`'s own doc comment already names this exact
failure shape as forbidden ("pairing it with the fresh mileage would assert a fact nobody stated").
**Fixed**: `projectAnchor` now derives the anchor from a SINGLE row - the most-recently-stated one
(greatest `EngineRecord.updatedAt`) among `OBSERVED`+`ASSERTED` for that service - taking BOTH axes
together from that one row, including its nulls. This mirrors the legacy schema exactly:
`MaintenanceItemDao.setAnchor` always overwrote both anchor columns in one UPDATE, so the row's live
state was always whatever the LAST write fully stated, never a blend of two different writes' own
fields. See `FleetRecordBridge.projectAnchor`'s own doc comment for the full reasoning, and "The
unification" section below for what this changes in practice. New/updated tests:
`FleetEngineStoreTest`'s `an OBSERVED insert that matches only ONE axis of the ASSERTED anchor does
NOT supersede it - the both-axes rule` now also asserts the derived anchor is the most-recent row's
own two axes, never a blend; `the derived anchor's date is null when the most-recently-stated row is
dateless, even though an older row has a real date` is new, pinning the null-not-borrowed case
directly.

**SHOULD-FIX - `MonthlyRecapController`'s spoken/rendered service count read as complete when it
is not.** `serviceCount` still reads the legacy `service_records` table (this doc's own ruling
table already named this as a deliberate, deferred exception - `MonthlyRecap` itself is one of Wave
4's own deferred entities), but every surface that showed the bare number read as a complete count
with nothing telling the reader otherwise. **Fixed**: the two render sites
(`ui/fleet/FleetDrilldowns.kt:1013,1041`) and the narrative string
(`vehicle/MonthlyRecapController.kt:197`) now state in words that the figure may not include recent
services, until `MonthlyRecap` gets its own follow-up-wave cutover (ticket 23's own tracking item).

chunks.heading: Cutover 4: Fleet becomes engine-native > The reader/writer ruling table
chunks.text:
Grep-proven, three methods (cutover 1's senior-review-forced methodology, applied from the start):

1. **DAO-shaped grep**: `\.(vehicleDao|serviceRecordDao|maintenanceItemDao)\(\)\.`
2. **Raw-table-name grep**: `"vehicles"|"service_records"|"maintenance_items"` as bare string
   literals.
3. **The no-dot, assign-then-use grep** (`\.(vehicleDao|serviceRecordDao|maintenanceItemDao)\(\)\s*$`)
   - the exact shape that caught `SyncEngine.REGISTRY` at cutover 1 and `goals/GoalProgress.kt` at
   cutover 3. **This is what actually caught real bypasses this branch**: `PopulateWrites.kt`'s
   `.restore(...)` call was on the line AFTER `.maintenanceItemDao()`, invisible to grep #1;
   `FleetSpendController.kt`, `BuildSheetController.kt`, `CarToolbelt.kt`, `MaintenanceAgent.kt`,
   `VehicleResolver.kt` all held a `val dao = db.xDao()` assign-then-use shape grep #1 cannot see on
   one line. Fourteen files total, beyond `VehicleController.kt` itself, were reading or writing
   these three tables directly - none of them named in `wave4-carve-2026-08-23.md`'s own voice-tool
   table, because that table only ever enumerated `LiveToolbox.kt`'s declarations, not every screen/
   digest/advisor consumer underneath them.

chunks.heading: Cutover 4: Fleet becomes engine-native > The reader/writer ruling table > `SyncEngine`/`MidnightImport` findings, stated either way
chunks.text:
**`sync/SyncEngine.kt`'s `REGISTRY`** carried raw-SQL `Spec`s for all three tables. Per cutover 1's
precedent (`places`):

- **`service_records` and `maintenance_items` `Spec`s were RETIRED** in this branch - both tables
  have zero writers now, so a merge pass over them can only ever see whatever synced before this
  build. `com.kevin.legion.engine.mirror.MirrorSync` is the live cross-device path for
  `ServiceHistory`/`MaintenanceSchedule` now, same as `places` at cutover 1. **Transition
  consequence, stated rather than assumed away**: identical shape to cutover 1's own - a peer phone
  on a pre-cutover build keeps syncing these two tables to itself only, and closes the moment both
  of Kevin's phones run a cutover-4-or-later build.
- **`vehicles`' `Spec` was KEPT**, deliberately, unlike the other two. It is not dead plumbing - see
  "The Vehicle mirror" below for why the legacy `vehicles` table is still a real, actively-written
  store (of exactly the columns the engine record type does not carry), and removing this `Spec`
  would silently strand `tripMilesSinceBaseline`/`archived`/etc. on whichever phone last wrote them.

**`data/MidnightImport.kt`** carries `TableSpec`s for all three tables, writing raw `INSERT OR
IGNORE` SQL. Same finding cutover 1 already made for its own `places` entry: this importer reads
from `assets/midnight_import/`, a directory that does not exist in this repo, so it is presently
inert on every real build - a one-time, pre-LEGION historical migration path, not an ongoing sync
surface. Left alone, for the identical three reasons cutover 1's doc already gave (unreachable
today, explicitly one-shot, out of this blocking finding's scope).

chunks.heading: Cutover 4: Fleet becomes engine-native > The Vehicle mirror - a genuine fork, resolved and stated in words
chunks.text:
Wave 4's carve deliberately did NOT carry `obdMac` as a field on the engine `Vehicle` record type -
its guid is derived from `obdMac` via a one-way hash (`FleetRecordBridge.vehicleGuid`,
`UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes`), so the engine record can be looked up FROM an obdMac string, but there is
no way to enumerate every registered car's `obdMac` FROM the engine payload alone - the hash cannot
be inverted. Seven more columns (`personaPrompt`/`voiceName`/`personaTraits`/`archived`/`onboarded`/
`lastOdometerPromptAt`/`tripMilesSinceBaseline`) were also deliberately left uncarried, per that same
carve's field-mapping table.

`getAll()`/`getAllIncludingArchived()` genuinely need every car's `obdMac`. `TelemetryRecorder.run`
(the single highest-frequency writer of anything fleet-related, once per 30 seconds while driving)
genuinely needs a legacy `vehicles` row to accumulate `tripMilesSinceBaseline` onto, per instruction
4's own "OBD-live state stays plugin-internal, keeps writing its own table."

**The resolution: `vehicle/FleetEngineStore.kt` is the ONLY writer of the legacy `vehicles` table's
identity columns, and it writes them ATOMICALLY alongside the engine record, every time.** Every
Vehicle-identity WRITE (`createVehicle`/`setIdentity`/`setEngine`/`applyDecodedIdentity`/
`setOdometerBaseline`) does both in one `db.withTransaction` block. Every Vehicle READ
(`getByMac`/`getAll`/`getAllIncludingArchived`) then serves straight from that always-in-sync
mirror - correct, because nothing else may write it, and it is the only place `obdMac` keys and the
seven uncarried columns can be read at all. `setArchived`/`markOdometerPrompted`/
`clearThisCarSentinel` touch ONLY the legacy-only columns, never identity - narrow, named,
single-purpose writers, not a second identity authority.

chunks.heading: Cutover 4: Fleet becomes engine-native > The Vehicle mirror - a genuine fork, resolved and stated in words
chunks.text:
**This is not the same failure mode ticket 29 diagnosed.** Ticket 29's bug was two INDEPENDENTLY
writable stores of ONE FACT (a service's last-done mileage/date), each free to drift from the
other with nothing reconciling them. The Vehicle mirror is the OPPOSITE shape: ONE writer
(`FleetEngineStore`), touching two tables in the same transaction, for facts that are either
engine-authoritative (identity, mirrored down) or legacy-only-authoritative (telemetry, never
touched by the engine side at all). There is no second writer for either half to disagree with.
Vehicle identity was never split across two competing stores before this cutover either - unlike
service history, this was never the bug ticket 29 named, and this cutover does not reopen it as one.

chunks.heading: Cutover 4: Fleet becomes engine-native > The unification: what actually changed, precisely
chunks.text:
**Before this branch**: `ServiceRecord` (the events) and `MaintenanceItem.lastDoneMileage`/
`lastDoneDate` (the schedule's own clock) were two Room tables, and Wave 4's copier already unified
them into one `ServiceHistory` record type (`kind = OBSERVED`/`ASSERTED`) - but nothing LIVE read or
wrote that table yet. The schema fix existed; the drift kept happening in the tables the live app
actually touched.

**After this branch**: `MaintenanceItem.lastDoneMileage`/`lastDoneDate` no longer exist as a stored
value anywhere - `FleetRecordBridge.toMaintenanceItem`/`projectAnchor` DERIVE them, fresh, on every
read, from the SAME `ServiceHistory` rows (`OBSERVED` and `ASSERTED` alike) the service-history
screen and every voice answer also read. **There is no second place either figure could be left
stale**, because there is no second stored copy of either figure at all.

`projectAnchor`'s rule (senior review, 2026-08-24, MUST-FIX - the first version of this doc's own
justification below was factually wrong, and is corrected rather than quietly replaced): the anchor
is BOTH axes of the single MOST-RECENTLY-STATED `ServiceHistory` row for that service (greatest
`EngineRecord.updatedAt`), taken together, including a null. **The two axes may never come from
different rows.** The original version of this function took the highest mileage across ALL rows and
the latest date across ALL rows independently, which can pair a mileage from one row with a date
from a completely different one - a joint fact nobody ever actually stated in one write, exactly the
cross-fact pairing `VehicleController.mergeBackfillAnchors`'s own anti-pairing rule forbids ("pairing
it with the fresh mileage would assert a fact nobody stated"). The corrected rule mirrors the legacy
schema's real behaviour: `MaintenanceItemDao.setAnchor` always overwrote both anchor columns together
in one UPDATE, so the row's live state was always whatever the LAST write fully stated, never a
blend of two different writes' individual fields - selecting the single most-recently-updated
`ServiceHistory` row and taking both its fields wholesale reproduces that exact last-write-wins,
no-cross-write-blending contract over N rows instead of one mutable pair of columns.

chunks.heading: Cutover 4: Fleet becomes engine-native > The unification: what actually changed, precisely
chunks.text:
**Due-ness implications for the Jeep's own shape, stated plainly.** The Jeep's real incident (a
dateless `ASSERTED` anchor at 227,483 mi, stated after a real 227,374-mile/12-Aug `OBSERVED` record)
migrates as two rows, neither superseding the other (the mileages disagree, so `explainedBy` is
false). Under the corrected single-row rule, whichever of the two was stated MOST RECENTLY (by
`updatedAt`) wins BOTH axes outright - if the `ASSERTED` anchor is the newer fact (the ordinary
case: a driver correction typically comes after the event it corrects), the derived anchor is
`(227,483 mi, null)` - the mileage axis is checkable against `intervalMiles`, the TIME axis reads as
unknown for this item until a dated write lands more recently, exactly matching what a legacy
single-row anchor would have shown after the SAME sequence of edits. This is a real, visible
narrowing versus the FIRST (buggy) version of this cutover, which would have shown `(227,483 mi,
12-Aug-dated)` - a due-ness figure on an axis nobody actually asserted together. The corrected
behaviour is the honest one: an unknown axis reads as unknown, not as borrowed certainty.

chunks.heading: Cutover 4: Fleet becomes engine-native > The unification: what actually changed, precisely > ASSERTED-supersession, extended live (instruction 3)
chunks.text:
Wave 4's own migration already had this rule for the ONE-TIME copy (`explainedBy`, the
both-axes-on-the-SAME-row correction from that carve's own senior review). This cutover adds the
LIVE version: `FleetEngineStore.insertObserved` - the one function EVERY real, precise "log a
service" write goes through, voice or hands - checks, in the SAME `db.withTransaction` as the
`OBSERVED` create, whether an `ASSERTED` row exists for the identical `(vehicleId, serviceName)`
pair (same deterministic guid the migration itself used, so a live write can supersede a MIGRATED
anchor exactly as readily as a live one). If every axis the `ASSERTED` row states agrees with the
new `OBSERVED` row on that SAME row - `FleetRecordBridge.explainedBy`, reused verbatim, not
reimplemented - the `ASSERTED` row is trashed in that same transaction. A real event that arrives
and explains a stated anchor makes the anchor's own separate existence redundant; a real event that
does NOT fully explain it (the Jeep's own dateless 227,483-mile anchor against a 227,374-mile/12-Aug
record) leaves both facts on file, stated as what they are, never silently reconciled - exactly
ticket 29's own instruction.

**Extended to the hands path too.** `ui/fleet/MaintenanceWrites.kt`'s `writeSetAnchor` DONE_AT-with-
cost addendum used to be a direct `ServiceRecordDao.insert` - a second writer, independent of
`logServiceDirect`'s own. It now calls the SAME `FleetEngineStore.insertObserved`, so a service
logged by hand on the ITEM DETAIL screen supersedes a matching `ASSERTED` anchor identically to one
logged by voice - the unification this cutover exists to land, extended to the supersession rule
itself, not just the read path. `FleetEngineStoreTest.kt`'s
`logServiceDirect through the voice path supersedes a matching ASSERTED anchor the SAME way` pins
this directly.

chunks.heading: Cutover 4: Fleet becomes engine-native > Atomicity (instruction 8)
chunks.text:
`FleetEngineStore.insertObserved` wraps the `OBSERVED` create and the `ASSERTED` supersession check
in one `db.withTransaction` block, `try`/`catch` OUTSIDE it (same primitive `ledger/IngestPipeline.kt`/
`pantry/PantryController.kt` already established) - `EngineWriteFailedException` thrown from either
step rolls the WHOLE transaction back. Two directions pinned:

- **Early failure**: a vehicle not on file (`engineVehicleId` resolves to null) fails before the
  transaction even opens, writing nothing - `insertObserved against a vehicle not on file fails
  with a worded reason and writes nothing`.
- **Both-halves-together**: a successful call leaves BOTH the new `OBSERVED` row AND the trashed
  `ASSERTED` row visible together, never one without the other - `a successful insertObserved
  leaves BOTH the OBSERVED create and the ASSERTED supersession applied together, never one
  without the other`. A genuine mid-transaction RecordStore failure on the supersession half (the
  `DeletePolicy.BLOCK` guard on `recordStore.delete`) is structurally unreachable today - nothing
  ever references a `ServiceHistory` row - so it is guarded defensively rather than independently
  fault-injected; stated as `reasoned`, not `tested`, in the assumptions ledger below.

`setAnchor`/`setNeverDone` (schedule-clock-clearing writes) also wrap their two-step writes
(neverDone flip + anchor write/clear) in one transaction each, same discipline.

chunks.heading: Cutover 4: Fleet becomes engine-native > `DeletePolicy.BLOCK`, exercised live (instruction 2)
chunks.text:
`FleetEngineStore.deleteVehicle` calls `RecordStore.delete` on the engine `Vehicle` record -
`ServiceHistory.vehicle`/`MaintenanceSchedule.vehicle` are both `DeletePolicy.BLOCK` references
(Wave 4's own field mapping, per instruction 1: "deleting a car with history should refuse, not
cascade silently"). `EngineDataMigrationWave4Test` already exercised BLOCK against MIGRATED data;
`FleetEngineStoreTest.kt` now exercises it against a LIVE write - `deleteVehicle on a car with live
ServiceHistory is BLOCKed, and nothing is written` / `...with a live MaintenanceSchedule (no
history yet) is also BLOCKed` / `...with neither history nor a schedule succeeds`.

**No live caller reaches `deleteVehicle` today.** Archive/unarchive (`FleetEngineStore.setArchived`)
is the only removal affordance this app currently exposes for a car - a hard-delete voice tool or
screen action does not exist, and this cutover does not add one (out of scope; no ticket
authorizes it). The refusal is real and worded (`DeleteResult.Blocked(blockers)`, every blocker
named), ready for whichever future surface calls it - stated so this is not mistaken for a wired,
user-reachable capability today.

chunks.heading: Cutover 4: Fleet becomes engine-native > Catch-up (instruction 5)
chunks.text:
**Checked, not assumed: Wave 4's own migration has no `catchUpOnce`, unlike Wave 1/2/3.**
`EngineDataMigrationWave4.kt` has exactly one entry point, `copyFleetIfNeeded`, guarded by a single
completion flag (`fleet_completed_v1`) plus the usual per-row `guid` backstop - there is no second,
reconciliation-shaped pass the way `EngineDataMigrationWave1/2/3.catchUpOnce` each have. Re-running
`copyFleetIfNeeded` is itself idempotent by construction (every row's `guid` is checked before any
write), so "re-run it once, idempotent" is satisfied by the EXISTING function - no new code was
needed or added for this instruction. Wave 4's own carve doc already named the one gap this leaves
open (owed-follow-up #8: an `ASSERTED` row computed once at copy time can go stale if a legacy
service is logged AFTER the copy but BEFORE this cutover installs) - **that gap is now closed by
this cutover landing at all**, not by a reconciliation pass: once `IngestPipeline`-shaped legacy
writes to `service_records`/`maintenance_items` stop happening (this branch's own ruling table:
zero writers), there is no more legacy-side drift for a catch-up pass to chase. The one remaining
window is between Wave 4's original copy and this cutover's install on a given phone - real, but
closed by installing this build, not by an additional migration step.

**No rekey pass needed - checked, not assumed**, same as cutover 2's own finding: nothing in this
codebase keys off a legacy `MaintenanceItem`/`ServiceRecord` row id (`ServiceRecord.id` is now
repurposed as the corresponding `EngineRecord.id` for a live-inserted `OBSERVED` row - see
`FleetRecordBridge.toServiceRecord`'s own doc comment - but nothing stored a legacy id anywhere
that would need remapping).

chunks.heading: Cutover 4: Fleet becomes engine-native > Voice tools (instruction 6)
chunks.text:
Per `docs/architecture/wave4-carve-2026-08-23.md`'s own voice-tool table, the fleet tools split
cleanly: the ones that read/write `vehicles`/`service_records`/`maintenance_items`
(`get_vehicle_data`'s identity/odometer half, `get_next_service`, `ask_maintenance`, `set_odometer`,
`log_service`, `log_past_service`, `set_maintenance_interval`, `register_vehicle`, `register_car`,
`list_vehicles`, `manage_vehicle`) already call through `VehicleController`'s public seam - this
cutover rewired that seam's INTERNALS, so every one of those tools is engine-backed now with **zero
changes to `LiveToolbox.kt`'s own tool declarations or dispatch shape** (confirmed by
`python tools/voice_guide.py` reporting zero drift - same 113 tools, same descriptions). The OBD-live
tools (`read_vehicle_sensor`, `get_mpg`, `activate_garage`, `set_driver`, `diagnose_codes`,
`triage_symptom`, `clear_codes`) are untouched, per instruction 4 and the carve's own ruling.
`get_spend`'s `service_records` half now reads through `FleetSpendController`/`FleetEngineStore`
(cutover-native); its `build_entries` half stays legacy, matching `BuildEntry`'s own deferred
status. Estimates stay labelled - nothing in this cutover touches the `[GUESS]`/`SEEDED`/`LOOKUP`
provenance vocabulary or its spoken caveats.

chunks.text:
- `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest -Pnokey` - green.
- `./gradlew testDebugUnitTest` (real key path) - green.
- `python tools/voice_guide.py` - exit 0, 113 tools, no drift (zero `LiveToolbox.kt` tool

- **New**: `engine/fleet/FleetRecordBridge.kt` (pure conversions - no dedicated test file; exercised

chunks.heading: Cutover 4: Fleet becomes engine-native > Tests, both key ways
chunks.text:
was deliberately changed, not just re-fixtured, and named as a real behavior change rather than a
  fixture nit**: `MaintenanceWritesServiceRecordTest`'s `DONE_AT with a cost but no typed mileage`
  used to assert the anchor's mileage stayed `null` while a `ServiceRecord` alone carried the

chunks.heading: Cutover 5: the widget pager becomes the app's home
chunks.text:
Owed by `.scratch/aspect-engine/issues/22-cutover-per-aspect.md` point 4 ("The pager becomes the
app home ... MainActivity's fate"), the last open item on that ticket now that cutovers 1-4 have
each landed and been merged (`cutover1-2026-08-24.md` through `cutover4-2026-08-24.md`). Written
before this doc's own author claims the branch is done, per CLAUDE.md §8's L11 - the same
discipline the four prior cutover docs already set, and the worked example this doc follows.

**This is the smallest of the five cutovers by lines changed, and the one with the widest blast
radius by definition** - it is the one branch that touches what every session opens the app onto.

chunks.heading: Cutover 5: the widget pager becomes the app's home > The flip mechanism, and why
chunks.text:
**Chosen: MainActivity hosts the pager as an ordinary `composable(LegionRoute.DASHBOARD)`
destination inside its existing `NavHost`, as its new `startDestination`. `WidgetPagerActivity` -
the separate, `exported="false"`, `adb shell am start`-only Activity ticket 18 shipped the pager
behind - is DELETED.**

**Rejected: moving the `LAUNCHER` `<intent-filter>` to `WidgetPagerActivity` and making it the
real entry point.** `MainActivity.onCreate`/`onNewIntent`/`onResume` carry real, load-bearing
lifecycle wiring that has nothing to do with which screen is on top:

- `readDeepLinkExtras` - `EXTRA_ROUTE` (five live callers: `LedgerIngestService`,
  `LiveSessionController` x3, `ReminderAlarmReceiver`) and `ReminderAlarmReceiver.EXTRA_OPEN_ITEM_ID`.
- The Spotify OAuth redirect (`com.kevin.legion://spotify-callback`), consumed via `intent.data` and
  exchanged in a `LaunchedEffect` above the `NavHost`.
- `onResume`'s three real side effects: `AssistantIgnition.resumeIfEnabled` (the foreground-service
  microphone-type re-promotion), `LocationController.init` (permission-grant-return detection),
  `SyncEngine.maybeAutoSync`, `SpotifyController.connectSilently`.
- `android:launchMode="singleTask"`, required for the Spotify redirect to land in `onNewIntent`
  rather than spawn a second instance.
- "Hey Google, ask LEGION X" (`MEDIA_PLAY_FROM_SEARCH`), also filtered on this Activity.

Making `WidgetPagerActivity` the launcher would mean either duplicating every one of those (a
second, competing copy of lifecycle wiring that already drifted once when `SavedPlacesActivity`/
`LedgerImportActivity`/`PantryImportActivity` existed as separate Activities - ticket 07's own
resolution deleted them for exactly this reason) or routing all of it through a second Activity
that would need `MainActivity`'s own private mutable state, which is not exported. **Hosting the
pager AS a `NavHost` destination inside the Activity that already owns all of this wiring makes the
flip a route-table change, not a lifecycle-wiring change** - zero lines of `onCreate`/`onNewIntent`/
`onResume` touched, and every one of the five `EXTRA_ROUTE` callers above needed zero changes,
confirmed by grep (`docs/architecture/cutover5-2026-08-24.md`'s own verification below).

not sampled.

chunks.heading: Cutover 5: the widget pager becomes the app's home > Voice ignition, wake word, proactive raises, notifications - verified unaffected
chunks.text:
Grepped every `MainActivity`/`EXTRA_ROUTE` reference outside `MainActivity.kt` itself:

```
service/DatesReminderAlarmReceiver.kt:97   Intent(context, MainActivity::class.java)
service/LedgerIngestService.kt:160-161     Intent(this, MainActivity::class.java), EXTRA_ROUTE
service/LiveSessionController.kt:995-1010  Intent(appContext, MainActivity::class.java), EXTRA_ROUTE (x3: places, ledger import, pantry import)
service/ReminderAlarmReceiver.kt:124-129   Intent(context, MainActivity::class.java), EXTRA_ROUTE = LegionRoute.NOTES
service/TelephonyController.kt:238         Intent(context, MainActivity::class.java)

Every one targets `MainActivity` by class, not a route string that assumes what the start
destination is - `readDeepLinkExtras`/`LegionShell`'s `LaunchedEffect(deepLinkNonce)` navigate
explicitly to whatever `EXTRA_ROUTE` says, and a caller with no `EXTRA_ROUTE` at all (the first and
last above) simply lands wherever the `NavHost`'s `startDestination` is now - `DASHBOARD` instead
of `TODAY`, which is the flip working as intended, not a break. **Zero of these five call sites
needed a code change.** Wake word / voice ignition itself lives entirely in
`AriaForegroundService`/`GeminiLiveSession`, neither of which references `MainActivity` or any
`LegionRoute` constant at all (grep-confirmed) - the assistant's own ignition path is orthogonal to
which screen the Activity's `NavHost` opens onto.

chunks.heading: Cutover 5: the widget pager becomes the app's home > The two hands paths this branch adds, and the one gap it does NOT close
chunks.text:
**`WidgetPagerRoot(onOpenRoute: (String) -> Unit)`** is the new seam - the pager reaches outside
itself the same way every other top-level screen in this app's `NavHost` already does (a plain
callback up to `LegionShell`, which calls `navController.navigate`), never by owning its own
`NavHostController`. Two callers wired this branch:

1. **The HOME page's "CLASSIC" button** (only rendered on page 0) - `onOpenRoute(LegionRoute.TODAY)`.
   Named CLASSIC because it is genuinely the old Today panel, unmodified, carrying capabilities the
   seeded HOME arrangement does not yet replicate: the ALERTS pane (quarantined-file count, tap-
   through to Money), the Gemini-key advisory row, and the media mini-bar's own tap-through to the
   Spotify panel. `DefaultArrangementSeeder`'s own doc comment already named TODAY -> HOME as its
   mapping target; this button is the honest acknowledgment that the mapping is not yet 1:1.
2. **Each aspect page's "OPEN FULL SCREEN" button**, present only when `legacyRouteForAspect(aspect
   .name)` resolves - a plain `when` keyed against the exact `ASPECT_NAME` string literal each of
   `engine/fleet/FleetAspectSeeder.kt`/`engine/ledger/LedgerAspectSeeder.kt`/
   `engine/pantry/PantryAspectSeeder.kt`/`engine/notes/NotesAspectSeeder.kt`/
   `engine/places/PlacesAspectSeeder.kt` seeds (`Fleet`/`Ledger`/`Pantry`/`Notes`/`Places` ->
   `FLEET`/`MONEY`/`MONEY_PANTRY`/`NOTES`/`FLEET_PLACES`), pinned by `LegionRouteTest`'s own test
   against those seeders' real constants rather than a second, hand-typed copy of the strings. This
   is the hands path to capabilities the generic engine widgets do not yet carry - statement/receipt
   ingestion, the OBD live views, settings screens embedded in the legacy Fleet/Notes/Ledger
   screens.

**The Dates aspect and any user-created aspect carry no such button, correctly** - `Dates` is
genuinely new (CLAUDE.md §10/ticket 19: it never had a pre-existing legacy screen to link to, so
this is not a capability the cutover removed), and a driver-created aspect from the pager's own "+"
page never had one either.

chunks.heading: Cutover 5: the widget pager becomes the app's home > The two hands paths this branch adds, and the one gap it does NOT close
chunks.text:
**A gap this branch did NOT introduce, found while building it, and explicitly out of this
branch's scope: no engine widget navigates anywhere on tap.** `RecordListWidget`/`StatTileWidget`/
`AgendaWidget`/`SingleRecordCardWidget`/`ChartWidget` (`ui/widgets/EngineWidgets.kt`) are all
read-only renders with zero `onClick`/`clickable` in the file (grep-confirmed), and `QUICK_ADD`'s
own `onAdd` callback is a literal no-op with a comment pointing at
`ui/generated/GeneratedFormScreen.kt` as the intended destination - unchanged by this branch.
`GeneratedListScreen`/`GeneratedDetailScreen`/`GeneratedFormScreen` (ticket 10's own "already
built" generated screens) are real, working composables, but grep across `app/src/main` shows
**zero live callers wire them into any `NavHost`** - the only place they are ever mounted today is
`GeneratedScreensScreenshotTest`, over a bare `ComponentActivity`. This was already true before
this branch (`WidgetPagerActivity` never wired them either), so it is not a regression this cutover
caused, but it IS the reason the aspect pages' own widgets cannot yet be each aspect's ONLY
drilldown path - the "OPEN FULL SCREEN" button above is what actually carries that weight today.
**Genuinely owed, named rather than silently worked around**: a follow-up ticket to give the
generated screens typed nav routes (`records/{recordTypeId}`, `records/{recordTypeId}/{recordId}`)
and wire `RECORD_LIST`/`SINGLE_RECORD_CARD`/`QUICK_ADD` taps through them. Out of scope here because
it is a nav-argument shape `LegionRoute.kt`'s own doc comment says this file has never needed before
("nothing here takes a navigation argument") - a real design decision, not a quick patch, and
exactly the kind of unscoped touch CLAUDE.md's working model asks an executing agent to stop and
surface rather than improvise.

chunks.heading: Cutover 5: the widget pager becomes the app's home > Default arrangements beyond HOME - deliberately not extended this branch
chunks.text:
`DefaultArrangementSeeder.seedHomeIfEmpty` seeds only the HOME page (`aspectId = null`); none of the
five real aspect pages (Fleet/Ledger/Pantry/Notes/Places) get a seeded arrangement, so a fresh
device's aspect pages read "NOTHING PLACED ON THIS PAGE YET" until a driver places a widget by
hand. **Deliberately not extended in this branch**, for two reasons stated rather than assumed
away: first, a reasonable per-aspect seed needs a real `FieldDef`/`RecordType` id to point a
`STAT_TILE`/`RECORD_LIST` at, and guessing one risks seeding a widget that reads as authoritative
over a field nobody chose (the same "not configured yet, in words" discipline the HOME seed's own
doc comment already holds itself to for `STAT_TILE`/`QUICK_ADD`); second, every aspect page already
has a real, working fallback today - the "OPEN FULL SCREEN" button this branch adds. The empty
state is honest, not broken: it says nothing has been placed, because nothing has, and one tap away
is the exact same full-capability screen that page's tab used to be. Extending the seeder with real
per-aspect defaults (mirroring `TODAY`'s BIO/CRED/FLEET/LOG half-tile row, ticket 08's own answer)
is a named follow-up, not a silent gap.

chunks.heading: Cutover 5: the widget pager becomes the app's home > Postscript, 2026-08-25: reverted after a night of real use
chunks.text:
**Kevin's own arc on this cutover, stated plainly rather than smoothed over**: "i like it" on
first look at the pager as HOME, then - after actually living with it overnight on the A25 -
"home screen > kill it, revert everything to classic." Both were genuine reactions at the time
they were said; the second is the one that governs. This is not a case of the first cutover being
wrong on arrival - the pager, its eight widget kinds, `DeckGrid`'s edit mode, and the per-aspect
pages all worked exactly as built and went through seven on-device grid-feel rounds before this
branch ever flipped HOME onto them. What field use showed is narrower: as an every-open HOME
surface, seeded arrangements read thinner than the old `TodayScreen` panel they were modelled on
(this doc's own "Default arrangements beyond HOME" section named that gap at the time, and it is
the gap Kevin felt).

**The revert, same shape as the flip itself - a route-table change, not a deletion.**
`LegionRoute.TODAY` is `NavHost`'s `startDestination` and the HOME hard key's target again, exactly
the pre-cutover-5 shape this doc's own "before" column recorded. `LegionRoute.DASHBOARD` (the
pager) is NOT deleted and NOT code-orphaned: it stays a real, reachable `composable` destination,
demoted from HOME/hard-key/start-destination down to a single **"DASHBOARD" button on
`TodayScreen`** (ui/TodayScreen.kt (deleted 2026-09-01, one-today ticket 07), a lone row at the top of the agenda list, deliberately not
inside the HERO pane's own whole-pane click target) - the mirror image of the "CLASSIC" button this
cutover added to the pager's HOME page, which is now removed as pointless (TODAY is home again, one
tap - or the back button - away from anyone who reaches the pager at all). This keeps the pager a
real hands path (ADR 0035) to the aspect engine's generic widgets rather than orphaning the seven
on-device rounds it went through.

chunks.heading: Cutover 5: the widget pager becomes the app's home > Postscript, 2026-08-25: reverted after a night of real use
chunks.text:
**The aspect-add bug, found while reverting, was real and is now fixed.** Kevin also reported
"adding an aspect doesn't work." Tracing it: this cutover's own "Cleanup" section never mentioned
the pager's own "+" page because that page was untouched by the home flip - the bug predates this
branch and was simply surfaced by using the app. `AddAspectPage` (`ui/widgets/WidgetPagerScreen.kt`)
was exactly the stub ticket 18's own report named it as ("stub screen is fine this pass"): it wrote
a bare `Aspect` row and NOTHING else - no `RecordType`, no `FieldDef`. A driver who tapped CREATE

chunks.heading: Harvest: what ui/generated/ knew before it was deleted
chunks.text:
> **Why this file exists.** 596 lines under ui/generated/ solved the problem of rendering an
> arbitrary record shape into Compose without crashing, and validating it before committing. ADR
> 0039-per-aspect-typed-tables retires them and backend-erp phase 6 deletes them. This is the
> transferable half, written down so the generated-ui renderer's builder does not rediscover it.
> Source: generated-ui ticket 07.
>
> **The three source paths in this document are deliberately NOT in backticks.** `tools/docs_check.py`
> resolves backticked package-relative Kotlin paths and fails when one does not exist. These files
> are scheduled for deletion, so backticking them would plant a check failure timed to phase 6.

| File | Lines | Role |
|---|---|---|
| ui/generated/GeneratedFormScreen.kt | 293 | One editor per field type, two-layer validation |
| ui/generated/GeneratedDetailScreen.kt | 161 | Rendering an arbitrary record's fields |
| ui/generated/GeneratedListScreen.kt | 142 | Rendering an arbitrary record type as a list |

---

chunks.heading: Harvest: what ui/generated/ knew before it was deleted > 1. The field-type-to-editor mapping
chunks.text:
Thirteen `FieldType` values, and the `when` over them is **exhaustive with no `else` branch**. That
is the single most transferable decision here: adding a fourteenth type is a compile error at every
render site, not a silent blank on a screen. Keep that property in the new renderer even though its
input is a UI schema rather than a data schema.

| Field type | Editor | Display form | Note worth carrying |
|---|---|---|---|
| TEXT, LOCATION | text field | raw string | LOCATION had no map picker; it was a string, honestly |
| NUMBER, RATING | text field, `toDoubleOrNull()` | `Double.toString()` | An unparseable keystroke writes `null`, not a stale prior value |
| MONEY_CENTS | text field labelled "(dollars)" | sign + `abs/100` + zero-padded remainder | **Displays dollars, stores `Long` cents.** `Math.round(dollars * 100.0)` at the boundary. CLAUDE.md section 4 rule 3 lives or dies in this one line |
| DATE, DATETIME | text field of epoch ms + a NOW button | `SimpleDateFormat("MMM d, yyyy")` | Raw epoch ms in a text box was a placeholder and always read as one. **Do not carry this forward** |
| BOOLEAN | switch | "YES" / "NO" | |
| CHOICE | radio group from `FieldConfig.choiceOptions` | string | Empty options renders "NO OPTIONS CONFIGURED" in quarantine colour, not an empty box |
| MULTI_SELECT_CHOICE | checkbox group | - | Value is `List<String>`; add/remove by set arithmetic |
| REFERENCE | radio group over candidate records | "Record #id" | Candidates loaded per-field in its own `LaunchedEffect`. Labelling a reference by id rather than by the target's title field is a **known weakness**, not a pattern |
| PHOTO | camera launcher, `EnginePhotoStore.save` | "PHOTO ON FILE" | Stores a path in the payload, never bytes |
| COMPUTED | **none - never user-editable** | value, or its error in words | Filtered out at the caller AND unreachable-branched inside the editor. Belt and braces on purpose |

chunks.heading: Harvest: what ui/generated/ knew before it was deleted > 1. The field-type-to-editor mapping > The four "unknown shape" cases, and what each one renders
chunks.text:
None of them throws, and none renders empty. This is the part to copy verbatim in spirit:

1. **Unconfigured choice field** - "NO OPTIONS CONFIGURED", quarantine colour.
2. **Unconfigured reference field** - "NOT CONFIGURED".
3. **Configured reference with no targets yet** - "NO CANDIDATE RECORDS YET", faint, *not*
   quarantine. A different sentence for a different condition; an empty result and a broken config
   are not the same fact. This mirrors CLAUDE.md section 1's "unreadable and empty are different
   sentences".
4. **Record not found** - "RECORD NOT FOUND", quarantine colour, rather than a blank scaffold.

Distinct loading and empty states throughout: `loaded` is its own boolean, never inferred from an
empty list. And "no records yet" versus "no records match '<query>'" are separate strings.

---

chunks.heading: Harvest: what ui/generated/ knew before it was deleted > 2. The validation layering
chunks.text:
Two layers, deliberately unequal, and the split is the lesson.

**Layer 1 - `engine/GeneratedFormValidation.kt` (pure).** No Compose import, no DAO, no
`RecordStore` call. A plain function of already-collected form state, so it unit-tests without
Robolectric. Catches only what the form can know by itself:

- a required field absent or blank
- a value whose runtime Kotlin type does not match its field type (`shapeMatches`)

It skips COMPUTED entirely and returns per-field errors in field order. Empty list means clean
enough to *attempt* a submit.

**Layer 2 - `engine/RecordStore.kt` (authoritative).** Only a real DAO read can answer whether a
reference target still exists or a field was deleted, so those checks live at the write door and
nowhere else. The form deliberately does **not** duplicate them.

The load-bearing property: **layer 1 never claims to be sufficient.** A form that passes it can
still come back `WriteResult.Failure`, and the screen renders that failure the same way it renders a
validation error - a worded banner, "COULD NOT SAVE: <reason>", never a raw exception, never a
silent no-op. Same rule as CLAUDE.md section 4: a check that could pass vacuously is not the gate;
the gate is at the write door.

**Carry this shape.** Cheap offline check for fast feedback, authoritative check at the single write
door, both surfaced in the same words. What must not happen is layer 1 growing database access to
"help" - that is how two validators start disagreeing.

---

chunks.heading: Harvest: what ui/generated/ knew before it was deleted > 3. Provenance and computed errors on a generated surface
chunks.text:
Two rules that were applied here specifically because the surface was generated, and generated
surfaces are exactly where a rule gets forgotten:

- **Provenance in words, never colour alone.** `provenanceWord()` maps to "DETERMINISTIC", "LLM
  RECONCILED", "UNRECONCILED - NOT VERIFIED", "HAND-ENTERED". CLAUDE.md section 4 rule 7 explicitly
  says every surface rendering a provisional row says so *in words*. A generated screen is a surface.
- **A computed-field error is rendered, not swallowed.** `renderFieldValue` returns the error string
  plus an `isError` flag, and the detail screen prints it in quarantine colour rather than showing a
  bare dash. Section 4 rule 6 read onto a generated surface: an unrecognised value is a hard, visible
  failure, never a skip.

---

chunks.heading: Harvest: what ui/generated/ knew before it was deleted > 4. The plugin escape hatch
chunks.text:
`GeneratedDetailScreen` takes `pluginOverride: (@Composable (recordId: Long) -> Unit)?`. When
non-null it renders and **returns immediately** - the generated screen below is never composed, so a
record type with a hand-built native detail (a car with live OBD) pays nothing for the fallback it
does not use. This is ADR 0035's hands-path rule with an opt-out that costs zero.

It had no production caller as of writing; only `GeneratedScreensTest` exercised it. Worth carrying
as a pattern, worth knowing it was never load-bearing in practice.

---

chunks.heading: Harvest: what ui/generated/ knew before it was deleted > 5. What does NOT transfer
chunks.text:
Listed explicitly so nobody ports it by habit.

- **The input is a DATA schema.** Every screen here reads `field_defs` and derives the UI from field
  types. The generated-ui renderer's input is a **UI schema** the model emits. Do not carry the
  `FieldDef`-scan shape; carry the exhaustive-`when` discipline that surrounds it.
- **Direct DAO access from the composable.** Each screen builds `CarDatabase.getDatabase(context)`
  and queries inside `LaunchedEffect`. Acceptable at this scale, wrong for a renderer whose numbers
  must come from tool results (ticket 02's binding contract), not from its own reads.
- **Epoch-ms text boxes for dates.** A placeholder that shipped. The new renderer needs a real
  picker.
- **"Record #<id>" as a human label.** Used for reference options and linked-record rows. Titles
  should come from the target's own title field.
- **`titleFor` duplicated from `WidgetDataSource`.** Copied because the original was `private`. Two
  copies of a title rule is one more than the new renderer should have.
- **Client-side filter and sort over a fully-loaded list**, with `PAGE_SIZE = 20` growing an
  in-memory window. Justified at 400 rows on one phone. It is not a pattern to carry to a
  server-backed multi-client world where the row count is not bounded by one household.

chunks.text:
- **Dies into meta-tools** - pure record CRUD (create/read/update/list a fact the user stated)
  that the nine meta-tools (`list_aspects`/`describe_aspect`/`query_records`/`create_record`/
  `update_record`/`delete_record`/`aspect_clerk`) already do generically, once that domain's data
  actually lives in the engine's `aspects`/`record_types`/`field_defs`/`records` tables instead of
  its own hand-rolled entity. **Deleting one of these tools today would be premature** - the
  underlying domain (fleet/ledger/pantry/body/goals/notes) has not been migrated onto the engine
  yet (CLAUDE.md §10's "migration-wave work", ticket 16's own brief: "do NOT rewire ledger/pantry
  onto it yet"). This bucket names what CAN eventually die, not what dies today.
- **Survives as a native verb** - not record CRUD at all: a live hardware read (OBD), a physical
  action (garage relay, a phone call), a read-through of something the app is explicitly forbidden
  to store (mail, calendar - CLAUDE.md §7's read-through-only rule), a domain-specialist dispatch
  (`ask_fleet` and its four siblings), or app/assistant control. No generic CRUD tool could ever
  replace these - they call a controller, a socket, or a specialist sub-agent, not a table.
- **Needs a call** - genuinely ambiguous: real CRUD in shape, but wrapped in domain-specific
  business logic a generic `create_record`/`update_record` cannot reproduce without either losing
  that logic or duplicating it - the ledger reconciliation gate (CLAUDE.md §4), OBD-derived
  maintenance-interval math, VIN decoding, computed due-dates. Whether that logic moves INTO the
  engine (as a capability-plugin hook, ticket 11's own unbuilt API) or stays outside it and the
  tool survives natively is a decision for whichever ticket runs that domain's migration wave, not
  this one. Listed here, not silently assumed either way.

Owed by `.scratch/aspect-engine/issues/21-migration-waves.md` point 2 ("per-aspect carve...
produced per wave before its build starts") and ticket 11 answer point 5 (the per-plugin
inventory table, deferred to be enumerated per wave). Written before any code in this wave, per

chunks.heading: Wave 1 carve: notes, lists, and places onto the engine > The finding that reshapes this carve
chunks.text:
**Notes and Lists are not two domains in the live code - they already collapsed into one, before
this map was ever charted.** `.scratch/notes-lists-calendar/` (a prior, separate effort) ran
`MIGRATION_9_10` and `MIGRATION_12_13`, which folded every named list and `CarTask` and
`PlaceReminder` into a single flat model: one `ItemList` row (`NotesController.theList`, "there is
exactly one... dissolve the car list. merge everything into one list model", Kevin 2026-08-11) and
every item a row in `ListItem` - checklist, note line, or reminder (time- or place-triggered) all
the same shape, distinguished only by which optional columns are populated. `car_tasks` and
`place_reminders` are **dead tables**: traced (`grep`, confirmed by reading `ReminderController.kt`
and `TelemetryRecorder.kt`) - nothing in live code writes a new row into either one anymore.
`car_tasks` gets nothing but a tombstone-purge sweep; `place_reminders` gets nothing but a stale
count read by `LogDigestBuilder` for a log line. Both tables stay in place (untouched, per this
wave's no-destructive-step rule) but are **not** a migration source - migrating them again would
either double-count content the `ItemList`/`ListItem` migration already carries, or copy rows a
prior migration already superseded.

This is not a contradiction of ticket 21's assumptions serious enough to block the wave (the
ticket authorizes exactly this kind of per-entity carve call: record type, plugin-internal, or
dies), but it changes the shape from "three aspects" to **two**: one **Notes** aspect absorbing
both notes and lists, one **Places** aspect. Flagged here in writing rather than silently decided.

chunks.heading: Wave 1 carve: notes, lists, and places onto the engine > What the copier does and does not copy
chunks.text:
- **Copies:** every `ListItem` row `WHERE deleted = 0` (via `ListItemDao.allActive()`, which
  already reads across every legacy `ItemList` - matching the live app's own "one list" reality),
  and every `TaggedPlace` row `WHERE deleted = 0` (via `PlaceDao.getAll()`).
- **Does not copy tombstoned rows.** A `deleted = 1` row is already gone from every user-facing
  surface today; carrying it into the engine as a live OR a trashed `EngineRecord` adds fidelity
  nobody can observe, and the old table's own tombstone-GC sweep still reclaims it regardless of
  whether this wave ever ran. Stated as a deliberate scope cut, not an oversight.
- **Preserves timestamps exactly, in one atomic write.** `RecordStore.create` takes an explicit
  `updatedAt` parameter (defaulting to `now`, senior review 2026-08-23) precisely so a source row
  whose `createdAt` and `updatedAt` differ lands both in a SINGLE call - `now = source.createdAt`,
  `updatedAt = source.updatedAt`. The first cut of this copier used `create` then a conditional
  `update()` to bump `updatedAt` separately; that left a real crash window (a row could exist with
  `updatedAt == createdAt` forever if the process died between the two calls, and the per-row
  `guid` idempotency check would then treat it as "already copied" on every retry, freezing the
  wrong timestamp in place). A single call has no such window. `TaggedPlace` has only one clock
  column (`timestamp`), used for both, so its copier simply never passes `updatedAt` at all.
- **Provenance is `USER`** for every copied row, both aspects - every source row here was voice- or
  hand-entered, never document-extracted, so CLAUDE.md §4's reconciliation gate does not apply
  (same reasoning `CalendarImportController`'s own doc comment already states for its
  `DETERMINISTIC` rows: a straight field-by-field copy has no stated total to reconcile against;
  here it is not even an ingestion path at all, just a storage-location change for data the user
  already owns).
- **Identity.** `ListItem.syncId` is already a stable, per-row UUID minted for exactly this kind of
  cross-device identity purpose (`ListItem`'s own `syncId` column doc, same shape as
  `EngineRecord.guid`) - reused directly as the copied record's `guid`, so a Notes item's identity
  is unchanged by the copy. `TaggedPlace` carries no such column; its copied record's `guid` is

chunks.heading: Wave 1 carve: notes, lists, and places onto the engine > What the copier does and does not copy
chunks.text:
derived deterministically from `label` (`UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes`), a real natural key rather than
  a fresh random UUID, so a second run of the copier (even one recovering from a mid-loop crash
  before the completion flag was set) can recognize and skip a row it already created instead of
  duplicating it - see the migration copier's own doc comment for the two-layer idempotency this
  buys.

chunks.heading: Wave 1 carve: notes, lists, and places onto the engine > Voice tools: what stays, what the carve marks for cutover-time removal only
chunks.text:
Per instruction 4: leave every existing tool working. Nothing is removed, changed, or rewired in
this wave. Named here only as the inventory ticket 11 point 5 deferred, so cutover (a later wave)
knows what it is retiring:

| Tool (in `service/LiveToolbox.kt`) | Backs onto | Dies into a meta-tool at cutover? |
|---|---|---|
| `add_item` / item-add family | `NotesController.addItem`/`addItemDue` | Yes - `create_record` against the Notes aspect |
| `manage_item` (tick/untick/remove/rename/etc.) | `NotesController.tick`/`untick`/`removeItem`/`renameItem` | Yes - `update_record`/`delete_record` |
| `set_reminder` | `ReminderController.add` (itself a thin wrapper over `NotesController`) | Yes - `create_record` with `triggerPlaceLabel` set |
| Place-tagging tools (`tag_place`/similar) | `PlaceController` | Yes - `create_record`/`update_record` against Places |
| `AlarmScheduler`-driven notification/missed-item surfaces | `notes/AlarmScheduler.kt` | **No** - alarm scheduling is native OS integration (`AlarmManager`), stays a plugin worker regardless of cutover; only the record STORAGE moves to the engine, the scheduling mechanism does not become a meta-tool. |

1. **Cutover per aspect** (ticket 14 point 2) is explicitly NOT this wave's job - old screens

2. **Uniqueness on `label`** (Places) is not engine-enforced in v1 - flagged above, not blocking
   this wave since the old `PlaceController`/`PlaceDao.upsert` remains the live write path.
3. **`ItemList`/`CarTask`/`place_reminders` are not dropped.** They stay exactly as they are today;
   this wave adds new tables' worth of DATA (rows in `aspects`/`record_types`/`field_defs`/
   `records`), not a schema change to any existing table.

**Kevin ruled 2026-08-23: ONE aspect.** Notes and lists stay a single Notes aspect and a single pager page; widgets filter by field where a list-only view is wanted. The reviewer-flagged fork is closed.

chunks.heading: Wave 2 carve: pantry onto the engine
chunks.text:
Owed by `.scratch/aspect-engine/issues/21-migration-waves.md` point 2 ("per-aspect carve... produced
per wave before its build starts") and ticket 11 answer point 5 (the per-plugin inventory table).
Written before any code in this wave, following [Wave 1's carve](wave1-carve-2026-08-23.md)'s own
shape and reusing its reasoning rather than repeating it.

chunks.heading: Wave 2 carve: pantry onto the engine > The finding that reshapes this carve: there is no quarantine state to migrate
chunks.text:
CLAUDE.md §4/§5 v3 note both call out that every `PantryReceipt`/`PantryLineItem` row is
LLM-extracted by construction. Read to its leaf (`pantry/PantryReceiptAgent.kt`,
`pantry/PantryController.kt`), that construction is stronger than "no `ingestMethod` column" - **the
gate is enforced upstream of Room, not inside it.** `PantryReceiptAgent.parseAndReconcile` returns a
sealed `PantryIngestResult`: `Success` (money reconciled exactly against the receipt's own printed
subtotal/tax/total, per CLAUDE.md §4 rules 2 and 6) or `Quarantined` (a worded reason string, no
data). `PantryController.importReceipt` only ever calls `pantryReceiptDao().insert()` /
`pantryLineItemDao().insertAll()` inside the `Success` branch - a `Quarantined` result returns
straight back to the caller as a failed `PantryImportResult` and **nothing is written to Room at
all**. There is no `quarantined_receipts` table, no quarantine flag column, no soft-delete/tombstone
column on either entity (confirmed by reading `PantryReceipt.kt`, `PantryLineItem.kt`,
`PantryReceiptDao.kt`, `PantryLineItemDao.kt` in full - neither DAO exposes a delete or an
update). **Every row this migration will ever find already passed the gate by the time it reached
disk.** The only artifact of a quarantined attempt is the source photo, left in place on
`PantryPhotoStore` for the user to retry from - not a Room row, not this wave's concern.

Consequence for this wave: point 2's "if the legacy schema has quarantine state, quarantined rows
are NOT migrated as clean records" has no work to do here - there is no quarantine state IN the
schema to find. Provenance for every migrated row is unconditionally `RecordProvenance.LLM_RECONCILED`
(never `USER`, unlike Wave 1's notes/places copy, and never conditional on a per-row flag that does
not exist).

chunks.heading: Wave 2 carve: pantry onto the engine > The carve table
chunks.text:
| Entity (table) | Live? | Carve | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PantryReceipt` (`pantry_receipts`) | Yes, primary | **Becomes the `Receipt` record type in a new `Pantry` aspect** | The reconciled receipt header - store, date, currency, printed total. |
| `PantryLineItem` (`pantry_line_items`) | Yes, primary | **Becomes the `LineItem` record type in the same `Pantry` aspect**, referencing `Receipt` | One line item per gated receipt row, plus the four LLM macro estimates. |
| `PantryPhotoStore` (filesystem, `pantry_receipts/` dir) | Yes, plugin-internal | **Stays plugin-internal - not migrated, not touched** | Ingestion-only staging: a photo lands here before extraction and is deleted on success (`PantryPhotoStore.delete`, called from `PantryController.importReceipt`'s `Success` branch) or kept on a quarantine for retry. By the time a `PantryReceipt` row exists to migrate, its own photo is almost always **already gone** - `PantryReceipt.sourceImagePath`'s own doc comment says exactly this: "kept as a text record of provenance, not a live reference." There is nothing live here for a migration to carry into `EnginePhotoStore` (the engine-native photo store `data/EnginePhotoStore.kt` already ships for `FieldType.PHOTO` on other record types) - only a path string, which the `Receipt.sourceImagePath` field below carries as-is. |
| `LedgerCurrency` (`SGD`/`USD` enum, shared with ledger) | Yes | **Not its own record type - becomes a `FieldType.CHOICE` field value on `Receipt`** | Same enum ledger already uses; the engine has no first-class currency type (`FieldConfig`'s vocabulary is TEXT/NUMBER/MONEY_CENTS/DATE/DATETIME/BOOLEAN/CHOICE/MULTI_SELECT_CHOICE/REFERENCE/PHOTO/LOCATION/RATING/COMPUTED, locked at ticket 03), so `CHOICE` with options `["SGD", "USD"]` is the closest fit and is what `RecordType`/`FieldDef`'s existing vocabulary offers. |

No entity here is "dead" the way `car_tasks`/`place_reminders` were in Wave 1 - pantry is a small,
young aspect (2026-07-31) with no prior absorption history to trace through.

chunks.heading: Wave 2 carve: pantry onto the engine > Field mapping: `PantryReceipt` -> Pantry aspect, `Receipt` record type
chunks.text:
Owner plugin id: `"pantry"`. Locked+required: `store`, `purchaseDate`, `currency`, `total` - the
four facts the reconciliation gate itself verified or requires before a row can exist at all.
`sourceImagePath` is NOT required/locked (see reasoning below).

chunks.heading: Wave 2 carve: pantry onto the engine > Field mapping: `PantryReceipt` -> Pantry aspect, `Receipt` record type
chunks.text:
| `PantryReceipt` column | Field name | `FieldType` | Required/locked | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `store` | `store` | TEXT | yes | |
| `purchaseDate` | `purchaseDate` | DATETIME | yes | **Not wired as `primaryDueDateFieldId`.** A past grocery purchase date is not an agenda-shaped "due" the way a Notes reminder or a Dates event is - promoting it would put every historical receipt into a cross-aspect agenda meant for upcoming, actionable items. Deliberate scope cut, stated rather than defaulted into. |
| `currency` | `currency` | CHOICE | yes | Options `["SGD", "USD"]` - `LedgerCurrency`'s own two values, duplicated as plain strings rather than a dependency on that enum, same "engine package never depends on a plugin package" reasoning `NotesAspectSeeder.REPEAT_KIND_OPTIONS`'s own doc comment states for `notes/RepeatKind`. |

Storing it as TEXT keeps the provenance string (matches the legacy column's own stated purpose - "a text record of provenance, not a live reference") without implying a photo picker UI should try to render a file that in the overwhelming case does not exist. chunks.text: | `id` | - | - | - | Not carried as a field. Its ENGINE identity (the new `EngineRecord.id`) is what `LineItem.receipt` below references - see the copier's own doc comment for why line items must be copied strictly after their receipt. |

chunks.heading: Wave 2 carve: pantry onto the engine > Field mapping: `PantryLineItem` -> Pantry aspect, `LineItem` record type
chunks.text:
Owner plugin id: `"pantry"`. Locked+required: `receipt`, `name`, `quantity`, `totalPrice` - the
fields present on every gate-reconciled row. The four macro fields are estimates by construction
(CLAUDE.md §4 rule 5) and are named with an `estimated` prefix rather than described as one, because
**`FieldDef` carries no separate description column** (confirmed by reading `FieldDef.kt` in
full) - `ui/generated/GeneratedFormScreen.kt:148` renders `fd.name` directly as the field's on-screen
label (`fd.name + if (fd.required) " *" else ""`), so the field NAME is the only user-facing string
this schema layer has, and it is the one CLAUDE.md §4 rule 5 requires to say "estimate."

chunks.heading: Wave 2 carve: pantry onto the engine > Field mapping: `PantryLineItem` -> Pantry aspect, `LineItem` record type
chunks.text:
| `PantryLineItem` column | Field name | `FieldType` | Required/locked | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|

This is the wave's one genuinely new engine-schema shape: no prior wave declared a `REFERENCE` field ([`RecordStoreTest`](../../app/src/test/java/com/kevin/legion/engine/RecordStoreTest.kt) exercises `REFERENCE`/`CASCADE` against hand-built test schemas only; this is the first REAL aspect to use it). |

| `totalPriceCents` | `totalPrice` | MONEY_CENTS | yes | **Wired as `primaryAmountFieldId`** on `LineItem` - this is the figure the gate itself verified (`sum(items) == subtotal`), so it is exactly the promotable "amount" for this record type. |
| `caloriesKcal` | `estimatedCaloriesKcal` | NUMBER | no | ESTIMATE - see this section's header note. |
| `proteinG` | `estimatedProteinG` | NUMBER | no | ESTIMATE. |
| `carbsG` | `estimatedCarbsG` | NUMBER | no | ESTIMATE. |
| `fatG` | `estimatedFatG` | NUMBER | no | ESTIMATE. |

except `LOCATION`, `RATING`, and `COMPUTED`, none of which pantry needs).

chunks.heading: Wave 2 carve: pantry onto the engine > Reconciliation status, quarantine, and provenance
chunks.text:
- **Provenance is unconditionally `RecordProvenance.LLM_RECONCILED`** for every `Receipt` and every
  `LineItem` this migration writes - never `USER`, never conditional on inspecting any column,
  because (per the finding above) there is no other kind of row this table can hold. This is
  CLAUDE.md §5's v3 note ("every row is LLM-extracted by construction") carried forward literally:
  the migration does not RE-DERIVE provenance, it STATES what was already true before the row ever
  reached Room.
- **Money is carried as `Long` cents, unchanged, at every step** - `totalCents`/`unitPriceCents`/
  `totalPriceCents` copy straight through with no floating-point conversion, matching CLAUDE.md §4
  rule 3.
- **Macro estimate fields are copied verbatim, never re-verified** - they were never part of the
  gate to begin with (CLAUDE.md §4 rule 5), and this migration does not invent a check that never
  existed.
- **No quarantine state exists to exclude** - see the finding above. Stated explicitly, not silently
  assumed, per instruction 2's own requirement to say what was found.

chunks.heading: Wave 2 carve: pantry onto the engine > What the copier does and does not copy
chunks.text:
- **Copies every `PantryReceipt` row, unconditionally** (there is no `deleted` column to filter on,
  unlike Wave 1's `ListItem`/`TaggedPlace` - see the carve finding above), via a new
  `PantryReceiptDao.getAll()` query (an additive `@Query`, no schema/version change - it reads the
  same columns `getRecent`/`getAllForCharts` already expose, just without a `LIMIT` or a narrowed
  projection).
- **Copies every `PantryLineItem` STRICTLY AFTER its own receipt has been copied** - a `LineItem`'s
  `receipt` field is a live `FieldType.REFERENCE`, and `RecordStore.create`'s `validateReferences`
  step rejects any reference pointing at a record id that does not yet exist. The copier keeps a
  `legacyReceiptId -> newEngineRecordId` map built while copying receipts, and looks up each line
  item's parent through that map, in the SAME pass (`db.pantryLineItemDao().getForReceipt(receipt.id)`
  per receipt) rather than a single flat query across all line items - this also means a
  line item can never be orphaned mid-migration even if the process dies between a receipt and its
  items (see idempotency below).
- **Preserves timestamps exactly, in one atomic write**, same `RecordStore.create(now =, updatedAt =)`
  shape Wave 1's senior-review fix established - `PantryReceipt` carries no separate
  `createdAt`/`updatedAt` (it was never edited after insert, per its own DAO having no `update`
  method), so both clocks are seeded from `purchaseDate` for the receipt... **correction, resolved
  during implementation:** neither `PantryReceipt` nor `PantryLineItem` carries any insert-time
  clock at all - `purchaseDate` is a USER-STATED fact from the receipt (when the shopping happened),
  not a bookkeeping timestamp for when the row was written to Room. Using it as the engine record's
  `createdAt`/`updatedAt` is the closest available anchor and is what this migration does, stated
  here as a deliberate substitution rather than left implicit - a receipt logged today for a
