chunks.heading: Wave 3 carve: ledger onto the engine
chunks.text:
Owed by `.scratch/aspect-engine/issues/21-migration-waves.md` point 2 ("per-aspect carve... produced
per wave before its build starts") and ticket 11 answer point 5 (the per-plugin inventory table).
Written before any code in this wave, following [Wave 1's carve](wave1-carve-2026-08-23.md) and
[Wave 2's carve](wave2-carve-2026-08-23.md)'s own shape and reusing their reasoning rather than
repeating it. This is the "gate re-plumb" wave named in ticket 14's answer point 1 - the highest-
stakes of the four, because this is the one aspect whose data carries CLAUDE.md §4's reconciliation
provenance for real, including rule 7's provisional rows.

chunks.heading: Wave 3 carve: ledger onto the engine > The finding that reshapes this carve: `ingestMethod` maps directly onto `RecordProvenance`
chunks.text:
`LedgerTransaction.ingestMethod` is `IngestMethod { DETERMINISTIC, LLM_RECONCILED, UNRECONCILED }`.
`RecordProvenance` (`data/local/EngineRecord.kt`) is `{ DETERMINISTIC, LLM_RECONCILED, UNRECONCILED,
USER }`. The first three spellings are IDENTICAL. This was verified by reading both enum
declarations side by side, not assumed from the names alone - `EngineDataMigrationWave3.provenanceFor`
is a plain, exhaustive Kotlin `when` with **no `else` branch**, mapping each of the three
`IngestMethod` values to the identically-named `RecordProvenance` value and nothing else. `USER` is
never produced by this wave - every `LedgerTransaction` row, without exception, came from a document
or a spoken pending-log entry, never a hand-authored record the way Wave 1's `ListItem`/`TaggedPlace`
were.

**On "if other values exist in the column, STOP and surface": traced, not assumed.** No custom
`TypeConverter` for `IngestMethod` exists anywhere in `data/local/` (confirmed by grep) - Room 2.6+'s
native Kotlin-enum column support is what's in play, which means Room itself calls
`IngestMethod.valueOf(...)` while reading a row out of SQLite and **throws before a
`LedgerTransaction` Kotlin instance can ever exist** if the stored string doesn't match one of the
three declared constants. By the time `EngineDataMigrationWave3` holds a `LedgerTransaction` object
in Kotlin, its `ingestMethod` is structurally guaranteed to be one of the three - "a fourth value
reaches the copier" is not a runtime case to defend against, it is a compile-time impossibility once
the row was successfully read at all. Nothing was found that would trip this stop condition, and the
reasoning for why nothing could is written into the copier's own class doc, not merely asserted here.

chunks.heading: Wave 3 carve: ledger onto the engine > The carve table
chunks.text:
| Entity (table) | Live? | Carve | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `LedgerTransaction` (`ledger_transactions`) | Yes, primary | **Becomes the `Transaction` record type in a new `Ledger` aspect** | The reconciled (or provisionally-tagged) transaction row - source file, account, currency, date, description, signed amount, optional running balance, category state. |
| `IngestedFile` (`ingested_files`) | Yes, plugin-internal | **Stays plugin-internal - NOT migrated, NOT becoming a record type** | The per-file ingestion ledger (scan work-avoidance + quarantine reasons + LLM spend audit). Its own doc comment states its identity is deliberately natural-keyed on `driveFileId`, not a generated `syncId` the way every migrated entity so far has had - it does not fit this engine's `guid`-keyed identity model without inventing one, and nothing in ticket 11's plugin inventory calls for it to. It is ingestion machinery, the same category Wave 2's `PantryPhotoStore` carve placed as plugin-internal. `LedgerTransaction.sourceFileId` (below) keeps a plain-text breadcrumb back to it, never a live `FieldType.REFERENCE`. |
| `Category` (`categories`) / `CategoryRule` (`category_rules`) | Yes, plugin-internal | **Stay plugin-internal - NOT migrated** | A fixed-but-editable classification vocabulary and its matching rules, not transaction data. `LedgerTransaction.category` (below) is carried as free TEXT rather than a `FieldType.CHOICE`/`FieldType.REFERENCE` against a migrated `Category` record type - see the field mapping table for why. |

No entity here is "dead" the way `car_tasks`/`place_reminders` were in Wave 1 - ledger has no prior
absorption history to trace through either.

chunks.heading: Wave 3 carve: ledger onto the engine > Field mapping: `LedgerTransaction` -> Ledger aspect, `Transaction` record type
chunks.text:
Owner plugin id: `"ledger"`. Locked+required: `sourceFile`, `accountId`, `currency`, `txnDate`,
`description`, `amount`, `lineRef` - every field a `LedgerTransaction` row carries non-nullably
today. `balance`, `sourceFileId`, `category`, `pendingLoggedAt` are optional, matching their
nullable legacy columns exactly. `categoryPending` is required (it is a non-nullable `Boolean` on
the legacy row, always `false` or `true`, never absent).

chunks.heading: Wave 3 carve: ledger onto the engine > Field mapping: `LedgerTransaction` -> Ledger aspect, `Transaction` record type
chunks.text:
| `LedgerTransaction` column | Field name | `FieldType` | Required/locked | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sourceFile` | `sourceFile` | TEXT | yes | |
| `accountId` | `accountId` | TEXT | yes | |
| `currency` | `currency` | CHOICE | yes | Options `["SGD", "USD"]` - `LedgerCurrency`'s own two values, same duplication-as-plain-strings reasoning `PantryAspectSeeder.CURRENCY_OPTIONS`'s own doc comment states (engine package never depends on a plugin package). |
| `txnDate` | `txnDate` | DATETIME | yes | **Not wired as `primaryDueDateFieldId`.** A settled, past transaction date is not an upcoming, actionable "due" the way a Notes reminder or a Dates event is - the same deliberate scope cut Wave 2's carve states for `PantryReceipt.purchaseDate`, stated here again for the same reason. |
| `description` | `description` | TEXT | yes | |
| `amountCents` | `amount` | MONEY_CENTS | yes | **Wired as `primaryAmountFieldId`** - the transaction's own signed, gate-relevant figure, same "the standard set" promotion reasoning as every prior wave's own primary-amount field. Signed (negative for debit, positive for credit) - carried through unchanged, no sign normalisation. |
| `balanceCents` | `balance` | MONEY_CENTS | no | Legitimately null for source formats with no running-balance column (Bank of America's section layout - see the column's own legacy doc comment). |
| `lineRef` | `lineRef` | TEXT | yes | |
| `sourceFileId` | `sourceFileId` | TEXT | no | **Deliberately plain TEXT, not `FieldType.REFERENCE`** - `ingested_files` is not a migrated record type (see the carve table above), so there is nothing for a REFERENCE field to validate existence against. This is an audit breadcrumb only, carried as-is, including `null` for any row imported before this column existed or through a path that predates the scan pipeline (the legacy column's own doc comment). |

chunks.heading: Wave 3 carve: ledger onto the engine > Field mapping: `LedgerTransaction` -> Ledger aspect, `Transaction` record type
chunks.text:
| `category` | `category` | TEXT | no | **Deliberately plain TEXT, not `FieldType.CHOICE`.** Unlike currency's fixed two-value set, `Category` (`data/local/Category.kt`) is Room-backed and explicitly user-editable ("so the set can be edited later without a schema migration" - that entity's own doc comment) - a `CHOICE` field's `options` list is fixed at seed time (`FieldConfig.serializeChoice`), so it would go stale the first time a category was renamed or added after this aspect was seeded. Carrying it as free text matches the legacy column's own type and defers "should this be a live reference to a migrated Category record type" to the cutover wave, where `Category`/`CategoryRule` migration (if any) would actually be decided. |
| `categoryPending` | `categoryPending` | BOOLEAN | yes | Carried exactly - `false` migrates as `false`, never defaulted or reinterpreted. Ticket 13 of `ledger-drive-ingestion` (`13-categorypending-default-drift.md`) fixed a DEFAULT-value drift on this exact column at the Room-schema level; this migration reads the already-correct in-memory Kotlin value off each row (Room's own default/migration handling already resolved any drift before this copier ever sees a `LedgerTransaction` object) and writes it through unchanged - it is not re-deriving or re-defaulting anything. |
| `pendingLoggedAt` | `pendingLoggedAt` | DATETIME | no | Carried exactly, `null` stays `null`. Non-null means "the user told me about this by voice; no file ever mentioned it" (the legacy column's own doc comment) - this migration does not re-derive or re-interpret that meaning, only copies the timestamp. |
| `syncId` | - | - | - | Reused directly as the migrated record's `guid` - already a stable, per-row UUID minted "for exactly this kind of cross-device identity purpose" (the legacy column's own doc comment), same shape as every prior wave's `syncId` reuse. |
| `id` | - | - | - | Not carried as a field. `Transaction` has no child record type in this engine (unlike Wave 2's `Receipt`/`LineItem` pair), so nothing needs to look up this record's new engine id through a map the way Wave 2's line items did. |

No `DURATION`/`LOCATION`/`RATING`/`PHOTO`/`MULTI_SELECT_CHOICE`/`COMPUTED` field type was needed -
10 of the 13 non-deferred `FieldType` values are enough.

chunks.heading: Wave 3 carve: ledger onto the engine > Reconciliation status, quarantine, and provenance
chunks.text:
- **Provenance maps directly, per-row, from `ingestMethod`** - see the finding above. Never
  upgraded (an `UNRECONCILED` row never becomes `LLM_RECONCILED` by migrating), never collapsed
  (all three stay distinct), never defaulted to `USER`.
- **Money is carried as `Long` cents, unchanged, at every step** - `amountCents`/`balanceCents` copy
  straight through with no floating-point conversion, matching CLAUDE.md §4 rule 3. Sign is
  preserved exactly (a debit stays negative).
- **No quarantine state exists to exclude, and this is a stronger claim than Wave 2's equivalent
  finding, not the same one.** Wave 2 found pantry has NO quarantine state anywhere. Ledger DOES
  have quarantine state (`IngestedFile.state == QUARANTINED`, with a `quarantineReason`) - but it
  lives entirely on `ingested_files`, which is plugin-internal and not migrated (see the carve
  table). **Zero rows are ever written to `ledger_transactions` for a quarantined file** -
  `IngestPipeline.commit`'s `is LedgerIngestResult.Quarantined ->` branch only ever writes to
  `ingestedDao`, never to `txnDao` (read in full, `ledger/IngestPipeline.kt` lines 247-259). So
  every `LedgerTransaction` row this migration will ever find already passed CLAUDE.md §4's gate in
  one of its three legal shapes (rules 1-2 for `DETERMINISTIC`/`LLM_RECONCILED`, rule 7 for
  `UNRECONCILED`) by the time it reached Room - the migration is a faithful COPY of that state, not
  a re-verification of it.

chunks.heading: Wave 3 carve: ledger onto the engine > Rule 7's transience guarantee: where supersession lives, and the dual-copy plan
chunks.text:
**Supersession lives in `ledger/IngestPipeline.commit`, operating directly on the LEGACY
`ledger_transactions` table, inside a `db.withTransaction` block, gated on
`stamped.first().ingestMethod != IngestMethod.UNRECONCILED`** (`IngestPipeline.kt` lines 284-301,
calling `LedgerTransactionDao.deleteSupersededProvisional`). Read in full: when a reconciled
(`DETERMINISTIC`/`LLM_RECONCILED`) statement commits, it first deletes any `UNRECONCILED` rows for
the same card (suffix-matched on the last 4 digits, per `sameCard`) whose `txnDate` falls inside the
incoming statement's own date range - BEFORE reading `getForAccountInRange` for dedup, and INSIDE
the same transaction as the insert, so a crash mid-commit can never leave the account with neither
the provisional nor the reconciled rows. A second deletion path exists alongside it:
`LedgerTransactionDao.deletePendingById` (`clear_pending_transaction`'s voice tool), which removes a
single voice-logged `pendingLoggedAt`-tagged row (also always `UNRECONCILED` - see that column's own
doc comment) once a user says it cleared. **Both of these keep operating on the legacy table only,
unchanged by this wave** - per instruction 5, nothing about `ledger/IngestPipeline` or
`ledger/LedgerController` is touched here.

**This means an engine-side `UNRECONCILED` copy of a provisional row can go stale the moment the
legacy row it was copied from is deleted by either path**, unless something on the engine side is
told to catch up. Two options were on the table, per instruction 2:

1. **The copier is re-runnable per-file/per-call**, and each run reconciles supersession itself.
2. **Cutover happens before the next ingestion event** that could trigger supersession, so the
   engine copy is never asked to represent a state past the one it was built from.

chunks.heading: Wave 3 carve: ledger onto the engine > Rule 7's transience guarantee: where supersession lives, and the dual-copy plan
chunks.text:
**Option 1 is what the code supports, and what this wave builds.** `EngineDataMigrationWave3`'s copy
half is additive-only (same as Wave 1/2 - it can never delete a mirrored row that a legacy row still
justifies), so option 1 as stated cannot fully close the gap by itself; a purely additive re-run
would keep ADDING newly-reconciled rows but would never notice a provisional row's legacy backing
had disappeared. **The copier therefore adds a fourth capability beyond the additive copy: a
`reconcileSupersededProvisional` pass**, run at the end of every call INCLUDING the fast path (the
one deliberate departure from Wave 1/2's "flag set, later calls do nothing at all" shape - see
`EngineDataMigrationWave3.Result`'s own doc comment). It compares the LIVE set of legacy `syncId`s
against every active engine `Transaction` record tagged `RecordProvenance.UNRECONCILED`, and trashes
(via `RecordStore.delete` - 30-day restorable, never a hard delete) any whose legacy row is gone.
This closes rule 7's specific guarantee - an `UNRECONCILED` engine record cannot outlive the legacy
row it mirrors, **as long as the copier is called again after the legacy-side deletion happens** (an
app start, per the `MidnightApplication` wiring below).

**What this does NOT close, named rather than silently accepted**: a `DETERMINISTIC`/
`LLM_RECONCILED` engine record whose legacy row is deleted by a replace-flow re-import
(`IngestPipeline`'s `staged.isReplace` branch calling `deleteBySourceFileId`) or by
`LedgerController.purgeAll` (the admin nuke) is **not** trashed by this pass - it is scoped
deliberately to `UNRECONCILED` only, because that is the provenance rule 7 actually places a
transience obligation on. A stale reconciled engine record surviving a legacy replace/purge is a
real gap, but it is not the gap CLAUDE.md §4 rule 7 exists to close, and closing it would mean
diffing the WHOLE table every call rather than the bounded `UNRECONCILED` subset - left to the
cutover wave, where the copier's job ends anyway (see owed follow-ups).

chunks.heading: Wave 3 carve: ledger onto the engine > Rule 7's transience guarantee: where supersession lives, and the dual-copy plan
chunks.text:
**Both copies therefore do not fully agree at every instant** - the legacy table is authoritative
and live at all times; the engine copy is a periodically-reconciled mirror, correct as of its last
run, with the one specific staleness mode above named and accepted rather than hidden. This is
consistent with instruction 5: nothing about the legacy ingestion path reads from or defers to the
engine copy in this wave.

chunks.text:
1. **Cutover per aspect** (ticket 14 point 2) is explicitly NOT this wave's job. `ledger/`,

   `EngineDataMigrationWave3.copyLedgerIfNeeded` calls it fresh at the top of every one of its own

chunks.heading: Wave 4 carve: fleet onto the engine
chunks.text:
Owed by `.scratch/aspect-engine/issues/21-migration-waves.md` point 2 ("per-aspect carve...
produced per wave before its build starts") and ticket 11 answer point 5 (the per-plugin inventory
table). Written before any code in this wave, following [Wave 1](wave1-carve-2026-08-23.md),
[Wave 2](wave2-carve-2026-08-23.md), and [Wave 3](wave3-carve-2026-08-23.md)'s own shape. This is
the biggest and last of the four waves ("fleet onto the engine") - it also inherits the widest
domain: OBD stack, maintenance, service records, fuel/drives, recaps, garage.

chunks.heading: Wave 4 carve: fleet onto the engine > Scope decision, stated up front (instruction 6)
chunks.text:
**This wave migrates the core chain completely - vehicles, service records, maintenance items,
odometer - and defers everything else, named below, to a follow-up wave.** The fleet domain is 18
entities wide (17 in `data/local/` plus `CarTask`, already ruled dead by Wave 1 - see below); trying
to carve and migrate all of them in one pass would repeat the exact mistake CLAUDE.md's L10/L11
lessons exist to catch (a grep-clean breadth pass that never gets the one hard entity - the
maintenance clock - actually right). The core chain is also the one instruction 2 names by name
(hands-and-senses ticket 29) and the one with a real, load-bearing correctness bug behind it
(service history and the maintenance clock disagreeing) - it is where the carve work is genuinely
hard, and where getting it wrong would ship the exact drift bug ticket 29 diagnosed straight into
the engine's own schema.

chunks.heading: Wave 4 carve: fleet onto the engine > The finding that reshapes this carve: ticket 29's diagnosis is the carve, not a footnote
chunks.text:
`.scratch/hands-and-senses/issues/29-one-source-for-service-history.md` (status `kiv`,
`status-detail: "superseded by the aspect engine... Wave 4"`) is not closed and unrelated - it is
explicitly parked THERE, waiting for THIS wave. Kevin's own diagnosis: *"service history and
maintenance clock should be tied together as one object no? thats why theres the bug."* Traced in
full (`data/local/ServiceRecord.kt`, `data/local/MaintenanceItem.kt`,
`vehicle/VehicleController.kt` lines 533-748): `service_records` (the events - what was actually
done, when, at what mileage) and `maintenance_items.lastDoneMileage`/`lastDoneDate` (the schedule's
own clock, meant to be a projection of those events) are two independently-writable stores of what
is supposed to be one fact. `logServiceDirect` writes both in the same call (line 571 + 608) and
usually keeps them in step, but `MaintenanceItemDao.setAnchor` can move the clock alone (a driver
backfill, an advisor-accepted proposal), and nothing enforces the two ever agreeing - which is
exactly how Kevin's own Jeep ended up with a clock reading 227,483 mi with no date, and a
`service_records` row for the same oil change reading 227,374 mi on 12 Aug, world's most obvious
avoidable disagreement.

chunks.heading: Wave 4 carve: fleet onto the engine > The finding that reshapes this carve: ticket 29's diagnosis is the carve, not a footnote
chunks.text:
**Ticket 29's own recommendation is adopted here, not reopened.** *"Does the override become a
`service_records` row of its own (tagged as asserted rather than observed)... This is the
recommendation."* The carve below does exactly that: one `ServiceHistory` record type carries
BOTH kinds of fact - `kind = OBSERVED` (migrated straight off a real `ServiceRecord` row) and
`kind = ASSERTED` (a user-stated anchor with no backing event, migrated off `MaintenanceItem`'s
`lastDoneMileage`/`lastDoneDate`) - so a screen or a voice answer built against this table cannot
read two different histories the way `ui/FleetScreen.kt`'s Service History section and
`MaintenanceAgent`'s spoken answer used to. The interval DEFINITION (how often, on what axis, who
set it) is schedule configuration, not an event, and stays its own record type, `MaintenanceSchedule`
- ticket 29's own framing: *"Records are the events. The clock is a projection of them, plus an
explicit override."* `MaintenanceSchedule` carries the projection's INPUTS (interval, provenance,
never-done); the actual last-done figure a schedule check would read is `ServiceHistory`, not a
column on `MaintenanceSchedule` at all - the drift is deleted by construction, because there is no
longer a second place for that figure to live.

**What this wave does NOT do: it does not build the schedule math against the new table.** Reading
"is item X due" off the new `ServiceHistory`/`MaintenanceSchedule` pair (the way
`VehicleController.dueItems`/`isDue` today reads `MaintenanceItem.lastDoneMileage` directly) is
cutover work (ticket 14 point 2), same as every other wave - `vehicle/VehicleController.kt` is not
touched by this wave at all. This wave's job is that the SCHEMA and the MIGRATED DATA no longer
have the split; making the live app read it is next.

chunks.heading: Wave 4 carve: fleet onto the engine > `ServiceHistory`'s dedup rule, stated as a judgment call (REASONED)
chunks.text:
Every `MaintenanceItem` whose `lastDoneMileage`/`lastDoneDate` is non-null represents a fact that
must survive the migration (CLAUDE.md-adjacent §4 rule 6 posture, applied to migration
completeness the same way Wave 2/3's `failedLineItemGuids`/`anyFailure` folding already does: "no
fact is lost" per ticket 29's own rule). The naive approach - always create an `ASSERTED` row for
every non-null anchor - would duplicate the common case where the anchor and a real `ServiceRecord`
already agree (`logServiceDirect`'s normal, non-drifted path). The other naive approach - try to
match an anchor to "the" corresponding `ServiceRecord` by nearest mileage/date - is exactly the
guessing ticket 29 warns against: *"A migration that guesses is worse than one that asks... prefer
preserving both facts... over silently picking a winner."*

chunks.heading: Wave 4 carve: fleet onto the engine > `ServiceHistory`'s dedup rule, stated as a judgment call (REASONED)
chunks.text:
**The rule this migration uses, mechanical and non-guessing:** for a `MaintenanceItem` with a
non-null `lastDoneMileage` and/or `lastDoneDate`, look at every `OBSERVED` `ServiceRecord` already
on file for the SAME `(vehicleId, serviceName)` pair (exact string match - `serviceName` is already
canonicalised identically by every write path per `ServiceRecordDao.getMostRecentForVehicleAndService`'s
own doc comment, so this is not a fuzzy match). If any SINGLE one of them agrees with the anchor on
EVERY axis the anchor actually states - `mileage == lastDoneMileage` when `lastDoneMileage` is
non-null, AND `date == lastDoneDate` when `lastDoneDate` is non-null (a null anchor axis is
vacuously satisfied, since there is nothing on it to contradict) - the anchor is considered
**explained** and no `ASSERTED` row is created. Otherwise, an `ASSERTED` row is created carrying
exactly the anchor's own `lastDoneMileage`/`lastDoneDate` (nulls preserved as nulls, never
invented). **Both present axes must match the SAME row** - senior review, 2026-08-24 (MUST-FIX):
the first cut of this rule OR'd the two axes across the whole candidate set (`.any` with an internal
`||`), so a coincidental mileage match on one `ServiceRecord` and an unrelated (or entirely absent)
date match on a DIFFERENT `ServiceRecord` could each satisfy one half of "explained" independently -
a two-field anchor was then treated as fully explained even though no single observed row actually
backed both facts, silently dropping the axis nothing really matched. Requiring an AND across both
present axes on one row closes that: this never merges evidence from two different `ServiceRecord`
rows into an explanation for one anchor, and never discards a value that does not match anything -
it only avoids the ONE case where duplication is provably certain (a single row that agrees on every
axis the anchor states). The Jeep's dateless 227,483 anchor does not match its 227,374/12-Aug
`ServiceRecord` on its one stated axis (mileage), so it survives the migration as its own `ASSERTED`
row, disagreement and all - **exactly what ticket 29 asked for**: both facts preserved, stated as
what they are, not silently reconciled. A regression case this fix specifically guards against: a
`ServiceRecord` with a coincidentally-matching mileage but a genuinely disagreeing date must NOT

chunks.heading: Wave 4 carve: fleet onto the engine > `ServiceHistory`'s dedup rule, stated as a judgment call (REASONED)
chunks.text:
explain the anchor - the anchor's date is a fact the driver stated and must still land as its own
`ASSERTED` row (`EngineDataMigrationWave4Test`'s own regression test for this).

`neverDone` is not an anchor at all (`MaintenanceItem`'s own doc: "always overdue... never treated
as due") - it produces no `ServiceHistory` row and is carried instead as a `MaintenanceSchedule`
field.

chunks.text:

Pure sync/telemetry machinery, same category as Wave 3's `ingested_files`. |
| `ChassisQuirk` (`chassis_quirks`) | Yes | **Stays plugin-internal** | Not even per-user data - keyed by a global `quirkId` slug (`e46_subframe_crack`), a shared reference knowledge base of known problems by chassis/engine, not something any user creates, owns, or deletes. |
| `ForesightNote` (`foresight_notes`) | Yes | **Stays plugin-internal** | Named out of scope for Wave 1 with an explicit forward pointer to this wave ("Belongs to the fleet wave (wave 4), not this one") - ruled here as promised. An AI-generated, dismissible risk observation (coolant-temp trend, oil-analysis pattern), not a user assertion - closer to `advisor/AdvisorAdvice`'s own shape (a system-generated suggestion) than to a fact the user stated. Deferred/plugin-internal rather than promoted, since nothing in the core chain references it and it carries no reconciliation-gate-relevant data. |

No entity here is ambiguous about being genuinely "dead" the way Wave 1's `car_tasks`/

chunks.heading: Wave 4 carve: fleet onto the engine > Field mapping: `Vehicle` -> Fleet aspect, `Vehicle` record type
chunks.text:
Owner plugin id: `"fleet"`. Locked+required: `name`, `make`, `model`, `year`, `confirmed` - the
identity facts a car cannot meaningfully lack once it is a real, on-file vehicle. `trim`/`engine`/
`odometerBaseline`/`odometerBaselineAt` are optional, matching their nullable-in-effect legacy
defaults (`""`/`0`).

chunks.heading: Wave 4 carve: fleet onto the engine > Field mapping: `MaintenanceItem` (interval half) -> Fleet aspect, `MaintenanceSchedule` record type
Wave 4 carve: fleet onto the engine > What the copier does and does not copy
chunks.text:
- **Vehicles first, unconditionally, from `VehicleDao.getAllIncludingArchived()`** - both `ServiceHistory`
  and `MaintenanceSchedule` rows reference a vehicle, so every vehicle (including an archived one -
  archived means hidden from the roster/picker, not deleted, and its history is exactly as real)
  must exist as an `EngineRecord` before any child row can validate its reference, the same ordering
  discipline Wave 2's receipts-before-line-items and Wave 3's (implicit, single-record-type) shape
  both already establish.
- **`ServiceRecord` rows, `WHERE deleted = 0` only** (`ServiceRecordDao` has no `getAll()`; a new
  `getAllIncludingDeleted()` is NOT added - deliberately: unlike `MaintenanceItemDao.getForVehicleIncludingDeleted`
  (which exists for a real reader, the populate diff), nothing needs a tombstoned `ServiceRecord` for
  this migration, and CLAUDE.md's own posture toward `service_records.deleted`'s doc comment - "this
  tombstone is LOCAL ONLY and CANNOT propagate across devices" - argues for treating a tombstoned row
  as genuinely gone here, matching how the OLD app already treats it everywhere except sync's raw
  snapshot).
- **`MaintenanceItem` rows, `WHERE deleted = 0` only** (`MaintenanceItemDao.getForVehicle`, already
  filtered) - a tombstoned schedule item is, per that entity's own doc comment, a driver-deleted row;
  carrying its interval OR its anchor forward as live engine data would resurrect something the
  driver removed, the same "don't resurrect a tombstone" posture Wave 1's `ListItem`/`TaggedPlace`
  filtering already states.
- **`ServiceHistory` copies happen in two passes per vehicle**: every `OBSERVED` row first (off
  `ServiceRecordDao`), THEN every `ASSERTED` row (off `MaintenanceItemDao`, applying the dedup rule
  above against the `OBSERVED` rows already read for that same vehicle+service in this pass) - so
  the dedup check always has the full `OBSERVED` set for that pair in hand before deciding whether an
  anchor is explained.
- **Preserves timestamps.** Neither `ServiceRecord` nor `MaintenanceItem` carries a real insert-time
  clock distinct from its own subject-matter timestamp - `ServiceRecord.date` (when the service
  happened) and `MaintenanceItem.updatedAt` (last schedule edit) are the closest anchors, same
  "closest available anchor, not a bookkeeping clock" substitution Wave 2/3's carves already state

chunks.heading: Wave 4 carve: fleet onto the engine > What the copier does and does not copy
chunks.text:
and name as deliberate rather than implicit. `Vehicle` similarly has no creation timestamp; its
  `updatedAt` is used for both clocks, same shape.
- **Identity**: `ServiceRecord.syncId` reused directly; every other row in this wave (`Vehicle`,
  `MaintenanceSchedule`, `ServiceHistory` `ASSERTED`) gets a deterministic `UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes`
  guid off its own natural key, per the field-mapping tables above - never a fresh random UUID,
  so a second run recognizes and skips what it already wrote.
- **Provenance is unconditionally `RecordProvenance.USER`** for every row this wave writes, across
  all three record types. Nothing here passed through CLAUDE.md §4's reconciliation gate (fleet has
  no document-ingestion path at all) - every fact originated from the driver speaking to LEGION or
  typing into a form, matching Wave 1's `USER` reasoning exactly ("a straight field-by-field copy has
  no stated total to reconcile against... not even an ingestion path at all").

instruction 5/ticket 11 answer point 5 rather than sampled):

| `ask_maintenance` | `MaintenanceAgent` | Yes, same target as `get_next_service`. |
| `set_odometer` | `VehicleController.setOdometer` -> `VehicleDao.setOdometerBaseline` | Yes - `update_record` on `Vehicle.odometerBaseline`/`odometerBaselineAt`. |
| `log_service` | `VehicleController.logServiceDirect` | Yes - `create_record` against `ServiceHistory` (`kind = OBSERVED`), which also folds in what today is a second write to `maintenance_items`' anchor, closing the drift by construction. |
| `log_past_service` | `VehicleController.logPastServiceDirect` | Yes, same target as `log_service`. |
| `set_maintenance_interval` | `MaintenanceItemDao.setIntervals` | Yes - `update_record` against `MaintenanceSchedule`. |
| `lookup_vin` | `VinDecoder` -> `VehicleSpec` | **No** - external NHTSA vPIC lookup is native network I/O; `VehicleSpec` itself is deferred (see carve table), so there is no engine record type for this to write into yet regardless. |
| `check_recalls` | NHTSA recalls API (live, not stored) | **No** - never touches Room at all; nothing to migrate. |
| `register_vehicle` | `VehicleController.registerDirect` | Yes - `create_record` against `Vehicle`. |
| `activate_garage` | `GarageController`/Shelly opener | **No** - hardware actuation (a real garage door), not data. |
| `list_vehicles` | `VehicleDao.getAll` | Yes - `list_records` against `Vehicle`. |
| `manage_vehicle` | `VehicleController` (archive/rename/correct) | Yes - `update_record`/`delete_record` (subject to the new `DeletePolicy.BLOCK` if the car has history). |

chunks.heading: Wave 4 carve: fleet onto the engine > Voice tools: what stays, what the carve marks for cutover-time removal only
chunks.text:
| `set_driver` | `ActiveVehicle` (per-device active-car selection) | **No** - device-local session state, not a stored record. |
| `register_car` | Same family as `register_vehicle` | Yes, same target. |
| `diagnose_codes` | `DiagnosticAgent`/`CodeEvent` | **No** - reads plugin-internal `code_events`, stays native. |
| `triage_symptom` | `SymptomAgent`/`ChassisQuirk` | **No** - `ChassisQuirk` stays plugin-internal (global reference data, see carve table). |
| `clear_codes` | `DtcClearController` | **No** - live Mode-04 hardware command plus its own `code_clear_events` audit row, both plugin-internal. |
| `log_build_entry` | `BuildSheetController` -> `BuildEntry` | Deferred - `BuildEntry` is out of this wave's scope (see carve table); revisit at the follow-up wave. |
| `list_build_history` | `BuildSheetController` | Deferred, same reasoning. |
| `get_spend` | `FleetSpendController` (`service_records` + `build_entries`) | Partial - the `service_records` half becomes a `ServiceHistory` `COMPUTED Aggregate` (`SUM` over `costCents`, filtered to `kind = OBSERVED`) once cutover's aggregate machinery is pointed at it; the `build_entries` half stays blocked on that entity's own deferred migration. **Not fully resolved here**, named as an open question for the follow-up wave, same posture as Wave 2/3's own `get_grocery_spend`/`get_balance` notes. |

chunks.heading: Wave 4 carve: fleet onto the engine > Owed follow-ups, named rather than silently dropped
chunks.text:
1. **Cutover per aspect** (ticket 14 point 2) is explicitly NOT this wave's job. `vehicle/`, every
   fleet screen (`ui/FleetScreen.kt` and friends), and every fleet `LiveToolbox` tool keep reading
   and writing the legacy `vehicles`/`service_records`/`maintenance_items` tables unchanged until
   this aspect is verified on the A25 and cut over in its own later commit - the schedule-math
   re-point (`VehicleController.dueItems`/`isDue` reading `ServiceHistory`/`MaintenanceSchedule`
   instead of `MaintenanceItem`'s own anchor columns) happens THERE, not here.
2. **`BuildEntry`, `VehicleSpec`, `OilAnalysis`, `MonthlyRecap`, `DailyDriveLog`, `YearlyWrapped`,
   `Drive` are deferred to a named follow-up wave** (Wave 5, fleet-continued) - each with its own
   one-line reasoning in the carve table above, not silently dropped.
3. **`OdbSample`/`CodeEvent`/`CodeClearEvent`/`VehicleCapability`/`DriveReassignment`/`ChassisQuirk`/
   `ForesightNote` stay plugin-internal, permanently** by this carve's own ruling - not a deferral,
   a decision, matching the guiding line's own "high-frequency telemetry and transient OBD state
   stay plugin-internal" instruction.
4. **`Vehicle.personaPrompt`/`voiceName`/`personaTraits`/`archived`/`onboarded`/
   `lastOdometerPromptAt`/`tripMilesSinceBaseline` are not carried as fields** - named in the field
   mapping table above with per-column reasoning, revisited only if a follow-up wave's cutover finds
   a live need for one of them on the record.
5. **`ServiceHistory`'s `ASSERTED`/`OBSERVED` dedup rule is intentionally conservative** (see its own
   section above) - it can under-collapse (an anchor that is a near-miss but not an exact match on
   either axis still gets its own `ASSERTED` row, even in cases a human would recognize as "the same
   event") but it can never silently drop or merge a fact. Named as a deliberate false-negative-safe
   choice, not re-litigated here.
6. **Neither legacy table is dropped.** `vehicles`, `service_records`, and `maintenance_items` stay
   exactly as they are today; this wave adds new tables' worth of DATA (rows in
   `aspects`/`record_types`/`field_defs`/`records`), not a schema change to any existing table -
   matching every prior wave's own closing note.
7. **`VehicleDao.getAllIncludingArchived()` and `ServiceRecordDao`'s existing filtered queries are

chunks.heading: Wave 4 carve: fleet onto the engine > Owed follow-ups, named rather than silently dropped
chunks.text:
reused as-is; no new DAO query was needed for `Vehicle`/`ServiceRecord`.** `MaintenanceItemDao.getForVehicle`
   is likewise reused unchanged. No Room schema/version change anywhere in this wave.
8. **The migration-to-cutover ASSERTED staleness window, named rather than silently accepted
   (senior review nice-to-have, 2026-08-24).** A `ServiceHistory` `ASSERTED` row is computed once,
   at copy time, from whatever `OBSERVED` `ServiceRecord`s existed for that vehicle+service AT THAT
   MOMENT. If the legacy app later logs a real service (`logServiceDirect`/`logPastServiceDirect`)
   that WOULD have explained an already-migrated `ASSERTED` row - matching it on every axis the
   dedup rule above checks - nothing re-runs that check retroactively: the copier is additive-only
   (same as every prior wave) and never deletes or re-evaluates a row it already wrote, so the
   `ASSERTED` row sits stale, now duplicating a fact an `OBSERVED` row also carries, with nothing on
   the engine side reconciling them. This is a DIFFERENT gap from Wave 3's `reconcileSupersededProvisional`
   pass (that one catches a legacy row's own DELETION; this one is about a legacy row's later
   ADDITION un-asserting a synthetic fact this wave invented) and this wave does not build an
   equivalent pass for it - `EngineDataMigrationWave4` has no per-call reconciliation step the way
   `EngineDataMigrationWave3` does. Left open deliberately (not a silent gap): cutover's design must
   answer whether this needs its own periodic reconcile pass (mirroring Wave 3's shape, scoped to
   `kind = ASSERTED` rows) or whether it is subsumed once cutover re-points writes at `RecordStore`
   directly and the legacy tables (and therefore new drift of this shape) stop being written to at
   all.

chunks.heading: Glossary
chunks.text:
**This file holds one-line glosses and pointers. It is not the definition.** CLAUDE.md owns the
vocabulary; a second competing glossary is the exact failure the read order exists to prevent. If a
gloss here starts explaining more than CLAUDE.md does, that is a bug in this file, not an
improvement.

Terms are listed because they are load-bearing and easy to misread, not because they are obscure.

chunks.heading: Glossary > The shape of the project
chunks.text:
| Term | Gloss | Defined in |
|---|---|---|
| **aspect** | a life domain LEGION keeps records for. Not "module", not "feature". CLAUDE.md §1 owns the list; the sync layer's `ASPECT_*` keys are a wider, differently-named set and are not it | CLAUDE.md §1, `backend/engine/EngineBackends.kt` |
| **LEGION** | the app. **Not** the assistant's name | CLAUDE.md §1, 0020-companion-identity-per-profile |
| **companion** | the thing you talk to. User-named per profile. Never hardcode a name | 0020-companion-identity-per-profile |
| **register band** | "Alfred/JARVIS" names a *tone*, not a character. `ai/Personas.kt` holds the copy | CLAUDE.md §1 |
| **clone-and-run** | a stranger clones, sideloads with their own cert and key, and it works | 0003-clone-and-run |
| **BYO key** | the user's own Gemini API key, direct to Google, no proxy. The web assistant is the exception: it runs on the household's key, held by the engine | 0002-no-hosted-backend, 0056-the-household-key-serves-the-web-assistant |
| **appDataFolder** | the private per-app area of the user's own Drive. Backup and restore only. **Not** the system of record | 0044-django-is-the-engine |
| **the engine** | the Django server over Postgres. The system of record and the only writer of it | 0044-django-is-the-engine |
| **limb** | anything that talks to the engine over HTTPS JSON: the phone, the web app, a future device | 0044-django-is-the-engine |
| **household** | the unit of tenancy, and the only one. Membership is the whole authorization model | CLAUDE.md §1, 0045-households-are-tenants |
| **outbox** | the phone's durable queue for a write the engine could not take yet. At-least-once, never silent | `data/local/SyncOutbox.kt`, 0044-django-is-the-engine |

chunks.heading: Glossary > Ingestion
chunks.text:
| Term | Gloss | Defined in |
|---|---|---|
| **the gate** | the reconciliation check. Not a permission gate, not a paywall | CLAUDE.md §4, 0006-reconciliation-gate |
| **quarantine** | a document that failed the gate and was written **nowhere**. Not "error", not "partial import" | CLAUDE.md §4 rule 2 |
| **anchor** | the total a document prints about itself, which the gate checks against | 0009-provisional-unreconciled-tier |
| **provenance** | `DETERMINISTIC` or `LLM_RECONCILED`. Both passed the same gate. **Not a trust discount** | CLAUDE.md §4 rule 4 |
| **`BANK_API`** | a ledger row from a linked bank's own feed (Plaid). Stored as fact with no gate, by ruling: the one exempt ingestion source | CLAUDE.md §4 rule 1, 0057-the-bank-feed-is-the-ledgers-truth |
| **`UNRECONCILED`** | a provisional row from a source with no anchor. Transient, and said in words on every surface | 0009-provisional-unreconciled-tier |
| **estimate** | a value the source never stated. Pantry macros are the canonical case. Never presented as fact | 0008-estimates-are-not-facts |
| **spend gate** | **two different things.** The LLM cost prompt (0016-llm-spend-gate-after-deterministic), and a retired Midnight AI access gate (0030-retired-carry-overs). Say which |
| **twin transactions** | genuinely identical rows within one statement. Why dedup counts rather than tests | 0015-dedup-counts-per-tuple |

chunks.heading: Glossary > The aspect engine
chunks.text:
| Term | Gloss | Defined in |
|---|---|---|
| **aspect engine** | the runtime metadata system (`aspects`/`record_types`/`field_defs`/`records`). One generic store, not a per-domain table set. **Retiring**: typed per-aspect tables are the direction and both shapes are live | 0039-per-aspect-typed-tables supersedes 0037-the-aspect-engine-is-the-spine |
| **record type** | a user- or plugin-defined schema (e.g. "Transaction", "Workout") made of field defs. Defines a type, not an instance | `engine/FieldConfig.kt`, 0037-the-aspect-engine-is-the-spine |
| **field def** | one typed field on a record type (13 field types v1: text, number, money-cents, date, etc.) | `memory/library/decisions.md` 2026-08-23 |
| **`RecordStore`** | `engine/RecordStore.kt`. The single write door for every engine record - reference integrity, delete policy, trash, computed fields | 0037-the-aspect-engine-is-the-spine |
| **provenance** *(engine sense)* | tagged per engine record same as ledger/pantry provenance, but the write path is now `RecordStore` rather than a per-aspect DAO | CLAUDE.md §4 rule 4, 0037-the-aspect-engine-is-the-spine |
| **widget pager / dashboard** | `ui/widgets/`, `LegionRoute.DASHBOARD`. Was the app's home screen from the 2026-08-24 home-flip cutover. **It is not HOME any more**: HOME is the calendar (`ui/home/`) | 0037-the-aspect-engine-is-the-spine, `docs/architecture/cutover5-2026-08-24.md` |
| **mirror** | the xlsx-per-aspect export into the user's own Drive folder (`engine/mirror/`) - the audit surface and the two-phone sync channel, not the legacy `sync/` mechanism | `memory/library/decisions.md` 2026-08-23 ticket 12/13 |
| **meta-tools** | the nine generic voice tools (`service/EngineToolbox.kt`) that do CRUD/query over any record type, replacing most per-feature tools | `memory/library/decisions.md` 2026-08-23 ticket 06 |
| **clerk** | the bounded Flash sub-agent behind the meta-tools that turns a loose voice request into a structured engine call. An executor, not a router | `memory/library/decisions.md` 2026-08-23 ticket 06 |

chunks.heading: Glossary > Planning and process
chunks.text:
| Term | Gloss | Defined in |
|---|---|---|
| **wayfinder map** | a charted effort: one `map.md` plus numbered tickets under `issues/` | `.claude/skills/wayfinder/` |
| **ticket** | one question or one build step inside a map. Has `type`, `status`, `blocked-by` | `vault/Board.md` |
| **fog** | work known to exist but not yet charted as a ticket | `.claude/skills/wayfinder/` |
| **graduated** | a ticket promoted out of fog, or an effort promoted to its own map | ticket `status` values |
| **ready** | open, with every blocker resolved. Computed, so it goes stale without a re-run | CLAUDE.md §12 |
| **L*n*** | a numbered lesson. L24 is "the repo is ahead of its docs" | `memory/library/lessons.md` |
| **assumptions ledger** | the tags every agent report ends with: `built` / `tested` / `traced` / `reasoned` / `on-device` | CLAUDE.md §8 |

chunks.heading: Glossary > Dead vocabulary
chunks.text:
These still appear in code, comments, and the frozen library. **Their meaning died with the pivot**,
which makes them more dangerous than terms that were simply deleted.

| Term | What it was | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Midnight AI** | the predecessor product, a commercial head-unit car launcher | Frozen archive. Read-only |
| **Zero** | the mascot | Dead. 0021-city-pop-retired |
| **city-pop** | the old design language | Dead. Replaced by mission control (0023-design-language-mission-control), itself superseded by soft Material (0051-design-language-soft-material) |
| **Instrument** | the first replacement design language | Superseded. 0022-design-language-instrument |
| **cyberdeck** | the second one. Shipped, then partly superseded | See `.scratch/cyberdeck-ui/map.md` |
| **Moose, Aria, Kaze, Nightrunner, Yoko** | former assistant names | Dead. See the register-band rule |
| **`CarTask`, `PlaceReminder`** | Room entities, still in the schema | Tombstones. Read by nothing new |
| **head unit** | the original target hardware | No longer constrains anything. 0001-phone-only |

The single sharpest trap: **a term that still exists in code but whose meaning died with the pivot.**
When in doubt, the code wins over the comment, and CLAUDE.md wins over both for what a word means
now.

chunks.heading: How LEGION is built with AI coding agents
chunks.text:
Kevin builds LEGION with AI coding agents: Claude Code sessions that plan, write, review and test
the code, while Kevin makes the decisions. This page describes that workflow as the repo itself
records it. Every claim here points at a file in the repo; the numbers are counted from the repo,
and the method is given next to each one.

The binding rules live in `CLAUDE.md` (section 8, Working Model; sections 12 and 13, the vault and
docs layers) and `TEAM.md` (the agent roster). This page summarises them for a reader from outside;
where they disagree, those files win.

chunks.heading: How LEGION is built with AI coding agents > The short version
chunks.text:
- **Kevin decides, agents build.** Standing rules carry the name and date of whoever decided them,
  and the decisions are Kevin's. Agents turn rulings into specs, code, tests and docs.
- **The loop is decide, spec, build in parallel, verify, record.** Large efforts are charted as a
  map of decision tickets; each resolved decision leaves a build ticket; anything ready is built.
- **Several agents run at once, each in its own git worktree,** so they never share a checkout.
- **Every agent report ends with an assumptions ledger** that tags each claim with how it was
  checked. An inferred claim is never relayed as a fact.
- **Mistakes become rules.** A failure is written up as a numbered lesson, and the lesson closes
  only when its rule is written into a prompt or a check that the next agent actually reads.

chunks.heading: How LEGION is built with AI coding agents > The tools
chunks.text:
- **Claude Code** is the agent runtime: one main session (the orchestrator) that talks to Kevin and
  dispatches project subagents defined in `.claude/agents/`.
- **Models, as the repo names them.** `CLAUDE.md` says: plan with a strong model (Fable or Opus) in
  plan mode, execute approved plans with Sonnet. The subagent definitions pin `model: sonnet`. The
  commit history shows the real mix (see the numbers below): most commits are co-authored by Opus,
  with Sonnet and Fable behind.
- **Hooks** in `.claude/settings.json` run before tool calls: a commit hook, destructive-command
  and generated-file guards, and two warnings. See "How quality is checked".
- **Project MCP servers** in `tools/mcp/` give agents typed access to the ticket board, Gradle runs
  and test totals, and the engine.
- **Skills** in `.claude/skills/`: vendored Kotlin and Compose guidance, plus four repo-specific
  planning skills: `wayfinder`, `to-spec`, `grillme` and `issue-tracker.md`.

chunks.heading: How LEGION is built with AI coding agents > The loop: decide, spec, build in parallel, verify, record
chunks.text:
1. **Decide.** A loose idea too big for one session is charted with the `wayfinder` skill as a
   map: `.scratch/<effort>/map.md` plus numbered decision tickets under `.scratch/<effort>/issues/`.
   Decisions are resolved one at a time, usually by interview: the `grillme` skill refuses to
   implement and instead asks one question at a time until a half-formed request is a tight brief.
2. **Spec.** The `to-spec` skill turns the conversation into a spec. Plans are execution specs:
   exact file names, signatures, edge cases and a verification section, with no taste calls left
   to whoever executes them (`CLAUDE.md` section 8).
3. **Build in parallel.** A resolved decision that authorises code must leave a build ticket behind
   in the same commit. **Anything ready is built, not parked** (Kevin's standing ruling): a ready
   ticket with no open decisions is unstarted work, and building may run in parallel with grilling
   the next effort.
4. **Verify.** The real build and the real test suite, not a grep. One logical change per commit,
   with compile and unit tests green before each commit. Anything that only hardware can settle is
   marked `built` and owes a run on the real device.
5. **Record.** The ticket's status and verification detail are updated, the decision is logged, the
   board regenerates on commit, and any mistake found on the way becomes a lesson.

chunks.heading: How LEGION is built with AI coding agents > How decisions are made and recorded
chunks.text:
- **Kevin makes the rulings.** Most rules in `CLAUDE.md` and `TEAM.md` carry his name and a date; the rest are lessons, named by number, often
  with his words quoted. Agents may propose and argue; a fork the plan does not answer means stop
  and surface it, not improvise (`CLAUDE.md` section 8).
- **Two decision stores with different jobs.** `memory/library/decisions.md` says what happened and
  when. `docs/adr/` says what is binding now. Every decision gets a dated entry; only standing ones
  also get an ADR. Superseded ADRs keep their original text and link to their replacement.
- **Decisions are re-opened on merit.** The dependency-injection choice was decided twice in one
  day: the morning research said manual DI, Kevin reopened it, a survey re-argued it, and the
  second ruling (Hilt on KSP) stands with the first kept in the dated log.
- **Tickets are files with frontmatter.** Status lives in YAML (`open`, `resolved`, `built`,
  `kiv`, and a few others). `built` means built and suite green but owing a run on real hardware;
  `kiv` means parked on purpose by Kevin. `tools/obsidian_sync.py` regenerates the board and the
  per-map dependency graphs from that frontmatter, and `tools/pending_wiki.py` renders the public
  ticket board.
- **A resolved decision with no build ticket is caught.** `tools/decision_debt.py` exists because a
  fully decided feature once vanished from the board, which lists only open tickets, and looked
  finished when nothing had been built. It runs on every commit.

chunks.heading: How LEGION is built with AI coding agents > What Kevin does and what agents do
chunks.text:
| Kevin | Agents |
|---|---|
| Sets the destination and makes every ruling | Chart maps, research options, argue trade-offs |
| Answers grilling interviews | Turn answers into specs and build tickets |
| Accepts or rejects an unmet verification step, in so many words | Report every unmet step as a gate, never a footnote |
| Uses the product for real, by voice and on the phone | Build, test, review and document; drive the attached phone over adb for reproductions |
| Decides when the rules change | Write lessons and graduate them into prompts and checks |

The main session dispatches subagents by default, not as an escalation: Kevin gave that as a
standing instruction so he does not have to ask per task. Judgement still applies; a one-line fix
does not need an agent.

chunks.heading: How LEGION is built with AI coding agents > The agent team
chunks.text:
Five seats, defined in `.claude/agents/` and explained in `TEAM.md`:

| Seat | Role |
|---|---|
| `builder` | Writes code. Executes a spec exactly. |
| `auditor` | Reads code adversarially: defects, arithmetic, data integrity, diff review against the rules. Runs after a feature lands and before anything ships. |
| `device` | Anything that needs the real phone: build, install, adb, database pulls, reproducing a bug on hardware. |
| `scout` | Read-only breadth search across code, the library or the ticket maps, returning only the conclusion. |
| `frontend` | The web client's UI: studies how shipped apps solve a screen, writes notes, then designs and builds it. |

**An agent file states no fact that can go stale.** No counts, versions, package maps or device
models: only the role, guardrails that were paid for, how to check things, and the reporting
contract. This rule came from a real failure: an old roster named the wrong phone, and three agents
in one session faithfully reported testing on a device that was not attached. In the words of
`TEAM.md`: a stale instruction is not ignored, it is obeyed.

chunks.heading: How LEGION is built with AI coding agents > How parallel agents avoid conflicts
chunks.text:
- **Every concurrent agent gets its own git worktree** (Kevin's standing rule in `TEAM.md`): a
  separate checkout, build directory and Gradle daemon over a shared `.git`. The repo's guards
  assume a tree routinely has two or more agents working in it.
- **Never `git add -A` in a tree another agent is working in.** Stage your own paths and commit
  with a pathspec, so another agent's half-finished work never rides along in your commit.
- **Copy the gitignored local config into a fresh worktree** before dispatching an agent that must
  build; otherwise the build cannot find the SDK and the isolation that prevents one failure causes
  another.
- **Why these rules exist** is lesson L32: two agents in one checkout produced commits that
  contained another agent's in-flight files, a generated page documenting code that was not
  committed, and two Gradle failures that looked exactly like test failures but were one agent
  stopping the other's daemon. The agents' code was correct; the shared workspace was not.
- **Completion contract.** A turn does not end with a subagent unfinished or its result
  unrelayed. Independent dispatches go out together so they run in parallel; dependent ones wait.

chunks.heading: How LEGION is built with AI coding agents > How quality is checked
chunks.text:
- **The assumptions ledger.** Every agent report ends with each non-trivial claim tagged by how it
  was checked:

  | Tag | Means |
  |---|---|
  | `built` | Compiled |
  | `tested` | A unit or integration test ran |
  | `traced` | The code path was followed to its leaf calls |
  | `reasoned` | Inferred, not executed |
  | `on-device` | Validated on real hardware |

chunks.heading: How LEGION is built with AI coding agents > How quality is checked
chunks.text:
A report without a ledger is sent back.
- **The relay rule.** The orchestrator carries a subagent's tag unchanged when reporting to Kevin.
  "The agent reasoned X" never becomes "X is true." Briefs going down to an agent carry tags too:
  a verified signature is not a verified meaning (lesson L3: a signature was checked, the brief
  asserted milliseconds, the value was nanoseconds).
- **Grep-clean is not done (L10).** A reconciliation pass fixed everything a grep could find, then
  the real compile caught a query on a dropped column, a deleted file core state depended on, and
  files that were never copied. Nothing greps for an absence. Run the real build.
- **A ticket's verification steps are gates, not notes (L11).** A skipped preview step let a colour
  bug ship into a first-run screen. The executing agent had reported the step as unmet; the
  failure was treating that as a footnote. Now every verification step is accounted for as done,
  deferred with a named follow-up, or impossible and why, before a ticket is reported built.
- **Hooks turn rules into checks** (`.claude/settings.json`, scripts in `tools/hooks/`):
  - Before every `git commit`: regenerate the board, the public ticket wiki, the voice guide, the
    devlog and the ADR index and stage them, so the generated layer never lags the commit. It also
    runs the decision-debt check.
  - `guard_destructive.py` blocks commands that have destroyed data here or would: uninstalling the
    app (which wipes its keystore-held key), forced pushes to the public repo, `git reset --hard`
    in a tree other agents are using.
  - `guard_generated.py` blocks hand edits to generated files.
  - `warn_long_kotlin.py` warns when a staged Kotlin file passes 1000 lines; detekt runs in the
    build with a baseline, so only new debt turns it red.
- **Docs are checked, not trusted.** `tools/docs_check.py` fails on a source path named in `docs/`
  that no longer exists, on invalid ADR frontmatter, on a one-sided supersession link and on a
  broken wikilink. `tools/voice_guide.py` fails if a voice tool has no user-facing copy.
- **Prompt rules get an eval.** `tools/evals/` is a prompt-obedience harness that turns "does the
  model follow the speech rules" into a number. It runs on demand, not in CI, because every run
  spends real API calls.

chunks.heading: How LEGION is built with AI coding agents > How quality is checked
chunks.text: - **Test totals come from the test reports,** not from memory or an agent's summary.

chunks.heading: How LEGION is built with AI coding agents > How mistakes become rules (so agents do not make the same mistake twice)
chunks.text:
Agents are not fine-tuned. The only way an agent learns is that a lesson graduates into a prompt
surface it reads on its next run: its `.claude/agents/*.md` file, `CLAUDE.md`, or a playbook. The
ledger is `memory/library/lessons.md`, and its loop has five steps:

1. **Capture.** The assumptions ledger flags every `reasoned` claim as a candidate failure.
2. **Catch.** Review or the orchestrator finds a `reasoned` claim that turned out wrong.
3. **Distill.** One numbered entry: what was claimed, what was true, the root-cause class, and the
   rule that would have caught it. Classes include unverified reachability, false success and
   relay without verify.
4. **Write back.** The rule graduates into an agent file or `CLAUDE.md`, and the entry records
   where. An entry closes only when its rule lives in a surface something reads.
5. **Measure.** One cheap regression check per entry: a grep, a test, a hook or a review-rubric
   line, so the same class of mistake cannot silently return.

Examples where the rule became a check rather than a hope: L32 became the worktree rule in
`TEAM.md`; the forgotten decision became `tools/decision_debt.py`; L24 (the repo is ahead of its
docs) became `tools/docs_check.py`; destroyed data became `guard_destructive.py`.

chunks.heading: How LEGION is built with AI coding agents > Auditing real conversations
chunks.text:
The voice assistant is improved from recordings of real use, not from impressions. When Kevin asked
for a way to audit what was said, an agent built a conversation audit log: one line per event (what
the user said, what the assistant said, each tool call and result, interruptions), with third-party
mail content redacted and keys scrubbed. `tools/voice_audit.py` turns a capture into a readable
timeline and summary, and `tools/voice_latency.py` does the same for timings.

Each real run read through those tools produced follow-up tickets that were then built: for
example, the async-lookups map has tickets for the third run's follow-ups and for the fifth and
sixth runs' follow-ups, covering holding lines that went dead, a "still checking" nudge, sign-off
behaviour and spoken figures. The audit tool itself was fixed in the same loop.

chunks.heading: How LEGION is built with AI coding agents > Honest limits
chunks.text:
- **Agents' claims are re-verified, not trusted.** That is the point of the ledger and the relay
  rule: a `reasoned` claim stays labelled `reasoned` until something runs it.
- **The phone is the final check.** A ticket that compiles and passes its suite is `built`, not
  done, until it has run on real hardware. The README's status table separates what was verified on
  hardware from what is built and not yet run.
- **Rules came from failures.** Most of the rules above exist because the failure happened first,
  sometimes twice. The lessons file records those failures plainly, including the orchestrator's
  own.
- **Evals are not a gate.** The prompt-obedience harness costs real API calls and runs on demand.
- **Merges and pushes are ruled, not improvised.** Agents may merge `dev` into `main` and push it,
  by Kevin's ruling, and only when `dev` is green; forced pushes are blocked by a hook.

chunks.heading: How LEGION is built with AI coding agents > Same approach at work
chunks.text:
At his data-engineering internship, Kevin runs multi-agent development with Claude Code, plus a
weekly review that turns repeated agent mistakes into automated checks.

chunks.heading: LEGION server
chunks.text:
The engine (ADR 0044): one Django server over one Postgres, every other
piece a limb that talks to it over HTTPS JSON. See `../CLAUDE.md` and
`../docs/adr/0044-django-is-the-engine.md` for the architecture; this file
is local setup only.

chunks.heading: LEGION server > Local setup
chunks.text:
```
cd server
uv venv
uv pip install -r requirements.txt
cp ../deploy/.env.example ../deploy/.env   # fill in SECRET_KEY, DATABASE_URL, etc.
uv run manage.py migrate
```

**This block used to say `uv sync`, and that was wrong** (corrected 2026-09-08,
web-and-households ticket 04). `pyproject.toml` here has no `[project]` table -
it carries only ruff and pytest configuration - so uv has no dependency list to
read from it. `uv lock` refuses outright ("No `project` table found"), `uv.lock`
is a three-line stub that pins nothing, and `uv sync` therefore syncs the
environment to an EMPTY dependency set: run against a working venv it uninstalls
Django, DRF, psycopg and everything else, and on a fresh clone it leaves nothing
behind for `migrate` to run. `requirements.txt` is the real dependency list and
`uv pip install -r` is what reads it.

`legion/settings.py` refuses to start with a missing required variable,
naming it - there is no Kevin-hosted default (CLAUDE.md section 7).

chunks.heading: LEGION server > First-run: making the first user a household member
chunks.text:
`manage.py createsuperuser` makes a `User` row. That alone is **not**
enough to pass `household.permissions.IsHouseholdMember`, which every
authenticated endpoint requires - a fresh superuser account gets a bare 403
everywhere until it also has a `household.models.HouseholdMember` row.
Found the hard way, 2026-09-05: the first superuser made on the live
database could not pass a single authenticated endpoint.

**A superuser gets this automatically now** (`household/signals.py`): the
moment `is_superuser` is true on a saved `User` - at creation via
`createsuperuser`, or later via the admin - a matching `HouseholdMember`
row is created if one does not already exist. Nothing to run by hand for
the first admin account.

**The second adult is not necessarily a superuser**, and needs the explicit
command:

```
uv run manage.py add_household_member second-adult@example.com
```

Idempotent - safe to run again, or unconditionally from a first-run script.
It says in words whether it created the row or found one already there,
and refuses in words (never a bare traceback) if the email does not match
any existing `User`:

```
$ uv run manage.py add_household_member nobody@example.com
CommandError: No user with email 'nobody@example.com'. Create one first
with 'manage.py createsuperuser' or the admin.
```

chunks.heading: LEGION server > Handing the server a login (Canvas, WebAssign, Drive)
chunks.text:
Scheduled feeds read upstreams with a session a person handed over, never a
password (backend-etl ticket 02). Set `LEGION_VAULT_KEY` in `deploy/.env`
first (`deploy/.env.example` has the one-liner); without it the vault refuses
to store anything. Then, on your laptop, as an owner of the household:

```
pip install playwright google-auth-oauthlib requests
playwright install chromium
python tools/connect_session.py canvas --server https://<your server> --token <device token> --base-url https://<your canvas>
python tools/connect_session.py drive --server ... --token ... --client-id ... --client-secret ...
```

**Google OAuth caveat:** the household's own OAuth client must have its consent
screen set to **In production** (unverified is fine for your own accounts). A
client left in **Testing** issues refresh tokens that die after 7 days, and the
Drive feeds stop a week later. The script prints this too.

When an upstream refuses a saved login, `/api/freshness` says so and names the
command to run, e.g. "Canvas needs you to log in again: run
tools/connect_session.py canvas".

chunks.heading: LEGION server > Running the tests
chunks.text:
```
uv run pytest
```

Requires Postgres - `tests/conftest.py` refuses to run against anything
else (CLAUDE.md section 4/5). Point `DATABASE_URL` at a role with
`createdb` (pytest creates and drops its own test database per run); never
point it at a database you cannot afford pytest to create a throwaway
sibling of.

chunks.heading: LEGION server > Device logs: reading what the head unit did
chunks.text:
The head unit has no ADB, so it uploads its own rolling log after every drive
(`POST /api/device-logs/`, `devicelogs/`, stored gzipped in `public.device_logs`, 60 days kept,
pruned on upload). To read it:

```
python manage.py device_logs --last 3                      # newest 3 batches, in time order
python manage.py device_logs --last 10 --grep spotify      # only matching lines
python manage.py device_logs --last 1 --reason drive_end --household <uuid>
python manage.py device_logs --last 3 --reason conversation --render   # conversation timeline
```

Each batch prints under a header with the device, app version, reason (`drive_end`, `startup`,
`manual`, `periodic`, `conversation`) and the DEVICE's clock window (untrusted: the unit's clock has reset itself). Against the
deployed engine, run it as a Cloud Run Job execution (`deploy/cloudrun/README.md`):
`gcloud run jobs execute legion-worker --region us-south1 --wait --args=manage.py,device_logs,--last,3`
and read the execution's log output.

A `conversation` batch holds only a device's `LIVE_AUDIT` and `LIVE_LATENCY` lines (2026-10-28,
"all logs on engine. both headunit and phone"). `--render` prints it as the timeline
`tools/voice_audit.py` prints for a phone capture; `devicelogs/voice_audit.py` is a byte-for-byte
copy of that tool (see `devicelogs/render.py`), and a test fails while the two differ.

chunks.heading: LEGION server > Claude session: deploy note
chunks.text:
`claude_session/` (ADR 0067) keeps tasks, files and session rows 30 days; `manage.py
claude_session_prune` deletes older ones and is a line in `deploy/crontab`. **After deploying,
run `python deploy/cloudrun/install_schedule.py --job legion-worker`** so Cloud Scheduler picks up
that line; without it nothing is ever pruned.

chunks.heading: LEGION server > The OpenAPI contract: `server/openapi.yaml`
chunks.text:
**A client generates from this file. It does not hand-write what it thinks
the shapes are.**

That is the whole reason the file exists (django-engine ticket 04, "the
schema is the handoff"). With one client a hand-written HTTP layer is
survivable; with two - the Android phone app and the head-unit app - it is
how they drift, and not on rules, which live in Django now, but on shapes:
a field renamed on the server, a date parsed differently, a null handled
two ways. One schema, generated clients, and a rename breaks the build.

chunks.heading: LEGION server > The OpenAPI contract: `server/openapi.yaml` > Regenerating
chunks.text:
```
cd server
uv run manage.py write_openapi
```

That is the one command, and it is the one the staleness test names when it
fails. It wraps `manage.py spectacular` and adds three things:

- it resolves `server/openapi.yaml` from `BASE_DIR`, so it writes the same
  file whatever directory you run it from (plain `spectacular --file
  server/openapi.yaml` writes `server/server/openapi.yaml` from inside
  `server/`);
- `--fail-on-warn`, so a view drf-spectacular cannot describe is an error
  rather than a path silently missing from the contract;
- `--validate`, so an invalid document fails here instead of in whoever's
  code generator reads it next.

There is no flag to switch either off. If a new view cannot be described,
describe it - `@extend_schema` on a plain `APIView`, or nothing at all for
a table on `api/synced.SyncedModelViewSet`, which `api/schema.SyncedAutoSchema`
describes from the viewset's own serializer.

chunks.heading: LEGION server > The OpenAPI contract: `server/openapi.yaml` > The staleness test
chunks.text:
`tests/test_openapi_schema.py` regenerates into a temporary file and
compares it line for line with the committed one, failing with the command
above and the first line that differs. Because it regenerates through
`write_openapi`, it fails on an undescribable view too - a view added
without an `@extend_schema` is caught by the test suite, not by whoever
generates a client from the file a week later.

Three of its checks go further and compare the schema against a REAL
response from the test client (`/api/places/`, `/api/events`,
`/api/changes`, and the `voice_notes` 404). That is the class of lie
nothing else catches: before `api/schema.py` existed, every `?since=` list
route was documented as returning a bare array of rows when it returns
`{"results": [...], "next": ...}`. Nothing was broken, no warning fired,
and the document was valid OpenAPI the whole time.

`.gitattributes` pins the file to LF so a Windows checkout does not read as
permanently stale.

chunks.heading: LEGION server > The OpenAPI contract: `server/openapi.yaml` > Reading it
chunks.text:
`/api/schema/` serves the same document from a running server, and
`/api/schema/swagger/` renders it. Both are unauthenticated.

chunks.heading: LEGION server > The web client
chunks.text:
`server/frontend/` is a React + Vite + TypeScript app (web-and-households
ticket 04, superseding django-engine ticket 08's HTMX choice). It is a limb
like the phone is: it talks to the same API over the same contract, and Django
serves its build output and nothing more.

**Prerequisite: Node 24.** Nothing else - no global npm packages, no
`npx create` step. Every version is pinned exactly in `package.json`, the same
way `requirements.txt` pins Python, so `npm ci` reproduces one resolution.

```
cd server/frontend
npm ci
```

chunks.heading: LEGION server > The web client > The dev loop
chunks.text:
Two processes. Vite on 5173 serves the app and proxies `/api`, `/admin`,
`/static`, `/media` and `/health` to Django on 8000, so the browser sees one
origin and the session cookie behaves exactly as it will in production.

```
cd server && uv run manage.py runserver      # terminal one, port 8000
cd server/frontend && npm run dev            # terminal two, port 5173, open this one
```

chunks.heading: LEGION server > The web client > After changing the API
chunks.text:
`openapi.yaml` is the contract and `src/api/schema.d.ts` is generated from it.
Regenerate after every `write_openapi`:

```
npm run gen:api
```

`npm run check:api` regenerates and then `git diff --exit-code`s the result -
it fails if the committed types no longer match the committed contract. That is
the front-end half of the staleness test above, and CI (ticket 08) runs it.

Nothing hand-writes a URL or a body shape. If a path is missing from
`schema.d.ts` the fix is on the server and then `npm run gen:api`, never a cast.

chunks.heading: LEGION server > The web client > Building for Django to serve
chunks.text:
```
npm run build          # tsc -b, then vite build into ../static/app
```

Then, and only then, `collectstatic` has something to collect:

```
cd server && uv run manage.py collectstatic --noinput
```

Order matters: `collectstatic` copies what is on disk, so running it before
`npm run build` gathers a bundle that is missing or stale. `server/static/app/`
and `server/staticfiles/` are both gitignored - the Docker image builds them in
its own node stage (ticket 09).

**Before the bundle exists, `/` answers 503 in words**, not a stack trace:
"The web client has not been built; run `npm run build` in server/frontend".
`web/views.py` is the whole of it.

chunks.heading: LEGION server > The web client > Tests
chunks.text:
```
npm test               # Vitest + Testing Library
```

chunks.heading: LEGION server > Checking for drift
chunks.text:
```
uv run ruff check .
uv run manage.py check
uv run manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run
uv run manage.py write_openapi
```
